title: Bitwise Projects $1.6 Million Bitcoin by 2036. Does Gold Hold the Key?
summary: Bitwise’s $1.6 million Bitcoin target draws about 82% of its value from a gold and Bitcoin market it sees hitting $109.8 trillion by 2036.
content:
Bitwise projects Bitcoin (BTC) will hit $1.6 million by 2036, about 19 times its $83,557 starting price. Most of that value depends on Bitcoin winning a quarter of the store-of-value market it shares with gold.

The store-of-value slot supplies about $27.5 trillion of the model's $33.6 trillion total, roughly 82% of Bitcoin's projected 2036 value. That leaves the target exposed to one assumption more than any other in the model.

Bitwise builds the target with a total addressable market model. It sizes each market Bitcoin could serve, applies a penetration rate, and divides by the full 21 million supply.

The firm expects the combined gold and Bitcoin market to grow from $31.1 trillion to $109.8 trillion by 2036. Its base case hands Bitcoin 25% of that pool.

At the starting price, Bitcoin's 20.1 million circulating coins are worth about $1.7 trillion, roughly 5% of today's $31.1 trillion market.

The six other markets in the model, including institutional portfolios and national treasury reserves, add only about $6 trillion combined.

Bitwise also highlights Bitcoin's tightening link with gold. Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold reached a record 0.58 on September 11.

"We would expect this relationship to persist and deepen over time as awareness of bitcoin's store-of-value properties continues to grow," the report read.

The model itself assumes a 0.21 correlation with gold over the next decade, up from a 10-year average of 0.11.

The bear case cuts the store-of-value share to 2.5% and gives every other market zero. That yields a 2036 price of $130,686, a 4.6% annual return.

Bitcoin trades at 79,902, down 1.12% over the past day.

Even Bitwise's base case sits far above JPMorgan's 2036 Bitcoin scenarios, which put base-case returns at 10% a year. Bitwise's base case implies 34.3%. Jim Cramer, for one, said this month he still prefers gold for portfolio insurance over Bitcoin.

Bitwise lists quantum computing, AI-driven mathematical advances, and regulatory reversal as key risks. Still, the widest swing in its model depends on how much of gold's role shifts to Bitcoin by 2036.

title: Treasury Buyback Fills $6 Billion Again: So Why Is Bitcoin Below $80K?
summary: Treasury filled its $6 billion buyback again, but Bitcoin did not rally. Here is what changed since August's jump.
content:
A US Treasury buyback filled its full $6 billion cap in 20- to 30-year bonds on Tuesday. Bitcoin (BTC) did not rally the way it did in August., in fact, it fell below the $80,000 mark.

Bitcoin traders who treated buybacks as a yield catalyst saw no such trigger. August's rally followed a policy surprise, while Tuesday's operation had sat on Treasury's tentative schedule for weeks.

On August 19, Treasury said it would double its long-dated buybacks to at least $4 billion per operation. The announcement caught investors by surprise.

Bitcoin gained about 7% that day, while the 30-year yield pulled back from its highest level in 19 years.

Tuesday brought no such surprise. Newsquawk calls these liquidity support operations routine, since their purpose is helping dealers offload older, thinly traded bonds. They are sized to avoid shifting yields, it added.

Dealers offered $10.7 billion, and Treasury accepted exactly $6 billion across six bonds. It was the fourth full-size fill, FXStreet reported.

Treasury paid between 52 and 71 cents on the dollar, for a cash outlay of about $3.8 billion.

The price response to later buyback operations has faded. Bitcoin has since slipped below $80,000 again, CoinGecko data showed on Thursday, down 1.5% over 24 hours. While the timing seems linked it would be difficult to directly correlate the buyback and the price dip.

Yields have resisted since. The 10-year touched 5.342%, its highest since April 2002, as Treasury filled its cap on October 1, Yahoo reported.

The Federal Reserve's two-day meeting also overlapped with Tuesday's operation. The central bank held rates steady on Wednesday, NPR reported.

The expanded schedule runs through November 4, Chase noted. Filled caps have not clearly pulled long-term yields lower. The program may read as routine plumbing rather than a signal for risk assets. A larger size could change that.

title: Bitcoin Controls 59.5% of the Crypto Market. Is Altcoin Season Still Possible?

content:
Bitcoin's 59.5% crypto market dominance reflects altcoins falling far faster, with Ethereum down 12.5% and Solana down 14.5% last month.

Galaxy Digital's Alex Thorn says the bear market ended in June and Bitcoin's 24.5% rise over 90 days signals a new cycle.

Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) accounts for a significant 59.5% of the crypto market. This percentage, known as Bitcoin dominance, shows how much of the $2.72 trillion crypto market Bitcoin controls. Traders and altcoin investors monitor this figure closely to gauge when it might be their turn to shine.

While Bitcoin has also dipped, currently priced at $80,566—down 3.0% over the past 30 days—its dominant share is driven by even steeper declines in altcoins. In the same timeframe, Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) fell 12.5%, Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) dropped 14.5%, and XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) fell 11.9%.

A senior researcher at Galaxy Digital ( NASDAQ: GLXY ) said the bear market is now behind us. This raises the question: Have altcoin sell-offs reached their limit, setting the stage for a potential recovery, or is Bitcoin still the preferred asset?

Bitcoin dominance is calculated by dividing Bitcoin's market cap by the total market cap of all cryptocurrencies. Market cap is calculated by multiplying a coin's price by its circulating supply. Currently, Bitcoin's market cap is at $1.62 trillion, while Ethereum accounts for 10.5% of this total.

Traders often use Bitcoin dominance as a sentiment indicator. When dominance rises, it typically signals that money is flowing into Bitcoin, viewed as a safer option (risk-off trend). Conversely, when dominance drops, it indicates a shift toward smaller, riskier altcoins. Traders call a prolonged decline in Bitcoin dominance "altcoin season," a period when many altcoins outperform Bitcoin.

According to Alex Thorn, head of research at Galaxy, a note from October 27 suggests the bear market ended in June, meaning Bitcoin is now in an accumulation phase that usually precedes a price rise. He claims the lowest point came in June, when Bitcoin was priced below $58,000.

Over the last 90 days, Bitcoin has risen by 24.5%, aligning with Thorn's predictions. Historically, in both the 2017 and 2021 cycles, Bitcoin led gains, and altcoins only began to outperform it after significant price moves. Increased liquidity and new retail investors entering the market fueled these rotations. If Thorn's perspective is correct, Bitcoin's current high dominance could signify the early stages of a new market cycle.

Bitcoin dominance can increase for two main reasons: either Bitcoin is gaining value faster than other cryptocurrencies, indicating new demand, or altcoins are losing value quicker than Bitcoin, suggesting that holders are selling off. In this current scenario, it's clearly the latter—Bitcoin has lost 3.0% over the last month, while Cardano (CRYPTO: ADA) has tumbled by 17.5%. Over the past year, Bitcoin has fallen 28.5%, Ethereum 41.1%, and XRP 49.1%.

The total used to measure dominance has its own peculiarities. It includes stablecoins—tokens tied to the value of the dollar—so Bitcoin's percentage can drop even if no one is buying altcoins, because traders often move funds into stablecoins for safekeeping.

While some altcoins are performing relatively well, they aren't enough to signal the start of an altcoin season. For example, Monero (CRYPTO: XMR) has risen 13.4% over the past month and a striking 77.4% over the last year, largely due to demand for privacy coins. Meanwhile, Pepe (CRYPTO: PEPE) rose 16.1% over 30 days, but with a $2.04 billion market cap, it's too small to significantly affect Bitcoin's dominance.

Market sentiment isn't particularly strong either. The Fear & Greed Index, which measures market emotions on a scale from 0 to 100 (where low numbers indicate fear), currently sits at 48—a neutral stance. Typically, counter-trend buying works best after most sellers have exited, and at 48, sentiment hasn't fully pivoted yet.

For an altcoin season to take hold, several conditions must align. Bitcoin dominance would need to decrease, the ETH/BTC ratio would need to rise, ETF investments would need to flow into altcoin funds, and investors would need a greater appetite for risk. Currently, the trend appears to be in the opposite direction.

On October 27, spot Bitcoin ETFs saw inflows of $176 million, following $110 million on October 26 and a $635 million outflow on October 22, with cumulative net inflows at $57.47 billion. In contrast, altcoin funds are struggling. U.S. spot Solana ETFs lost $19 million on October 27 and $8 million on October 26, with net assets dropping from $1.94 billion on September 29 to $1.54 billion.

XRP ETFs reported no net flows on October 27 after a $3.6 million outflow on October 26, indicating weak demand for altcoin funds.

The ETH/BTC ratio, which measures Ethereum's price against Bitcoin, remains a crucial indicator of potential altcoin rotations since Ethereum is the leading altcoin. Ethereum has dropped 12.5% over the last 30 days, while Bitcoin has fallen only 3.0%.

Ethereum trades at $2,334, which is 4.2% below its 20-day moving average of $2,435 and 8.1% below its 50-day average of $2,540. Although sellers currently dictate the trend, Ethereum remains 8.1% above its 200-day moving average of $2,158.

While an altcoin season remains possible, current data shows no signs of it unfolding yet. The prevailing 59.5% Bitcoin dominance largely reflects altcoin weakness rather than strong demand for Bitcoin. Keeping a close watch on market trends will be essential to determine if a rotation toward altcoins is truly on the horizon.

title: What Is Going On With MARA Stock After Its Steep Fall?
summary: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
content:
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Holders are wondering if the business is coming apart after MARA (MARA) stock lost 41.5% from September 28 to October 27, 2026. The S&P 500 gained 0.6% over the same period. Over that stretch, crypto-linked stocks slid as bitcoin fell toward $80,000, and news reports said MARA sold about $81 million of its bitcoin. Part of the answer is already known. MARA mined about 64 more bitcoin in its June 2026 quarter than a year earlier, and it is borrowing against its bitcoin to build a power business. So why is MARA taking in less money while it mines more bitcoin?

MARA's Revenue Fell With Bitcoin's Price

A 28% drop in the average price of bitcoin from a year earlier outweighed MARA's higher output. Revenue for the June 2026 quarter was $175 million, down 26.7% from a year earlier. On its August 6, 2026 earnings call, MARA said that mining more bitcoin added $7.2 million to revenue, while the lower price took away $65.9 million and other revenue fell about $4.9 million.

Profit swings even more. MARA reported a net loss of $610 million for the June 2026 quarter, compared with net income of $808 million a year earlier. About $343 million of the latest loss came from a lower marked value of the digital assets the company holds, a loss on paper rather than in cash, MARA said.

The company also runs at an operating loss. Over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, MARA's operating margin was negative 126.1% , against a positive 18.5% for the S&P 500.

What Is MARA Buying With Bitcoin-Backed Debt?

A power business. During the same call, MARA said it is paying for the $1.5 billion Long Ridge acquisition with bitcoin-backed debt and by taking on Long Ridge's balance sheet. At the time, the deal still needed FERC approval.

That plan may be what buyers are paying for. MARA trades at 3.4 times its sales, close to the 3.2 for the S&P 500, though those sales shrank in the latest quarter. Management expects its power portfolio to reach about 4.8 gigawatts once its pending deals are approved and closed. More than 70% of Long Ridge's power output is sold under long-term contracts, so that income would not move with bitcoin's price. Management also said it was confident of signing at least two leases before the end of 2026 at sites it is developing with Starwood.

The cost is debt. MARA's total debt equals 91.2% of its market value, against 19.4% for the S&P 500. MARA expects to take on about $900 million of Long Ridge's debt when that deal closes. Its latest borrowings are backed by its bitcoin, and with 54% of its holdings pledged as collateral, a fall in bitcoin's price hits both its revenue and the collateral behind its loans.

How Far Has MARA Stock Fallen In Past Shocks?

The stock has fallen further than the S&P 500 in each of the five market shocks since 2022, and much further in most of them. In the 2022 inflation shock, MARA fell 84% while the S&P 500 fell 24%. During the five percent yield shock of summer and fall 2023, MARA fell 55%, against 9.5% for the index. The smallest gap came in the 2023 regional banking crisis, when MARA fell 8.9% and the S&P 500 fell 6.7%.

When Will MARA Holders Learn More?

Holders will learn more in November 2026, when MARA is expected to report its September quarter. For the risk to be worth taking, MARA's power business would need to start bringing in revenue that does not rise and fall with bitcoin's price. The two things to look for in that report are revenue against a year earlier, and whether the Long Ridge acquisition has closed.

title: Could Bitcoin Price Crash Like Silver? Warning Signs Are Showing
summary: Benjamin Cowen warns Bitcoin could follow silver's path after a fake-out, while Charles Edwards sees capped downside.
content:
For the second straight week, Bitcoin's price closed below $83,000, a key support level to confirm a bullish trend. This confirms a fake-out, according to popular analyst Benjamin Cowen. The analyst now fears Bitcoin could trace silver's slow post-2011 collapse, when the precious metal's price crashed 73% in 4 years.

Cowen, a member of BeInCrypto's Market Intelligence Expert Council, set a simple test in his latest video. One weekly close below $83,000 would favor bears, and a second would confirm it.

Bitcoin closed at $82,042 the prior week and at $80,154 on October 25. It still trades around the same level this week, failing to hold the $83,000 support.

His next target is the bull market support band (BMSB), a pair of 20-week and 21-week moving averages near $72,000 to $76,000. If Bitcoin price drops to this level, it could be a warning sign for further decline.

The S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Ethereum (ETH) already lost their 50-day averages and slid to that band.

Silver offers Cowen the closest precedent. After its 2011 peak near $49, the metal held its lows twice, and its rallies resembled a recovery.

One rally even closed above the 50-week moving average in late 2012. Silver still broke down in 2013 and slid to about $14 by 2015.

"What keeps me up at night is more so what if it follows like the silver path… I hope it doesn't and I'm constantly looking for reasons for why it won't."

For Bitcoin, that means a February low, a July low, and perhaps a fourth-quarter low. Rallies would fade until a breakdown arrives in 2027 or 2028.

A drop to $60,000 and a rebound would worry him most, turning September's breakout buyers into resistance. A new low below the realized price, the average cost basis of all coins, would instead force real capitulation.

Silver is living through a similar unwind today. The metal closed Friday at $53.83, nearly 56% below its January record, at its lowest level of 2026.

Cowen expanded his earlier bearish Q4 roadmap into an 11-step sequence.

Bitcoin posts a second weekly close below $83,000

The fake-out is confirmed

BTC drops to the BMSB

The Federal Reserve holds rates on Oct. 28

Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation comes in hot on Oct. 29

The 10-year Treasury yield climbs again

Bitcoin and stocks fall

Oil reaches $120

The Fed raises rates in December

The US Dollar Index (DXY) rises into the Fed's December meeting

Long-term yields drop into year-end

If one step fails, he says, the rest becomes doubtful. A weekly close above roughly $84,000 would undercut the thesis.

Charles Edwards, founder of Capriole Investments and a fellow council member, sees a different short-term picture. Bitcoin's put/call ratio, comparing bearish options bets with bullish ones, has hit 1.46.

His chart shows similar spikes near the February and June lows of 2026. In 2022, however, a May spike near $29,000 preceded a slide to about $17,600.

The two views may not conflict. A local floor still allows a test of the support band. Cowen's deeper fear is a silver-style grind lasting years, which no options signal can rule out.

title: 3 Reasons Why Bitcoin Is Worth Buying Right Now
summary: Are you waiting for the perfect chart pattern before you finally buy Bitcoin? Find out why the real buy signal is coming from the blockchain's newest infrastructure upgrades.
content:
2026 has felt like an extended crypto winter . Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) got stuck in a frustratingly long consolidation phase. If you check CoinMarketCap's popular Fear & Greed index, it's sitting at a perfectly neutral 45, while the Altcoin season index is hovering at an equally lukewarm 55. Bitcoin itself is down 30% over the past 52 weeks and 4% over the past month, as of Oct. 28.

Despite the market's sideways shuffle, Bitcoin dominance remains a formidable 60.1%. I can see a steady institutional presence in spot-price Bitcoin funds like the massive iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (NASDAQ: IBIT) and the newer Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust ETF (NYSEMKT: MSBT), both of which bring trusted brand names to the crypto market.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But staring at technical charts won't tell you exactly when this freeze will finally thaw. As with any other open-market investment, market timing is usually a bad idea for Bitcoin buyers. Having an active interest in the market is more important than starting at exactly the right price-chart squiggle, as long as you expect the target asset to rise in the long run.

That said, I see three distinct reasons to grab some Bitcoin (or your favorite Bitcoin ETF ) at the end of October 2026. The developer community has a few important projects going on.

Here are three structural reasons to consider buying Bitcoin now:

A more robust transaction engine: The brand-new Bitcoin Core 32.1 release brought a serious upgrade to how the blockchain network handles traffic. Instead of individual nodes getting bogged down during high-volume spikes, the system now uses a global transaction relay backlog and pre-fetches data in parallel. The network essentially got a massive upgrade to its traffic control system. In other words, instead of every individual computer on the network (called a "node") getting overwhelmed by its own massive line of traffic during a rush, the whole system now shares one highly organized, central queue.

Proactive security posture: The developer community has aggressively targeted emerging threats. Core maintainers recently overhauled security policies to rapidly patch vulnerabilities easily discovered by AI models. Furthermore, active development of BIP-361 (a formal Bitcoin Improvement Proposal) demonstrates serious, forward-looking preparation for post-quantum cryptographic migration -- essentially, upgrading the lock on the Bitcoin vault before quantum computers become powerful enough to threaten it.

Hardened decentralized infrastructure: The latest updates have made the network much more resilient against targeted attacks. Bitcoin's developers are adding anti-spam defenses to Tor hidden services. For the uninitiated, Tor stands for "The Onion Router," which is a privacy network that wraps data in layers of encryption (yum, onions). The developers are also phasing out older, less secure privacy protocols.

While the market sentiment might look a bit sleepy right now, the protocol itself is rapidly evolving. Buying now means investing in a deeply fortified, highly optimized network that's already dressed and ready for the next spring.

title: Datavault AI Stock Jumps 31% Even as Its Bitcoin Sits Stuck at Biconomy
summary: Its restatement takes every reported bitcoin off the books, including 837 BTC Scilex agreed to buy in June. No definitive deal has been disclosed.
content:
Shares of Nasdaq-listed Datavault AI rebounded about 31% on Wednesday with no new filing from the company. Two days earlier, the company said in an 8-K it cannot withdraw its bitcoin from Biconomy and will restate four sets of financial statements, removing every bitcoin it had reported, including the 837 BTC that Scilex Holding signed a binding term sheet in June to buy for $50 million .

DVLT closed at $0.13 on Monday, near $0.067 on Tuesday and about $0.088 on Wednesday, on roughly 383 million shares, according to Yahoo Finance data . Neither Datavault nor Scilex has filed with the SEC since.

That filing, made just after Monday's market close, says the Philadelphia company asked in June to move bitcoin from its wallet at Biconomy PTE. Ltd. to an external account and has "been unable to complete the withdrawal." It does not say why. On Oct. 20, its audit committee concluded that investors should no longer rely on its financial statements for the third quarter of 2025, full-year 2025 and the first two quarters of 2026.

Get Unchained's crypto news in your inbox with the free Unchained Daily newsletter .

The coins date to a September 2025 deal in which Scilex agreed to buy Datavault stock and a pre-funded warrant for $150 million , payable in bitcoin. Scilex credited 1,309.04 BTC to Datavault's Biconomy wallet in September and November 2025, and Datavault later sold 491.431 BTC back to it for about $40.5 million, the 8-K says.

Datavault now says that bitcoin "did not meet the requirements for recognition as a digital asset of the Company." It will record the purchase instead as a receivable from Scilex, shown as a reduction of stockholders' equity. The change is expected to cut total assets by $92.2 million at Dec. 31, 2025, and by $49.0 million at June 30, 2026.

Those match the crypto-asset values in Datavault's own quarterly report filed Aug. 19, which counted 1,054 BTC at the end of 2025 and 837 BTC at the end of June. Management is reassessing its going concern evaluation because "the collection of amounts owed by Scilex is uncertain," the 8-K says. The company has not set a date for the restated filings.

On June 24, Scilex signed a binding term sheet to buy those 837 BTC, described as held in Datavault's Biconomy wallet, for $30 million up front plus $20 million in quarterly payments running through 2028. Scilex's 10-Q , filed Aug. 14, and Datavault's 10-Q five days later both said no definitive agreement had been entered into. No later filing from either company reports a signing, a closing or a termination, and the Oct. 26 8-K does not mention the term sheet.

Scilex's own bitcoin also came from Biconomy: its 10-Q says it sold Semnur Pharmaceuticals shares to Biconomy in September 2025 for $200 million in bitcoin and used $150 million of it to buy the Datavault stake.

The 8-K lists among its risks the outcome of efforts "to collect amounts from Scilex or obtain the cooperation of Biconomy." Biconomy has made no public statement, and CoinDesk reported that the company had not answered its questions.

title: Grant Cardone challenges Bitcoin bear to $1 million bet
summary: Grant Cardone answers Jason Calacanis’s bearish Bitcoin prediction with a seven-figure challenge and a two-year deadline.
content:
Bitcoin's slide from its record high has split some of its loudest backers and critics into two camps. One side says the rally is over.

The other is now offering to put serious money behind the opposite view.

Real estate investor Grant Cardone has challenged Jason Calacanis, an early Uber investor and co-host of the All-In podcast, to a $1 million wager on whether Bitcoin can return to its peak.

Bitcoin hit an all-time high of $126,080 on Oct. 6, 2025. At the time of writing, it was trading near $80,847, about 36% below that mark.

Related: Top analyst calls Nasdaq AI firm's SEC filing 'one of the ugliest' ever

On Oct. 27, Calacanis told his followers on X that "a brutal year for Bitcoin is just getting started" and urged them to "dump it now."

He pointed to money flowing out of Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, or ETFs, which let investors buy Bitcoin exposure through a regular brokerage account.

He predicted Bitcoin would " test the 57k low again in the next 12 months."

Calacanis called Bitcoin "a dead network that offers nothing beyond a store of value."

A store of value is an asset people hold to preserve wealth over time, a role gold has long played.

He urged investors to "shift from Bitcoin to Super Intelligence," arguing AI offers "unlimited upside for humanity."

He ended the post with the line Cardone later picked up: "Bitcoin will never break its all-time high again."

"Jason, I'll bet you $1,000,000 it will break its ATH," Cardone wrote on X. ATH is short for all-time high.

His terms set a target of $126,210.50, slightly above the record. The deadline is noon Pacific time on Oct. 28, 2028.

The wager would settle either when Bitcoin reaches that price or when the deadline passes.

Coinbase CEO says gold's supply can change, Bitcoin's can't

Cardone said he was "happy to trust" Calacanis to pay. He also offered to have both men deposit the money with an independent party, an arrangement known as escrow.

"Do we have a bet?" he asked.

Cardone isn't the only one taking the other side.

Investor Fred Krueger has also offered Calacanis a $1 million bet that Bitcoin will top its October 2025 peak before Oct. 28, 2036. Hollywood producer turned Bitcoin educator Terence Michael added another $1 million offer.

So far, Calacanis hasn't accepted any of them.

Some institutional investors lean toward Cardone's side, though over a much longer stretch.

Bitwise, an asset manager that runs crypto investment funds, published its long-term Bitcoin outlook in October.

Its base case puts Bitcoin at about $1.6 million by 2036, which works out to an average annual return of 34.3%.

Its bull case reaches $3.67 million. Even its bear case, at $130,686, sits above today's record.

Bitwise expects Bitcoin to be "the best-performing major asset in the world over the next decade."

For comparison, it projects annual returns of 6.7% for U.S. stocks and 5.5% for gold over the same period.

The firm also flags risks.

It calls the figures illustrative rather than predictions and names "technological disruption" among the biggest long-term threats to its forecast.

Cardone's own optimism goes back further.

In September, he told followers that Bitcoin would become an everyday means of payment once its total market value reaches $20 trillion.

For now, the two investors are two years and roughly $45,360 per coin apart.

title: Fed Holds Rates, but Warsh Is Shrinking Its Rate-Setting Calendar
summary: Warsh held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% and said the Fed rate-setting calendar will drop from eight meetings to seven in 2027.
content:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh held interest rates at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday. He also said the Fed will shrink its rate-setting calendar, starting in 2027 with one meeting that skips rate votes.

Only seven of the Fed's eight 2027 meetings will set rates, and Warsh expects six of eight in 2028. Bitcoin (BTC) and other rate-sensitive assets could face fewer scheduled catalysts.

Warsh said the strategy-only meeting would give Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) members room to debate long-term questions.

Those strategy meetings would carry no policy statement and no vote on the Fed's benchmark federal funds rate.

He argued the calendar itself matters.

"I believe the setting of the meeting schedule and agenda is more than some administrative detail."

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6az4zH0_jLM

Historically, the Fed has used eight yearly meetings since 1981, with four as the minimum.

However, the hold was not unanimous. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and one other official dissented for a hike, making the vote 10-2.

Warsh said first-half growth estimates rose to 2.4% from 1.8%, and inflation has topped target for nearly six years.

He said new data over the coming weeks will sharpen the December call on raising rates. Morgan Stanley had warned beforehand that the hold won't end hikes.

With a December hike under debate, fewer decision days may make each vote a bigger event for traders. That read weakens if strategy meetings still move expectations, though Warsh said he does not expect policy decisions from them.

Meanwhile, Warsh told reporters politics played no role in the decision, Reuters reported. Elections that decide congressional control arrive Nov. 3.

President Donald Trump has tried to remove Cook for over a year. The White House has scheduled a possible proceeding against her for Nov. 5.

A thinner calendar could therefore squeeze the hike debate into fewer votes. In contrast, the White House keeps pressing against hikes, and the Fed's independence is on the line.

Bitcoin fell five straight days to $80,566, representing a 4.7% weekly decline, even as nearly 15,000 BTC worth $1.2 billion left exchanges during the slide.

Jesse Marre called Bitcoin's five-day losing streak "pretty rare," noting it was the first such downturn in 90 days, with prior four-day runs each rebounding within two weeks.

During this period, traders withdrew 14,942 BTC—worth about $1.2 billion—from crypto exchanges ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision. Typically, higher Bitcoin exchange outflows are viewed positively, suggesting that holders are removing supply from the market, which is usually bullish. However, in this case, the price kept falling.

Bitcoin trades at $80,566, down 4.7% over the past week and 3.6% in October. Jesse Marre from Hilbert Group described this streak of daily losses as "pretty rare" in his weekly update. So, does the combination of falling prices and decreasing exchange balances set the stage for a rebound, or is there a valid reason behind this selling pressure?

An exchange outflow occurs when Bitcoin moves from exchange-associated wallets to untagged wallets. Traders usually see this as a positive sign because coins held on exchanges can be sold instantly, while those in private wallets take more effort to liquidate. Significant outflows often indicate that long-term holders are withdrawing assets from the market.

The streak of negative days has intensified selling pressure. After peaking at $84,856 on October 21, Bitcoin posted five consecutive red days, briefly dipping below $80,000 and hitting a low of $79,107 on October 24.

This marks the first five-day downturn in the last 90 days. Prior runs lasted only four days, seen in August, September, and early October, each followed by a rebound within two weeks. For example, Bitcoin closed at $76,537 on September 10 before rising to $86,595 by September 21.

However, those recoveries occurred as Bitcoin bounced back from a lower price of $58,566 on June 30. The cryptocurrency is still up 24.5% over the past three months, but upward momentum has stalled over the past month.

An outflow merely tracks Bitcoin moving from an exchange-associated address to one not labeled as such. This doesn't clarify who moved the coins or their reasoning. For instance, a corporate treasury transfer looks the same on-chain as an individual investor moving coins for long-term holding.

Notably, Whale Alert detected a transfer of 640 BTC worth $52 million from Coinbase Institutional—the large client division of Coinbase Global ( NASDAQ: COIN )—to an unidentified wallet. This movement could indicate a fund shifting assets to cold storage, a trading desk involved in a private deal, or a new buyer—all of which would appear the same on-chain.

Moreover, Lookonchain reported that MARA Holdings ( NASDAQ: MARA ), a Bitcoin mining company, transferred another 1,000 BTC valued at $81 million to BitGo Holdings ( NYSE: BTGO ), a digital asset custody firm. A miner might send coins to a custodian for various purposes, such as storage, loan collateral, or sale, but each action shows up similarly on the blockchain.

Additionally, a significant visibility gap remains. Most buying activity occurs within an exchange's internal order book. When trades occur, they update the exchange's ledger without affecting the blockchain, so a quiet blockchain could signal either accumulation or a lack of investor interest.

Marre interpreted this week's price movements as driven mainly by spot trading, suggesting the selling came from active traders, which affects price more than simple wallet transfers.

October is shaping up to be one of Bitcoin's worst months in six years, continuing a "Downtober" trend driven by weakened U.S. demand for spot Bitcoin. Spot Bitcoin ETFs directly reflect demand: net inflows create new shares, forcing the fund to acquire actual Bitcoin to back them.

Bitcoin is currently trading below its 20-day average of $81,875 and its 50-day average of $81,840, both about 1.6% higher, but still well above its 200-day average of $73,029, which is about 9.4% lower.

At this point, a bounce doesn't appear imminent. The previous four-day downturns rebounded during a dominant uptrend, but unlike those situations, the current uptrend seems to have lost momentum.

title: Bitcoin Shrugs Off a Hawkish Fed as Volatility Bets Barely Budge
summary: Deribit’s bitcoin implied volatility index ended the afternoon where it started and bitcoin gained 0.33% on Coinbase, even as December hike odds rose after Kevin Warsh’s Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4%.
content:
Bitcoin's options market priced in almost no added risk after the Federal Reserve kept rates unchanged on Wednesday, even though two policymakers wanted a hike and traders lifted their bets on one in December.

Deribit's DVOL index , which tracks 30-day implied volatility on the exchange's bitcoin options, stood at 37.59 at 2 p.m. ET, when the statement was released. It dipped to 37.41 within the hour and read 37.58 at 4:45 p.m. ET, staying between 37.22 and 37.63, Deribit's public data shows.

Spot prices barely moved either. Bitcoin changed hands at $80,763 on Coinbase just before 2 p.m. ET and at $81,027 at 4:45 p.m. ET, a gain of 0.33% . In the first hour after the release it traded between $80,600 and $81,234. Ether rose 0.35% on Coinbase over the same window, to $2,351 from $2,342.

Funding on Deribit's bitcoin perpetual future, the fee long holders pay short holders, eased to an eight-hour rate of 0.0058% at 4 p.m. ET from 0.0074% at 2 p.m. ET, Deribit data shows.

The Federal Open Market Committee left the federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote. Two of the 12 voters, Governor Lisa Cook and the Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack, pushed for another 25-basis-point move. The hold came one meeting after the Fed's first hike since 2023, in September, which crypto markets absorbed with little damage .

The statement said inflation "remains elevated" and that the Committee "will deliver price stability." Annual CPI inflation reached 3.7% in September, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Oct. 14 release , and bitcoin slid to about $80,500 that night.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said in his press conference opening statement that conditions had begun to change since the September move and that "market participants are becoming somewhat more discerning in their capital allocations." He added: "While overall financial conditions are tighter, I'm unwilling and unable to call them tight." His prepared remarks did not mention crypto.

The odds of a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting rose to 82.6% from 78.3% a day earlier, according to CME FedWatch figures cited by Fox Business in an update at 3:55 p.m. ET.

The response differs from June, when bitcoin slid after a hawkish hold at Warsh's first meeting as chair. With DVOL near 37.6, bitcoin options were pricing a one-standard-deviation daily move of about 2%, dividing the index by the square root of 365.

title: Bitcoin’s ‘Uptober’ rally just fell apart as demand weakens
summary: Bitcoin is heading for its weakest October in years as US buyers step back, data shows.
content:
October was once Bitcoin's most dependable month. This year, it is shaping up to be one of its worst.

Bitcoin is down 4.2% so far this month, according to a new report from on-chain analytics firm CryptoQuant. It closed September at $83,567 and fell to $80,051 by Oct. 25.

That puts Bitcoin on track for a second straight losing October, and the weakest in CryptoQuant's data going back to 2020.

Every October from 2020 to 2024 ended higher, with gains averaging 18.1%, before October 2025 broke the streak with a 3.8% loss.

Weak demand is the main culprit.

CryptoQuant's 30-day measure of apparent demand fell to minus 76,000 BTC on Oct. 25, and has been negative every day since Oct. 14. In other words, new buyers are taking in less Bitcoin than miners are creating.

Related: Elon Musk has a bold answer to America's $40 trillion debt crisis

American investors have been especially quiet. The Coinbase Premium, which tracks demand from US buyers, dropped to minus 0.146 on Oct. 24, its lowest since June 30. It has been negative on every day of October.

Recent buyers have also lost most of their profit cushion . Traders who bought in the past one to three months are now up just 8.1%, down from 33.4% on Sept. 22.

"The cushion that absorbed September's dips is mostly gone," CryptoQuant said.

Still, the firm's Bull Score Index stands at 60, a reading it calls "bullish, cooling," not bearish.

It pointed to the Fed's Oct. 28 rate decision and the Nov. 3 midterms as the next tests, with support between $73,000 and $77,600.

Not everyone is worried.

Michael Sullivan, author of Bitcoin Sentiment Weekly, believes Bitcoin is significantly undervalued around $80,000.

In a recent podcast , he described Bitcoin's climb from its $58,000 low earlier this year as a "disbelief rally" that has been steadily climbing a "wall of worry," with prices rising despite widespread doubt.

Sullivan pointed out that investor excitement is near levels last seen in 2015, and weaker than during the 2022 bear market.

He said such conditions have historically created strong long-term buying opportunities.

title: Bitcoin Treasury Datavault AI Says It Can’t Access Its BTC, Stock Tanks
summary: Datavault AI says it has been unable to withdraw its Bitcoin from Biconomy since June and will restate four financial reports tied to a $150 million Scilex deal.
content:
Datavault AI shares fell more than 50% on Tuesday to close at $0.06, after the Nasdaq-listed company disclosed that it has been unable to withdraw Bitcoin from the crypto exchange Biconomy since June. The company also said four sets of its financial statements can no longer be relied upon.

The disclosure came in a Form 8-K filed Oct. 26, in which Datavault said it requested a withdrawal to an external account in June and has been "unable to complete the withdrawal." The filing does not explain what is holding it up.

The Bitcoin traces to a Sept. 25, 2025, agreement in which Scilex Holding, a pain-medicine company, agreed to pay $150 million in Bitcoin for 15 million Datavault shares and a pre-funded warrant covering another 263.9 million shares. A pre-funded warrant is a right to buy stock in which nearly the whole price is paid upfront.

At $112,915.52 per Bitcoin, the deal came to about 1,328.43 BTC. Scilex credited 1,309.04 BTC to Datavault's account at Biconomy on Sept. 26 and Nov. 25, 2025, the filing says, a figure that reflects a 19.39 BTC deduction for cash advances Scilex had made.

Those credits were off-chain transfers, meaning the exchange changed balances on its own books rather than moving coins across the Bitcoin blockchain. Between Sept. 26, 2025, and Jan. 30, 2026, Datavault sold 491.431 BTC back to Scilex the same way, for about $40.5 million in cash.

After reviewing the transaction, Datavault concluded the Bitcoin never qualified as a digital asset of the company. It will instead book the deal as a subscription receivable, money a buyer owes for newly issued stock, shown as a reduction of stockholders' equity, with the $40.5 million in cash reducing what Scilex owes.

The restatements are expected to cut total assets by $8.1 million as of Sept. 30, 2025, $92.2 million at the end of 2025, $57.1 million as of March 31, and $49 million as of June 30. They cover the 2025 annual report plus three quarterly reports filed between November 2025 and August 2026, and Datavault expects to reverse the crypto gains and losses it had recorded on the coins.

Datavault had counted those Bitcoin balances as a source of liquidity, so management is reassessing whether the company can continue as a going concern, the accounting test for whether a business can keep operating and meet its obligations. The filing says collection of the amounts owed by Scilex is uncertain, and its risk list includes Scilex's creditworthiness, the company's reliance on a third-party custodian, Nasdaq listing compliance, and litigation or regulatory inquiries tied to the restatement.

Scilex's own quarterly filing shows Biconomy was already part of the deal. Scilex said it sold 12.5 million shares of its Semnur Pharmaceuticals subsidiary to Biconomy on Sept. 23, 2025 for $200 million in Bitcoin, then used $150 million of that to buy Datavault stock.

More Americans Have Tried Crypto, But Few Are Sticking With It: Survey

On June 24, 2026, the same month Datavault says it asked to withdraw its Bitcoin, Scilex signed a binding term sheet to buy 837 BTC held in Datavault's Biconomy wallet for $50 million, subject to a definitive agreement. Scilex agreed to an initial $30 million payment and the remaining $20 million in quarterly installments through Dec. 31, 2028, payable in cash or Scilex securities at its discretion. The 837 BTC, added to the 491.431 BTC already sold back, equals the 1,328.43 BTC of the original agreement.

Datavault stock bounced to near $0.085 on Wednesday. Scilex's purchase price under the 2025 agreement worked out to an effective $0.5378 per share. Datavault has not said when it will file the restated statements, and it warned that delays could extend to its quarterly report for the period ended Sept. 30, 2026.

title: Kevin O’Leary says he still owns Bitcoin, but two risks have his attention
summary: The Shark Tank investor says regulatory uncertainty and quantum computing are weighing on Bitcoin, and he is looking at IBM as a way to play the shift.
content:
Kevin O'Leary says he has not walked away from Bitcoin, even as the asset struggles to push higher.

In a post on X , the Shark Tank investor named two factors behind the plateau and said he is tracking both closely.

"Why is Bitcoin plateauing ?" O'Leary asked. His answer: institutions want regulatory clarity before they invest, and quantum computing has become a growing concern for some investors.

"Why is Bitcoin plateauing? Two factors are weighing on it: institutions want regulatory clarity before they invest, and quantum computing has become a growing concern for some investors," he wrote in his post.

"I still own Bitcoin, but I'm paying close attention to both sides of this shift," he added.

He also sees opportunity in the second risk. "The quantum opportunity is also why I'm looking at companies like IBM," O'Leary said, suggesting the same technology that worries Bitcoin holders could reward investors elsewhere.

Yesterday angel investor Jason Calacanis had issued one of his bluntest warnings on Bitcoin, telling followers to sell and move their money.

Related: Elon Musk has a bold answer to America's $40 trillion debt crisis

He predicted Bitcoin "will test the 57k low again in the next 12 months," pointing to outflows from Bitcoin exchange-traded funds as a warning sign.

The post echoes comments O'Leary made last month. Speaking at the Avalanche Summit in New York, he said he was adding crypto positions again .

"I'm back in the saddle buying new positions, putting my bets on for this next cycle," he said. He added that he is waiting for a major stock exchange to adopt a blockchain, which he called a "watershed moment."

On regulation, O'Leary had said he expects crypto legislation to return after the CLARITY Act's Senate setback, since lawmakers are working on tax policy for digital assets. He does not expect a bill before the midterms.

On quantum, he had said in a separate interview that Bitcoin could reach $1 million, but only if the industry settles the doubt around the technology. He called the threat "Q-Day," the point at which quantum machines could break the algorithms and encryption protecting blockchains .

O'Leary has also said Bitcoin could eventually take a 1% to 3% share of alternative-asset allocation, similar to what institutions hold in gold.

title: Fifteen-Minute Bets Scratch the Bitcoin Itch
summary: Bloomberg's Emily Nicolle joins Scarlet Fu and Isabelle Lee on "Bloomberg Crypto." While Bitcoin appears to have fallen into an autumnal slumber, another corner of the speculative trading arena is thriving. Prediction-market volumes are soaring to new heights, and even with token prices rangebound, crypto's playing its own role in the bounce.
content:
Bloomberg's Emily Nicolle joins Scarlet Fu and Isabelle Lee on "Bloomberg Crypto." While Bitcoin appears to have fallen into an autumnal slumber, another corner of the speculative trading arena is thriving. Prediction-market volumes are soaring to new heights, and even with token prices rangebound, crypto's playing its own role in the bounce.

Emily, you had a fantastic newsletter. It's titled 15-minute bets scratch the Bitcoin itch. But to the uninitiated, can you talk to us about the so-called up-down contracts?

Yeah, so these are a type of contract that you can get on Polymarket, Kalshi, a lot of different prediction market venues, and they're really growing in popularity. We've been seeing them all across this year and they're hitting new heights as you said at the beginning. Uh, what it means is that you can bet on the price of Bitcoin in the future in different intervals. So, on Polymarket that goes as short as five minutes, on Kalshi as short as 15. You can do it the next half an hour, the next hour, uh, all the way to the end what the price will be at the end of this year. But those short-dated bets are what really drive volumes at the moment. It's what got traders excited. It's getting a lot of new people into the space as well, if you're familiar with crypto but not with prediction markets and vice versa. And they've become a really exciting part of the area.

So, it just sounds like people are trading for the sake of trading as opposed to having conviction in the price action of Bitcoin or any other crypto asset. Is is that the right way to think about it?

I'd say so, yeah. I mean, if you look at the markets that are more like, you know, where will Bitcoin end up at the end of this year, betting on, you know, if it'll hit 100,000, if it'll hit 200,000, those are probably ones that involve a bit more analysis. I think one of the people I spoke to for the newsletter said that once you get to kind of 30 minutes and up, maybe you can start applying a model to that. But anything shorter than that, it really is more of a coin flip. And so in those cases, we're more likely seeing traders who are wanting just to have a bit of fun, speculate on where they think Bitcoin might be up or down. And even, you know, within that window, you can be trading in and out of your positions. You don't have to hold it the whole time. So you can be watching the charts, seeing how it's going, and in the end of the day, it is basically a coin flip. It's a yes or a no.

But Emily, what is the appeal of this? Because why can't they just trade contracts or options or buy the coin themselves and sell it again? Like, I feel like it's another layer, another added vehicle, so to speak, in this entirely sprawling ecosystem.

I guess you have to think about it in terms of people who are less familiar with crypto. For them, it's kind of, you know, they might be on Kalshi or Polymarket because they're more familiar with that structure. You know, you're playing in regular cash money, not necessarily cryptocurrency. And in those spaces, you might be thinking, well, okay, this is something I can do. I've had one person describe it to me for example, something that I can do while I'm watching a sports game and I'm waiting for my sports game bet to end, I might want to go and play some of these and just go up and down. And they don't have to think about the the custody requirements of crypto or the security requirements of crypto, they can just do it within the prediction markets app themselves. It's also, however, something I wrote about earlier this year, it's a big attraction for traders who want to deploy kind of big armies of trading bots to look at this kind of stuff. It's very easy to do both sides of these things.

title: Bitcoin Keeps Hovering in the Same Range. These 5 Cryptocurrencies Are Showing More Volatility.
summary: Zcash, Dash, Hyperliquid, Bitcoin Cash and NEAR have distinct developments to watch, but recent price reversals complicate the case for a broad rally.
content:
Bitcoin was trading near $81,000 Wednesday as cryptocurrency traders looked for signs of another sustained rally, with several altcoins drawing attention through price swings, technological developments and growing interest in decentralized financial services.

Zcash, Dash, Hyperliquid, Bitcoin Cash and NEAR Protocol are among the cryptocurrencies attracting interest, although their recent performance has varied considerably. Ethereum, the second-largest cryptocurrency, hovered near $2,345, with both it and Bitcoin trading below their levels from a week earlier.

The broader cryptocurrency market rebounded during the third quarter, with total market capitalization rising 39.6% to approximately $3 trillion, ending three consecutive quarters of declines, according to CoinGecko's industry analysis. However, average daily trading volume fell 8.6% from the previous quarter, while spot trading on centralized exchanges declined 14.2%.

Among the five tokens, Zcash (ZEC) has attracted attention for its focus on financial privacy. It traded around $1,300 Wednesday, with a market capitalization exceeding $20 billion and daily trading volume approaching $800 million.

Unlike Bitcoin, whose transactions are recorded on a publicly accessible blockchain, Zcash allows users to conceal details such as the sender, recipient and amount through cryptographic technology.

Use of those features has also increased. Nearly 5 million ZEC were held in shielded pools in September, representing approximately 23% of the cryptocurrency's circulating supply at the time, according to data examined by The Block. The figure measures use of the network's privacy features rather than establishing what drove its recent price movements.

Dash (DASH) has also been expanding its privacy technology. The cryptocurrency traded near $53 Wednesday, with a market value of approximately $686 million.

In August, Dash introduced shielded transactions on its Evolution mainnet, allowing users to conceal certain payment details. The upgrade builds on technology developed for Zcash and forms part of Dash's efforts to improve its payment and wallet services.

The project said the new functionality was designed to combine transaction privacy with faster settlement in an official development announcement.

While Zcash and Dash focus on payments and privacy, Hyperliquid (HYPE) operates in decentralized derivatives trading, allowing users to trade cryptocurrency futures and other products without relying on a conventional centralized exchange.

HYPE traded between $80 and $82 Wednesday after a substantial rally earlier in the year. The token climbed 40.5% over four days in August following developments concerning potential access to U.S. markets. It subsequently reached a record $98 on September 23, according to CoinGecko's third-quarter report.

Trading activity also expanded, with the platform's average daily volume increasing 35.2% during the quarter to approximately $850 million.

Bitcoin Cash (BCH), meanwhile, has drawn attention through short-term price gains rather than a major new technological or regulatory announcement.

The cryptocurrency traded around $290 Wednesday after rising approximately 4% to 5% in earlier market snapshots. Its market capitalization approached $6 billion.

Bitcoin Cash emerged from a split with Bitcoin in 2017 and was designed to support peer-to-peer digital payments. Its blockchain allows larger blocks than Bitcoin's original design, enabling more transactions to be processed within each block.

No single verified development has been established as the cause of its latest price movement.

The fifth cryptocurrency, NEAR Protocol (NEAR), focuses on blockchain infrastructure supporting decentralized applications and transactions across different networks.

NEAR traded between $4.60 and $4.70 Wednesday, with daily trading volume approaching $470 million.

One of its projects, NEAR Intents, is designed to simplify transactions between blockchains. Users specify the outcome they want, while the system handles the technical steps required to complete it.

However, the platform suffered a security incident on Oct. 1 when a vulnerability involving its deposit and withdrawal infrastructure resulted in approximately $3.8 million being compromised. Affected services were temporarily suspended, and the team subsequently said it had patched the vulnerability and recovered the funds.

Beyond developments involving individual tokens, Bitcoin's performance remains an important factor in the broader cryptocurrency market.

U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded $176 million in net inflows on Oct. 27, including $151.5 million into BlackRock's IBIT and $24.5 million into Fidelity's FBTC.

Despite those inflows, Glassnode's Oct. 28 on-chain analysis found that Bitcoin had repeatedly struggled to maintain prices above $84,000 to $85,000 during 2026.

The research also identified declining ETF trading activity and lower volatility, with buying interest on Binance concentrated around $78,000 to $79,000. Glassnode said volatility had fallen to levels last seen in the summer of 2023.

Derivatives trading, however, has expanded more rapidly. Open interest in perpetual futures on centralized exchanges increased 40.6% during the third quarter, exceeding $100 billion, even as spot trading volumes declined.

content:
Itaú Unibanco became the first Brazilian bank to register for crypto trading and custody, covering 15 digital assets including XRP, Bitcoin, and Ether.

Itaú's filing does not involve XRP for settlements or any Ripple partnership. XRP is simply one of 15 assets available to buy.

Itaú's recent filing aligns with Brazilian Central Bank Resolution 520, which took effect on February 2, 2026. This resolution required licensed financial institutions to notify the central bank of their cryptocurrency activities within 270 days, and each filing must include an independent technical certification. Any bank that fails to meet this requirement must stop its crypto services within 30 days, while crypto exchanges need to apply for full authorization.

Itaú's registration combines trading with custody services, meaning the bank holds customers' cryptocurrencies on their behalf. Under the new rules, this categorizes Itaú as a brokerage, allowing it to buy and sell cryptocurrencies according to customers' instructions and store them.

The 15 digital assets available through Itaú's íon investment app include Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP, USDC, Arbitrum, Bitcoin Cash, Chainlink, Avalanche, Litecoin, Optimism, Aave, Uniswap, Polygon, and PAX Gold, as listed on the bank's product page.

Although crypto is part of Itaú's broader investment strategy, it has not yet contributed significantly to the bank's reported financials. In its third-quarter 2025 report, Itaú Asset established a structure to manage crypto funds, a first for Brazilian banks. Moreover, Itaú completed its acquisition of a 50.1% stake in Avenue, a U.S. digital securities broker, in January 2026.

However, these ventures haven't been reported as distinct revenue streams. Itaú's financial results are divided into three segments, with only a 5.8% increase in commissions and banking fees reported, focusing on cards, investment banking, and insurance, and no mention of crypto-related income.

While Itaú was the first bank to register for crypto trading and custody, it isn't the only one offering these services. Nubank ( NYSE: NU ), Brazil's largest fintech, lists 28 different cryptocurrencies, but it's unclear if XRP is among them.

Banco do Brasil, the state-owned bank, began letting customers buy Bitcoin and Ether directly in January 2026 and reported over R$11 million in transactions. Other banks, including Bradesco and Santander Brasil, have expanded their cryptocurrency offerings since 2025.

BTG Pactual, Brazil's largest investment bank, launched a crypto trading platform, and in September 2025, Banco Safra went further by issuing a dollar-pegged stablecoin called Safra Dólar and keeping custody in-house. All these banks face the same October 30 deadline.

It's worth noting that Itaú did not mention any specific settlement asset in its filing, meaning the bank did not say it would use XRP, or any other token, for cross-border transactions. XRP is simply one of the 15 cryptocurrencies available for purchase, alongside Litecoin and Uniswap. There has been no indication of the XRP Ledger being used, nor any partnership with Ripple for payment routing.

Furthermore, central bank filings as of March 2026 have shown that Brazilian banks hold no virtual assets on their balance sheets, indicating that any XRP purchased through Itaú's platform belongs entirely to customers.

Itaú's research has not favored XRP in its recommendations. The bank previously suggested a 1% to 3% allocation to Bitcoin, calling it a supplementary holding, while not highlighting XRP.

title: MicroStrategy Approves Daily Dividends. Will Bitcoin Buying Return?
summary: MicroStrategy wins a 99.3% vote for daily dividends after a week with no Bitcoin buys. Here is how it could restart buying.
content:
Michael Saylor's MicroStrategy (now Strategy) has approved daily dividend payments across four preferred stocks, potentially reopening a major funding route for Bitcoin purchases after a week of buying nothing.

Shareholders backed the change on Wednesday, October 28, with 99.3% of votes cast in favor, according to Saylor and an SEC filing.

In simple terms, investors holding Strategy's preferred shares will receive smaller, more frequent payments instead of waiting weeks or months. Annual dividend rates remain unchanged.

The company's flagship Stretch (STRC) stock, currently offering a 12% annual dividend, switches on November 1. Three other preferred stocks follow in January, subject to final implementation.

That is the bigger question.

Strategy bought no Bitcoin between October 19 and 25. Instead, it spent $204.9 million repurchasing STRC shares.

The company holds 848,517 BTC, but its preferred-stock funding model has faced pressure.

STRC targets $100 per share. The closer it trades to that price, the easier it becomes for MicroStrategy to raise fresh money by issuing more shares.

Daily dividends could attract buyers and help stabilize STRC's price. Strategy says the change should improve liquidity.

However, another Bitcoin purchase this week remains uncertain. The vote creates no immediate cash, and Strategy had just $242.4 million in unrestricted operating cash as of October 25.

For common shareholders, the potential benefit is indirect.

Stronger demand for preferred shares could give Strategy more money to buy Bitcoin, supporting its accumulation strategy and potentially MSTR's valuation.

But issuing preferred stock creates additional dividend obligations. Investors must also consider Bitcoin's price and the company's financing costs.

Strategy's buying power remains substantial, although its recent purchases have become relatively small.

It bought just 267 BTC in the week before its pause, worth $22.1 million. Bitcoin now sees tens of billions of dollars in daily trading.

Coinbase Institutional research shows ETFs have overtaken corporate treasuries as Bitcoin's main buyers since August.

Strategy's purchases still matter to long-term supply. For the wider market, ETF demand and macroeconomic conditions increasingly carry more weight.

title: Can ORE Make Hard Money Without Proof of Work?
summary: ORE has dropped computational proof of work. Here is how it works, and the case for and against it as a store of value.
content:
I remember writing about ORE when it first launched in 2024 and the congestion it caused nearly brought Solana to its knees.

A budding proof-of-work (PoW) protocol then, ORE's explosive popularity showed the enduring allure of mining among crypto natives. Who doesn't love the idea of "earning passive income" and striking digital gold? And as the activity that originally secured Bitcoin, mining has become central to the idea of cryptographically "hard" money.

Last cycle offered little reason to look beyond Bitcoin as crypto's leading store of value, but that is changing. Between its unresolved quantum vulnerability, questions about its long-term security budget, and increasing institutionalization, people are looking at cryptocurrencies that might offer some of the same monetary qualities.

Fittingly, the assets getting the most attention as alternative stores of value retain Bitcoin's PoW foundation while building on it to address some of BTC's shortcomings.

Zcash, for example, pairs PoW and a fixed supply with native privacy and its pursuit to turn quantum-resistant . Newcomers like Pearl hope to improve on the economics of BTC mining and solve its security budget concerns as a result.

And the market has started to reward these ideas. Over the past three months, Zcash and Pearl have gained roughly 170% and 400%, respectively, outpacing Bitcoin 's ~25% gain. ORE has joined them, rising approximately 170% and increasingly finding itself in the conversation around alternative stores of value.

Yet unlike Zcash and Pearl, ORE has abandoned computational proof of work altogether.

Today, ORE still operates on Solana, with a maximum supply of 3 million tokens . Its tokens are "mined," or rather distributed through a lottery-like mechanism where participants commit SOL for a chance to win newly issued coins.

That makes ORE an unusual contender for hard money: its design looks more aimed at making mining accessible again while turning Solana's speculative culture toward something more enduring. Let's look at how ORE works and the arguments for and against its potential as a store of value.

ORE calls its foundation virtual mining . Each round, participants commit SOL to one or more squares on a shared 5×5 grid, hoping to land on the winning one. Here's how it works:

Commit SOL: Miners deposit SOL across any of the grid's 25 squares, each with an equal 4% chance of being selected.

Determine the winner: Roughly every minute, one of the 25 squares is randomly selected to receive 1 ORE. Fifteen squares are "split" squares : if one wins, its miners divide the ORE in proportion to how much SOL they deposited there. If one of the other ten "solo" squares wins, a single miner takes the full ORE, with their odds based on their share of deposits on that square.

Collect winnings: All miners receive most of their deposited SOL back. The protocol keeps 1% of deposits on the winning square and 10.9% on losing squares . The 1% is an admin fee paid to a separate fee wallet on every deposit; the other 9.9% taken from losing squares is the protocol's revenue.

ORE's 5×5 mining grid. Starred squares are "solo" squares. Source: ORE

There's also a jackpot called the Motherlode . An additional 0.2 ORE is issued into it each round, and each round has a 1-in-500 chance of triggering a payout to miners on the winning square.

So "mining" is more of a lottery where participants compete to acquire ORE below market price, though whether they actually secure a discount depends on expenses, the ORE price, and, of course, luck. Claiming newly mined ORE also incurs a separate 10% "refining" fee , which rewards miners who leave their earnings unclaimed.

Much of what miners pay, however, goes toward supporting the asset they are trying to win.

The 9.9% of deposits the protocol takes from losing squares is its revenue, most of which is used to buy existing ORE from the market . Those purchased tokens are then split two ways:

90% are burned and removed from supply. Because ORE's 3 million cap limits the supply that exists at any one time, not the total ever minted, each burn frees room for new ORE to be mined. That mining generates the revenue that funds more buybacks, and so on.

10% goes to stakers, rewarding holders who deposit (stake) their ORE with the protocol.

The loop scales with activity: greater mining generates more revenue, funding larger buybacks that can potentially offset new issuance.

Founder Hardhat Chad describes this as addressing proof of work's " value leak ." Bitcoin miners spend on electricity and hardware to secure the network, with that money going to outside providers. ORE, by comparison, uses miners' expenditures to buy ORE off the market, directing that spending back toward the asset itself.

ORE has also recently introduced a reserve , which holds a portion of mining revenue in assets including SOL, USDC, tokenized gold (GLDx), and JitoSOL. It deploys these assets as buy orders across different price ranges below the market price, with acquired ORE following the same 90/10 split.

So it doesn't "back" ORE in the traditional sense. Holders can't redeem ORE for these assets, nor does the reserve guarantee a minimum price. Rather, it's a pool of capital the protocol can use to buy ORE during selloffs.

It's a novel approach to distributing and supporting a scarce asset.

But does it mean ORE's hard enough to store value? Let's look at both sides of the debate.

The major objection to ORE as a store of value, as Tulip King argues , is that it doesn't control the blockchain securing it.

Unlike Bitcoin or Zcash, whose native tokens are integral to their networks' security, ORE relies on Solana. Its future is therefore tied to another network's incentives, governance, and development. An upgrade that benefits Solana, for example, might not benefit ORE, and ORE holders would have little say in that decision.

Tulip also questions whether ORE has a compelling reason to exist , noting that Bitcoin has a political and social reason for existing . For context, Zcash was created to bring privacy to cryptocurrency and is now working toward quantum resistance, while Pearl is responding to miners' growing interest in AI and concerns about Bitcoin's long-term security budget. ORE, by comparison, seems to offer mainly fairness and accessibility, giving anyone with a Solana wallet the opportunity to mine. Is that enough to make it a lasting store of value? For many, like lesabrefomo and No Limit Holding's Brian Breslow , it doesn't.

Proponents, though, like ORE advocate NSE , see these characteristics differently.

To them, accessibility matters. Bitcoin mining has gone from something anyone with a computer could participate in to an industry dominated by specialized hardware and large-scale operations. Bitcoin's not the only one. Both Zcash and Pearl have high barriers to entry for ordinary miners. With ORE, anyone with a Solana wallet and some SOL can participate. Yes, there are still costs, but the barrier to entry is considerably lower. For them, giving people the opportunity to participate in mining, rather than simply buying an asset, is valuable in itself.

NSE also sees ORE's dependence on Solana as a trade-off worth making rather than a weakness. NSE argues that ORE inherits Solana's security and low fees, which lets it concentrate on issuance and distribution, while conceding that it is not fully sovereign. Others, like ORE supporter yourfriendbrett , argue that the design deliberately prioritizes usability over maximal independence of settlement, offering a scarce, accessible asset inside the Solana ecosystem.

Lastly, there's the cultural argument, made by supporters such as pokerchessman and NYSoul2x , which positions ORE as a foil to Solana's frenetic environment of short-lived speculation: a scarce, fairly distributed asset designed to retain value amid this environment.

There's something fitting about using a lottery-like mining mechanism on the "casino chain," but directing that activity toward something people might actually want to hold.

ORE's accessibility and cultural fit offer a compelling answer to why it needs to exist. It's responding to the barriers of traditional PoW mining while attempting to turn Solana's speculative instincts toward something more enduring.

While I wouldn't put ORE in the same category as Bitcoin, Zcash, or Pearl, ORE's mechanism design and cultural fit make a compelling case for the project, even if they don't yet establish it as a lasting store of value.

Whether ORE can sustain its momentum and prove resilient over time will tell us more about how far those qualities can take it. For now, it's an interesting experiment in what hard money might look like without its own proof-of-work consensus.

title: Matt Damon’s Crypto Ad Turns Five: What $1,000 in Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP Is Worth Now
summary: Key Takeaways A $1,000 Bitcoin purchase on the campaign’s launch date would now be worth about $1,333, compared with $548 for Ethereum and $1,255 for…
content:
Key Takeaways

A $1,000 Bitcoin purchase on the campaign's launch date would now be worth about $1,333, compared with $548 for Ethereum and $1,255 for XRP.

All three investments suffered substantial losses before recovering to varying degrees.

Damon is listed as a keynote speaker at Ripple Swell through his work with Water.org.

On this day five years ago, Matt Damon appeared in a Crypto.com advert telling crypto investors that "fortune favors the brave."

Five years later, those who were taken by the campaign and put money into Bitcoin or XRP would be modestly ahead — while Ethereum buyers would be sitting on major losses.

The anniversary coincides with Damon's latest crypto industry engagement, a scheduled appearance at Ripple's Swell conference in New York.

The advert casts entering the crypto market as an act of courage, with Damon drawing a distinction between those who seize opportunities and those who hesitate.

"History is filled with almosts," Damon says at the start of the advertisement.

"With those who almost adventured who almost achieved but ultimately for them it proved to be too much."

Viewers were encouraged to identify with "the ones who embrace the moment and commit," framing the decision to use a crypto platform as part of a much grander story of ambition.

Over the last five years, the advert has gained over 18 million views on YouTube alone.

Crypto has grown and changed dramatically in the five years since Damon's advert aired.

The industry has weathered a multibillion-dollar fraud scandal, expanded onto Wall Street, and become a major policy priority in Washington.

In 2024, FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison for fraud involving billions of dollars in customer money.

The technology changed, too.

Ethereum abandoned energy-intensive mining in September 2022 through the Merge, switching to proof-of-stake and cutting its estimated energy consumption by 99.95%.

Wall Street, however, may be the biggest breakthrough.

In January 2024, the US Securities and Exchange Commission approved spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products , allowing investors to gain exposure through conventional brokerage accounts.

Approval of exchange rule changes for spot Ether products followed that May. Buying crypto exposure no longer necessarily means opening an account with a crypto exchange.

By 2025, crypto had an advocate in the White House.

Donald Trump made support for digital assets part of his campaign to return to power.

Once back in office, he ordered the creation of a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve in March.

Five years after Damon urged viewers to be brave, crypto had secured a foothold on Wall Street and support in Washington.

For those who bought in, however, greater acceptance has not always translated into greater returns.

To see whether fortune favored those who bought in, CCN calculated what a $1,000 investment in Bitcoin, Ethereum or XRP on the day Damon's advert launched would be worth five years later.

Bitcoin delivered the strongest return of the three, producing a nominal profit of approximately $333.

However, getting there required first enduring a much weaker position.

By Dec. 31, 2022, Bitcoin traded at $16,547.50, reducing the original holding to about $273, a loss of nearly 73% against the purchase price.

The fifth-anniversary result also comes after another retreat.

However, Bitcoin remains about 29% below its price from a year ago.

Ethereum produced the weakest result, leaving the hypothetical buyer with a loss of approximately $452.

At the end of 2022, the holding would have been worth about $279, based on ETH's price of $1,196.77.

That represented a decline of roughly 72% from the initial investment.

Ethereum has since recovered from that level, but its anniversary price remains well below the entry point.

From $2,347.32, Ethereum would need to rise by approximately 83% to return to the original $1,000, before costs.

XRP would have left the investor with a profit of approximately $255.

Its path was also uncomfortable.

At the end of 2022, XRP traded at $0.3399, putting the holding's value at around $321, down approximately 68% from the initial purchase.

title: Fed Stands Pat, Bitcoin Holds Steady—But a December Rate Hike Is in Play
summary: The Federal Reserve left rates unchanged Wednesday in a 10-2 vote, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favoring a hike.
content:
The Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote, with two officials dissenting in favor of another quarter-point hike. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted against the decision, according to the Fed's statement.

Bitcoin barely moved, edging up about 0.2% to roughly $80,950 in the minutes after the 2 p.m. ET announcement. CME FedWatch, a tool that converts bets on interest rate futures into probabilities, had put the odds of no change at around 90% before the decision.

The decision reaches well beyond Wall Street, because the federal funds rate, which is what banks charge each other for overnight loans, sets the baseline for what consumers pay on credit cards and car loans. The Fed raised that rate in September, its first hike since 2023 , in a unanimous 12-0 vote.

"Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace," the Fed said in its statement, a step up from the solid pace it cited in September. "Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little," it added.

On inflation, the Fed said it remains elevated and that "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal."

Hammack also dissented in July, when the committee held rates in a 9-3 vote with Neel Kashkari and Lorie Logan joining her in favoring a hike. Kashkari and Logan sided with the majority this time, so the number of dissents fell to two from three.

Oil remains a major driver of inflation because the U.S.-Iran war has squeezed global supply, and U.S. crude settled at $99.90 a barrel on Tuesday. Pricier crude lifts gasoline and shipping costs, which eventually show up on grocery shelves, and consumer prices rose 3.7% in the 12 months through September, with gasoline alone jumping 9.1% in the month, the Labor Department reported.

Higher inflation makes investors demand more interest for lending to the government, which lifts Treasury yields, the interest rate on U.S. government debt. The 10-year yield, the benchmark that mortgage rates follow, closed Tuesday at 4.99% after peaking at 5.31% on Oct. 5, so a nearly risk-free return is available without owning anything volatile.

Bitcoin pays no yield, so when Treasuries pay more, money tends to drift out of riskier assets such as crypto and stocks. The price briefly poked above $81,600 earlier Wednesday before slipping back, below a resistance zone between $81,000 and $82,500 that has capped several rally attempts this year.

Leverage, meaning borrowed money used to make bigger bets, tends to exaggerate those moves around Fed events. When prices swing against a trader, the exchange automatically closes the position, a liquidation that adds to the selling pressure. After Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech in August, about $481 million in crypto positions were liquidated within 24 hours.

Traders had put the odds of another quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting above 70% before the decision. Minutes from September's meeting show most officials judged another increase would likely be appropriate by year-end.

The October jobs report arrives Nov. 6, October inflation data follows on Nov. 10, and the Fed meets again Dec. 8-9, when it will also publish new economic projections. Fed Chairman Warsh will hold a press conference at 2:30 p.m. to elaborate on the Fed's decision.
