title: Grant Cardone Says Fannie Mae Will ‘Wish They Gave Me a Loan on That Bitcoin, Not on the Real Estate’ But He Never Mentions the Bitcoin When He Borrows
summary: Cardone says he has Bitcoin inside his real estate dealings, and thinks that could end up being the better investment.
content:
Grant Cardone says the apartment buildings his firm finances through Fannie Mae (FNMA) carry Bitcoin (BTCUSD) alongside them, and the lender isn't told. "I never tell Fannie Mae I'm putting Bitcoin on it," he said on stage at the Bitcoin Treasuries Conference in New York, in remarks reported by Stocktwits on Oct. 11, adding that he leaves the Bitcoin out of the conversation "because it's just too much."

Cardone is the sales trainer and real estate investor whose Cardone Capital raises money from retail investors for apartment deals, and who this month said a SpaceX (SPCX) employee who just became a millionaire would be making a mistake by selling stock. At the time of his Bitcoin remarks, he was speaking on a panel alongside Anthony Bassili, the President of Coinbase Global's (COIN) Coinbase Asset Management. The conference agenda lists the session for Sept. 28. Every figure that follows is his own, and no filings accompany them.

By Cardone's account, his firm is working on about $600 million in deals, carrying about $350 million in debt. Bitcoin was trading near $83,330 when the Stocktwits report ran. Cardone repeated a forecast that the crypto could reach $400,000 or $500,000 within five years, and tied the lender comment to it: If Bitcoin gets there, "they're going to wish they gave me a loan on that Bitcoin, not on the real estate."

He also described how he sells the idea, and the pitch runs the same way. Cardone said he has brought about 3,000 people into BTC over the past 18 months by leading with property rather than the cryptocurrency. "I never talk about Bitcoin. I talk about the real estate." As Stocktwits reports it, that line is about investors, not lenders, but the method is the same one he described using with Fannie Mae. The real estate is the conversation, and the Bitcoin sits behind it.

Fannie Mae is the government-sponsored enterprise — in federal conservatorship since 2008— that buys and guarantees mortgages, including loans on apartment buildings through its network of approved multifamily lenders. Multifamily underwriting centers on the property's cash flow, with Fannie Mae's Multifamily Selling and Servicing Guide setting out the sponsor's and any guarantor's financial requirements. Cardone did not describe what his own loan documents require of him, and nothing in the remarks establishes that a BTC position held alongside a property has to be disclosed to the lender at all. Barchart has not seen the loan agreements.

What makes the admission land is where the lender was already heading. In June 2025, the Federal Housing Finance Agency directed Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac (FMCC) to prepare proposals for counting cryptocurrency held on regulated U.S. exchanges as an asset in mortgage risk assessments, and in March 2026, Barchart reported that Fannie Mae is now accepting crypto-backed mortgages. Those moves cover single-family home loans to individuals, not the apartment-building loans Cardone described, so the lender he says he keeps Bitcoin from has been moving toward counting it on a different side of its business. Cardone's version of the same idea arrives from the borrower's side: He would rather Fannie lent against the coin.

Cardone has been promoting the pairing publicly since at least June, when it drew a response from Peter Schiff, the gold investor and Bitcoin critic. "Combining real estate with Bitcoin solves nothing," Schiff posted on X on June 21, arguing that a building's rental income already covers its running costs. "Happy to debate this," he added. The Stocktwits report also noted that Better Home & Finance (BETR), which offers a Bitcoin-backed down-payment loan, requires the pledged crypto to be worth 250% of the loan, a reminder of how much haircut a lender applies when it does count crypto.

Cardone's position, as he put it on stage, is that the agency has the collateral backwards: It lent him money against the buildings, and the asset he expects to appreciate is the one it never asked about. Whether Fannie Mae agrees is a question it has not answered publicly, and Cardone's five-year number is the kind of forecast that can be scored in 2031.

title: Is Bitcoin Heading for Another New Record High?
summary: After falling below $58,000 per token, Bitcoin has recovered. After the implosive price action that halved Bitcoin's value from October 2025 through July 2026, Bitcoin could be back on track for another explosive rally.
content:
I asked if Bitcoin was going to trade above $100,000 per token on Barchart on September 11, 2026, when I concluded with the following:

With four months left in 2026, Bitcoin could reach and exceed $100,000 per token. From April through August 2025, Bitcoin rose nearly $50,000 per token. With the leading cryptocurrency close to $23,000 below the $100,000 level, a rally to that level is not out of the question, but time is running short.

Bitcoin was trading at $76,792.27 on September 11, and Coinbase (COIN), a leading cryptocurrency exchange, was $172.28 per share. On October 26, Bitcoin was just above $80,000, and COIN shares were around $161.

Bitcoin isn't running away on the upside, but the recovery from the July 2026 low could mark the start of another explosive rally.

The monthly chart shows that Bitcoin has experienced explosive and implosive price behavior over the past years, but that the long-term pattern of higher lows and higher highs remains firmly intact.

Bitcoin is a highly volatile asset. If the July 2026 low was a bottom and the pattern holds, the leading cryptocurrency could head toward a higher high above the October 2025 high of $126,184.05 per token.

Over time, Coinbase Global (COIN) correlates well with Bitcoin's price action.

The monthly chart shows that COIN has experienced massive volatility since its April 2021 IPO, which opened at $381 per share. COIN has traded as low as $31.55 in January 2023, and as high as $444.64 per share in July 2025. While COIN does not track Bitcoin precisely, it does tend to move higher and lower with the leading cryptocurrency. Bitcoin now accounts for nearly 60% of the total cryptocurrency market cap. As the asset class leader, rising Bitcoin prices increase market activity, boosting COIN's revenue and earnings. During implosive price action, COIN's business suffers. As a result, COIN's financial results are as volatile as cryptocurrency prices.

The year-to-date charts highlight the current support and resistance levels for Bitcoin and COIN.

The daily chart shows that Bitcoin has traded between the July 1 low of $57,717.55 and the January 14 high of $97,764.04 in 2026. Current technical resistance sits at the September 21, 2026, high of $87,397 per token, a gateway to the January 14 high and the October 2025 all-time high of nearly $126,185 per token. Nearby technical support is at the September 15 low of $74,887.50 per token. Below that, the July low is the next downside target.

If the historical implosive and explosive pattern holds, Bitcoin offers a slightly better-than-1:1 risk-reward ratio at $80,200 per token based on its first technical support and resistance levels.

The daily chart shows that COIN has traded between the July 31 low of $139.11 and the January 14 high of $263.07 in 2026. Current technical resistance stands at the September 21, 2026, high of $208.33 per share. Above the late September high, technical resistance levels for COIN are at the May 14, 2026, high of $222.35, the January 14, 2026, high of $263.07, the December 9, 2025, high of $284.74, the October 2025 highs of $373.25 and $402.16, and the July 2025 record high of $444.64 per share.

Nearby technical support is at the July 31, 2026, low of $139.11 per share

COIN offers a better-than-1:2 risk-reward ratio at $161 per share, based on its first technical support and resistance levels.

Risk is always a function of potential rewards. Assets like Bitcoin and COIN, with extremely high volatility, offer trading opportunities, but careful attention to risk-reward dynamics is crucial for success.

Any long or short position in the leading cryptocurrency or the cryptocurrency trading platform requires a plan, including stops and profit horizons that reflect a logical risk-reward balance, and favor rewards over risks. If price moves in the anticipated direction, it is acceptable to raise profit targets, but only by adjusting stop levels to protect profits and/or capital. If price moves contrary to expectations, stop levels protect capital and leave room for other trading opportunities. Explosive and implosive price action requires planning and discipline that increase the odds of success. Meanwhile, just because historical trading patterns and current price action favor higher prices, past performance does not guarantee future performance.

Bitcoin's path of least resistance will likely pull the correlated COIN share price along. With a little over two months until the end of 2026, the odds of Bitcoin reaching $100,000 are declining. From the current level, Bitcoin would have to rally around $20,000 per token to reach that level. While $20,000 is about 25% of the current price, Bitcoin has plenty of examples of moving more than $20,000 over a two-month period.

I am cautiously bullish on Bitcoin at the current price levels, but the potential for extreme volatility remains high. A risk-off period in markets could send prices lower, but a continuation of the current trend since the recent lows could lead to another in a long series of explosive rallies. A plan that includes tight stops, favorable risk-reward dynamics, and the understanding that accepting small losses in pursuit of significant gains could be optimal over the coming weeks and months.

title: Coinbase Now Offers Fixed-Rate Bitcoin-Backed Loans. Here's What Crypto Investors Need to Know.
summary: The crypto exchange previously only offered Bitcoin-backed loans with variable rates.
content:
Coinbase (NASDAQ: COIN), one of the most popular crypto exchanges, has offered on-chain Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC)-backed loans since January 2025. These loans allow you to borrow USDC against your Bitcoin, but until recently, only variable-rate loans were available.

On Sept. 22, Coinbase announced fixed-rate Bitcoin-backed loans through Morpho Midnight. While this could be a useful option in certain situations, investors should understand the terms first.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Coinbase offers loans through its Coinbase Borrow service. Morpho Midnight is a lending protocol that operates on Base, an Ethereum Layer-2 blockchain. When you borrow this way, your Bitcoin is converted to Coinbase Wrapped BTC and locked in a smart contract on Base.

These are short-term loans, with payment due in full by maturity. Loans mature on either the last Friday of the current month or the next month, so you can't use them for long-term financing. If you don't repay the loan before maturity, the lender has a claim on your collateral. You can repay your loan early if you want, but you owe the same amount of interest.

Coinbase hasn't shared available interest rates. A spokesperson for the crypto company disclosed that rates are determined by supply and demand, with borrowers and lenders posting offers on an on-chain order book.

The new fixed-rate loans are another borrowing option on Coinbase, which already offered variable-rate loans. Variable-rate loans allow users to borrow up to $5 million in USDC against their Bitcoin. This type of loan has no set term length, minimum payment requirements, or due dates, making it a much more flexible borrowing option, but you risk your loan rate increasing.

Coinbase's variable-rate loans have an initial loan-to-value (LTV) limit of 75%. If you have $100,000 in Bitcoin, you could borrow up to $75,000. The liquidation threshold is an LTV of 86%. Given Bitcoin's often significant price fluctuations, LTV can change quickly.

If you take out a loan for the full 75% limit against your collateral, Bitcoin only needs to drop about 13% to hit that 86% liquidation threshold. Coinbase hasn't clarified whether fixed-rate loans are subject to the same LTV limit and liquidation threshold.

Being able to borrow against your Bitcoin is convenient. You can get a loan while holding your crypto, similar to how investors with margin accounts can borrow against their stock holdings.

However, the short terms on Coinbase's fixed-rate loans limit what you can do with them. They're really only useful in situations where you need some quick cash, like an emergency expense, and you know you'll be able to repay the loan in full within one to two months. The volatility of the crypto market also makes Bitcoin-backed loans much riskier than loans backed by other types of collateral.

If you borrow against your crypto, keep your LTV ratio low to protect against a sudden margin call.

title: Moody's sounds crypto crash alarm: Why Bitcoin investors should care
summary: A new Moody’s risk matrix ranks a crypto crash among the likeliest economic shocks, just two days before the Fed’s rate decision.
content:
A crypto market crash is now among the most likely economic shocks of the next 12 to 18 months, according to Moody's Analytics.

Chief economist Mark Zandi shared the firm's latest risk matrix on X , just two days before the Federal Reserve announces its Oct, 28 rate decision.

"The Fed won't raise interest rates again when it meets this week, and it shouldn't. The economy is threatened by a growing list of risks, and a Fed misstep is one of them," Zandi wrote in his post.

The matrix ranks 27 potential shocks by how likely they are and how much damage they would do.

A crypto crash sits near the top of the probability scale, though Moody's sees its hit to the wider economy as relatively limited.

Related: Elon Musk has a bold answer to America's $40 trillion debt crisis

It offers no crash probability or price forecast. Still, high borrowing costs weigh on speculative assets, and a deeper stock selloff could add pressure.

Leveraged positions could speed up losses through forced liquidations. "There's a lot of red in the matrix," Zandi wrote, pointing to risks becoming more likely or more severe.

Four bigger threats are worsening: an AI stock selloff, an escalating Iran war, bond market turmoil and Fed policy mistakes.

As per data , the 10-year Treasury yield recently touched 5.31% before easing toward 4.99%. The Fed raised rates in Sept to 3.75%–4%, with inflation still elevated.

"Unless rates recede soon, this will do real damage. Bond investors are already doing the Fed's work for it," Zandi wrote.

Traders agree for now, giving another increase in October just a 10.5% chance, per CME FedWatch report.

For crypto investors , a pause could bring temporary relief, though stubborn inflation and tightening later this year remain threats.

Wednesday's decision is the first real test of that view, and Bitcoin holders will be watching closely.

title: 2 Fed Debates Could Move Bitcoin and Gold Now That a Hold Is Priced In
summary: A Fed hold is priced in. See the 2 debates on rates and Warsh's silence that could move Bitcoin and gold next.
content:
Futures traders give a 90% chance that the Federal Reserve leaves rates unchanged on Wednesday. With the decision priced in, the market's focus has moved to two debates inside the central bank.

One is over where rates go next. The other is over how much officials tell the public about it. Both reach Bitcoin (BTC) and gold (XAU), which pay no interest and lose appeal when borrowing costs are expected to rise.

The Fed raised rates in September to a range of 3.75% to 4%, its first hike since 2023.

The bet on the next hike has now moved to December. Futures put a 75% probability on a hike at the December 8-9 meeting, according to CME FedWatch data.

Officials agree rates must climb but disagree on why, as an energy shock and an AI boom hit the economy, the Journal reported.

The next test of that bet lands on Thursday. September inflation data and third-quarter growth figures both come out at 8:30 a.m. ET.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, in the job since May, refuses to preview future moves.

"We're committed to a discipline, not to a decision," he said.

Investors still read his remarks and the data as pointing to another hike that week, putting the odds near 70%. Then New York Fed President John Williams said there was "no need for urgency." Vice Chair Philip Jefferson echoed him, Reuters reported.

By October 16, the odds of an October hike had dropped to 15%. Bitcoin and gold then split.

Bitcoin climbed from near $76,000 on hike day to above $85,000 on September 30, when cooler inflation data landed. Gold went the other way. December gold futures opened near $4,190 on October 1, down from about $4,340 for spot gold on hike day, Yahoo Finance data showed.

The report tied gold's weakness to rising bond yields and a firmer dollar. The 10-year Treasury yield rose from 5.01% on Sept. 16 to 5.29% on Sept. 30.

Sixteen longer-serving Fed officials made at least 59 public comments between the September meeting and this week's quiet period, a Journal tally found. That roughly matches the 54 from a year earlier.

"It's probably the worst of all possible outcomes. Nobody can force him to talk for the committee. And frankly, he can't force other committee members to shut up," WSJ reported, citing former Fed economist Claudia Sahm.

Bitcoin traded at $80,458 on Tuesday, while spot gold traded for $4,059 an ounce. Meanwhile, the dollar held near a one-week high, whereas the 10-year yield sat at 4.9% on Monday.

BeInCrypto flagged on September 16 that Warsh's press conference could matter more than the decision itself. Brandon Zureick, chief economist at Johnson Investment Counsel, made the same point this week.

Independent analyst Nadim Zidan set out both paths. A hawkish lean, meaning firm signals toward a December hike, would lift yields and the dollar and test Bitcoin's $79,000 support, he wrote. A dovish, softer lean would let gold rebound.

For gold, Ilya Spivak, head of global macro at Tastylive, told Reuters a break below $3,900 could open a slide toward $3,800.

title: Strategy vs. CleanSpark: Which Bitcoin Stock Has Greater Upside Now?
summary: Strategy and CleanSpark offer distinct Bitcoin investment opportunities, but treasury strength, mining pressures and AI ambitions make one stock more appealing.
content:
Bitcoin's reach now extends well beyond cryptocurrency exchanges. Companies owning Bitcoin or supporting its network offer investors different ways to participate in Bitcoin price movements. Strategy MSTR and CleanSpark CLSK share a clear connection to Bitcoin, making both sensitive to changes in the digital asset's value, investor sentiment and access to financing. Their approaches, however, differ. Strategy has made Bitcoin accumulation the center of its financial strategy, using capital markets to build a large corporate treasury while maintaining an enterprise software business. CleanSpark earns revenues by mining new Bitcoin, operating energy-intensive facilities and increasingly developing infrastructure for artificial intelligence workloads. This creates two distinct sources of opportunity and risk. Strategy depends heavily on Bitcoin prices and its ability to manage capital efficiently. CleanSpark must contend with mining costs while converting new data center projects into dependable cash flows. Comparing these paths helps clarify what could drive each stock next.

Strategy offers a relatively direct way to gain corporate exposure to Bitcoin without relying on the economics of running mining facilities. Its holdings reached 848,517 Bitcoin as of Oct. 18, giving the company a scale that CleanSpark's treasury cannot approach. A sustained recovery in Bitcoin could lift the value of this reserve and improve investor confidence in MSTR. Another advantage is Strategy's established access to financing. It can raise funds through common shares and preferred securities, pursue Bitcoin purchases or manage existing obligations. Its expanding digital credit business provides more options than the operating cash flows available to a typical miner. This flexibility matters when market conditions change quickly. The company has also worked to protect liquidity. Its dollar reserve stood at about $4.83 billion, supporting preferred dividends and debt interest. Strategy repurchased $193 million of STRC shares and expanded its digital credit repurchase authorization to $3 billion, demonstrating active management of financing costs and obligations. Still, these strengths come with risks. Issuing common shares can dilute investors, while preferred dividends create recurring commitments. Strategy's second quarter included a large noncash Bitcoin valuation loss, showing how sharply reported earnings can swing. Its software operations offer diversification but remain secondary to the treasury strategy. Compared with CleanSpark, Strategy avoids direct exposure to mining equipment replacement, electricity costs and construction schedules. Its future remains closely tied to Bitcoin, yet its treasury scale and financing flexibility provide a stronger foundation for investors willing to accept substantial volatility and prolonged drawdowns.

CleanSpark has built a Bitcoin mining network, but scale may not translate into stronger shareholder returns. In September, CleanSpark reported 50 exahashes per second of operational capacity and produced 529 Bitcoin. Mining remains sensitive to electricity prices, network difficulty and equipment efficiency, factors Strategy avoids through its treasury-focused model. That pressure is visible. CleanSpark's fiscal third-quarter revenues declined 30.5% year over year, while its gross margin slipped sequentially. A large net loss reflected Bitcoin valuation changes as well as the difficult backdrop. Larger fleets alone may not offset weaker mining economics. Its shift toward artificial intelligence infrastructure offers an alternative. Its Sandersville project has a 20-year lease representing about $6.6 billion in contracted revenues. CleanSpark also closed $2.276 billion of secured notes carrying a 7.875% rate, which management says fully funds construction. These are meaningful achievements, but contracted revenues are not immediate cash flow. Initial delivery is expected in late 2027. Expansion in Texas adds another layer of uncertainty. It has an exclusivity arrangement covering up to 885 megawatts, not a signed long-term lease for those sites. Conditional grid classifications represent progress, but final development, customer commitments and project execution still matter. Financing costs could weigh on returns if schedules slip. CleanSpark ended September with 13,530 Bitcoin, including holdings committed to collateral arrangements. Unlike Strategy, it must keep investing in physical capacity while navigating a changing business model. Until new infrastructure delivers recurring income and mining profitability improves, its apparent growth opportunities carry considerable execution risk.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MSTR's 2026 and 2027 sales calls for year-over-year growth of 5.51% and 1.70%, respectively. Over the past 30 days, earnings estimates for 2026 have improved, while those for 2027 have declined. For MSTR:

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CLSK's fiscal 2026 and 2027 sales implies a year-over-year decline of 23.77% and growth of just 0.80%, respectively. The consensus mark for CLSK's fiscal 2026 and 2027 earnings has been revised southward in the past 30 days. For CLSK:

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Over the past three months, MSTR shares have surged 45.4%, while CLSK shares have plunged 42.4%. In comparison, the S&P 500 composite has advanced 2.9% in the same time frame.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Valuation-wise, none of the stocks look attractive. Both MSTR and CLSK have a Value Score of F.

Both stocks could rebound sharply if Bitcoin strengthens, and neither offers a defensive investment profile. However, their paths to improved shareholder returns look different. Strategy already controls a much larger Bitcoin reserve and can use established capital market channels to manage its holdings. The risks of dilution and preferred dividends deserve attention, especially during extended downturns. CleanSpark has a genuine opportunity in data centers, but its mining pressures and long construction schedule leave more results to prove. For investors deciding where to maintain Bitcoin-related equity exposure, MSTR looks more defensible while reducing exposure to CLSK appears prudent for now. title: Money 20/20 USA: Fireblocks CFO Michael Levine on why banks are moving onchain
summary: When the internet first took off, people asked what you could possibly do with an email address. Michael Levine, CFO of Fireblocks, believes blockchain is at that same early stage today. Levine sits down with JD Durkin at Money 20/20 USA in Las Vegas to explain how Fireblocks, the digital asset infrastructure platform used by asset managers, hedge funds, payments companies and some of the world’s biggest banks, is seeing banks and payments companies now drive more transaction volume than crypto trading firms. He shares how the passage of the GENIUS Act opened the door for banks to explore tokenized deposits and tokenized real world assets, and why, borrowing from Wayne Gretzky, everyone knows where the puck is going, even if institutions are skating there at different speeds. Levine also explains why many of his CFO peers still confuse stablecoins with Bitcoin, and why he expects tokenized stocks to become so common that most people won’t even realize they own them.
content:
When the internet first took off, people asked what you could possibly do with an email address. Michael Levine, CFO of Fireblocks, believes blockchain is at that same early stage today. Levine sits down with JD Durkin at Money 20/20 USA in Las Vegas to explain how Fireblocks, the digital asset infrastructure platform used by asset managers, hedge funds, payments companies and some of the world's biggest banks, is seeing banks and payments companies now drive more transaction volume than crypto trading firms. He shares how the passage of the GENIUS Act opened the door for banks to explore tokenized deposits and tokenized real world assets, and why, borrowing from Wayne Gretzky, everyone knows where the puck is going, even if institutions are skating there at different speeds. Levine also explains why many of his CFO peers still confuse stablecoins with Bitcoin, and why he expects tokenized stocks to become so common that most people won't even realize they own them.

Michael Lavine is the CFO at Fireblocks. He is generous enough to take time out of his busy schedule to sit down with us here at Money 2020. Really grateful for a few minutes of your time, Michael. Good to see you.

Thank you. Excited to be here.

Let's start foremost with a bit of an introduction to Fireblocks, as if anyone watching doesn't know, and walk me through a few of your top priorities here this year.

Sure. So, uh, Fireblocks is uh a infrastructure company for blockchain.

Uh, we've been around since uh, 2018. Uh and uh have established ourselves as an important part of the ecosystem.

Uh, we provide, we're a software provider at the end of the day and our software is a platform that allows our customers to manage their digital assets and our customers range from uh asset managers, hedge funds, to payments companies and some of the biggest banks in the world.

How has your underlying business had to continue to evolve as more banks enter the crypto ecosystem?

I I think it's reflective of the whole market. So, what's happening now is that we're seeing and really I think uh, I would say it really started to change when the Genius Act was passed and a lot of the pressure came off of the banks to stay away from uh digital assets. And banks, and I think one of the exciting things about the space was recognizing that blockchain technology

really gave uh a new set of uh utilities to financial institutions that uh they never had before. And I think once the um uh, maybe the correct term to say is, you know, the uh, shackles were released uh so to speak that uh there weren't penalties or or heavy uh regulatory pressure not to not to be involved in digital assets, uh that banks started to realize that there were opportunities uh in tokenization, tokenized deposits, uh um tokenization of real world assets, uh being able to support more of their uh customer base, uh that really pe- people and institutions started to realize that there were more opportunities to leverage uh what was available on digital assets. And so, we being an infrastructure partner, uh were a natural um go-to for them to figure out how do they expand into digital assets. And so today, banks, payments companies are a growing part of our business. But I think that represents what's happening in the industry. People are realizing when they think about the evolution of crypto, they think of trading one asset for another, one token for another, the speculation aspect. And I think that was part of the uh original um growth of the industry. But now you're really seeing the technology expand to many more use cases. And so, we're seeing what we call traditional finance or TradFi as we refer to it, really starting to expand uh and come in in a very big way.

You mentioned the passage of the Genius Act. Yeah. The Clarity Act, however, did not pass Congress earlier this year. To be fair, it is a midterm year election, so we know getting bills passed would would be difficult. Does that change the regulatory calculus at all for your underlying business?

You know, if Clarity passed, it would have been a benefit for sure. It doesn't necessarily, you know, if you kind of think in sort of the way we always talk of being like Wayne Gretzky, being Gretzky-esque, of, you know, go to where the puck is going to be, not where it is now. I would say that everybody has a good idea of where the puck is going. The question is what is the speed of the puck? So, if you're skating to where the puck is going, you could be sort of in the middle of the ice or down at the end of the ice. And I think that's still the question. But where the puck is going is undubtable that blockchain is becoming a core part of most financial institutions' infrastructure. And they're moving at different speeds. So, some are at the one part of the ice, the rink, and then others are starting to move towards the middle and some are even moving further down towards the end.

Banks and payment companies are now accounting for more transaction volume on fire blocks than even crypto trading firms. Yeah. What does that mean?

It's it's exactly what I was saying in the sense that you're really starting to see utility. So in payments companies as an example, we're starting to see PSPs or uh you know, brand name, uh global remittance companies starting to uh communicate to their customer base the value of moving stable coins, both in terms of speed, uh cost, uh and efficiency. And so we're seeing the volumes really go up tremendously. But a lot of it is just even the derivative knowledge base of everybody out consumers and so forth, and we haven't even scratched the surface. So I think as more um more consumers, more institutions around the world really start learning the advantages and you know, the simple case is stable coins. It's a common term, uh a lot of people are speaking about it, but I know a lot of the CFO peers that I have, when I speak to them outside of the industry, they still have a very low understanding of even stable coins. And they'll come to me and they'll say, I know it's happening, I know I have to get up to speed,

but how risky is it? I don't know, they they conflate it with Bitcoin and other digital currencies that have prices that move. title: Investor Who Called the AI Boom Predicts a Bitcoin Crash
summary: Jason Calacanis says dump Bitcoin before a fall to $57,000. Here is how BTC has fared against AI stocks since his 2023 call.
content:
Three years ago, Jason Calacanis told crypto founders to abandon their industry for AI stocks. Now, the prominent Silicon Valley investor has another warning: sell Bitcoin before it crashes again.

Calacanis predicted on Tuesday that Bitcoin would fall to $57,000 within 12 months, nearly 29% below its $79,774 price at the time.

He went further, claiming Bitcoin would never reach another all-time high.

"A brutal year for Bitcoin is just getting started," he wrote.

Calacanis has a reputation for spotting technology trends early. He backed Uber and Robinhood before they became household names and co-hosts the influential All-In podcast.

His June 2023 advice to "pivot to AI" proved well-timed.

An investment of $10,000 in Nvidia that day would now be worth approximately $56,100. Bitcoin would have returned around $30,100.

Yet his record deserves context. Semiconductor stocks broadly performed similarly to Bitcoin over that period. Calacanis also recommended buying Bitcoin directly in September 2025.

Calacanis believes Bitcoin is losing investor interest while AI offers greater economic value.

"Just sell and shift from Bitcoin to Super Intelligence," he argued, describing Bitcoin as a "dead network."

There are reasons for concern. Bitcoin has fallen roughly 37% from its October 2025 peak near $126,200.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs also lost approximately $773 million on October 22–23.

Glassnode estimates that these funds purchased their holdings at an average price near $81,500, leaving them under pressure at current levels.

However, ETF inflows recovered by approximately $110 million on October 26. The data has yet to establish sustained institutional selling.

The performance gap is striking. Over the past year, semiconductor stocks gained roughly 62% while Bitcoin lost 30%.

Yet Bitcoin remains positively correlated with technology stocks. Its 90-day correlation with the Nasdaq stood at 0.38 through October 25, suggesting both can fall when investors retreat from risk.

Even Calacanis's own AI-linked cryptocurrency investment, Bittensor (TAO), has fallen approximately 40% over the past year.

Meanwhile, Galaxy Digital's Alex Thorn believes Bitcoin bottomed in June and could recover toward $125,000 as long-term selling eases.

His bullish outlook would weaken if Bitcoin stayed below roughly $76,540. That makes the coming weeks critical for judging whether Calacanis's crash prediction has substance.

title: McDonald's McRib Doesn't Actually Boost Bitcoin's Price, Sorry Everyone
summary: Crypto traders think the McRib’s return to McDonald's means a Bitcoin pump is coming. Experts say there is "no correlation at all."
content:
The McDonald's McRib has become a crypto meme in recent years, due to many traders believing that its reintroduction to the menu precedes a boost in Bitcoin's price. And, with the tangy pork sandwich back in certain states across the U.S., crypto traders are getting excited.

But experts have taken the McRib theory off the menu, saying that those parroting the theory are forgetting all of the times that the McRib hasn't coincided with a Bitcoin price increase.

"There is no correlation at all," Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, told Decrypt . "Whilst it is a fun exercise, it seems to be that people omit McRib returns when it doesn't fit the narrative."

Nolan shared a chart tracking the McRib's return compared to Bitcoin's weekly close, and only three out of 10 McRib returns posted clear positive Bitcoin returns. In fact, it often comes before major drops in valuation.

Carlos Guzman, vice president of research at crypto trading firm GSR, told Decrypt that there is "no causal mechanism" and that any price increases following the McRib's reintroduction is just a "funny coincidence."

"Let's say, hypothetically, it did indicate the start of a bull run, it would be quite nonsensical, similar to when people overlaid the Dune movie releases," Nolan said. "So yes, it's fun, generates some excitement, but even in the best case, purely coincidental."

Guzman agreed, adding that the crypto community likely just clings to the theory as it's "silly," "obviously absurd," and because people find it funny.

This year's McRib return comes as Bitcoin sits in what André Dragosch, head of research at Bitwise Europe, called " wait and see mode ," with traders waiting for the Federal Reserve's next moves before making big bets.

Bitcoin in 'Wait and See Mode'—And That Might Be a Good Thing

Bitcoin has seen fairly limited activity over the past month, according to Decrypt data, dropping just 6% as it sits at $79,750.

The Fed raised rates in September for the first time since 2023 , and CPI then rose 0.6% for the month. Its next rate decision is on Wednesday.

That decision is one of three catalysts coming in the next two weeks, Jake Koch-Gallup, senior research analyst at Blockworks, told Decrypt . The other two are an options expiry of $11.69 billion worth of Bitcoin on October 30 and the U.S. midterms on November 3.

"If the Fed keeps rates the same and ETF inflows keep coming, I'd expect the break to be upward," Koch-Gallup told Decrypt last week. "If the Fed hikes again, the $75,000 to $77,000 floor comes back into play."

So if the Fed gives the market what it wants, then Bitcoin's price could actually jump over the coming days… just as the McRib returns to McDonald's stores. Coincidence? Experts think so.

title: Altcoin Fever Has Cooled. Watch What Breaks the Silence
summary: Altcoin spot trading has cooled to its long-run median as Bitcoin dominance holds at 60.49%, between two key levels.
content:
Altcoin trading has cooled back to normal levels. Total crypto spot volume now runs at about 3 times Bitcoin's (BTC), down from nearly 4 times in late September.

The speculation has cooled, although the market has not yet tilted toward Bitcoin or altcoins. That leaves Ethereum (ETH) and altcoin holders without a clear signal. Bitcoin dominance sits at 60.49% on October 27, between the levels one analyst ties to Bitcoin leadership and altcoin rotation.

Glassnode lead analyst AntiFragile compares total spot volume with Bitcoin's own spot volume over 7 days. A higher ratio means more trading activity in altcoins relative to Bitcoin.

The ratio ran near 4 in late September, when Blockchaincenter's Altcoin Season Index climbed to about 63. It has since slipped to about 3, its median since 2022.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

A median reading points to ordinary trading activity. Breadth weakened as well. By October 18, 48.4% of Binance-listed altcoins sat below their 200-day average, up from under 10% earlier that month.

Whether that calmer market draws fresh altcoin buying depends on Bitcoin dominance. The metric tracks Bitcoin's share of total crypto market value.

Dominance reads 60.49% on October 27, after touching 60.91% on October 18. That October peak was the highest level since mid-May.

The last turn lower from this zone favored altcoins. Dominance fell to about 58% between mid-May and early June. Over the same weeks, the Altcoin Season Index rose from about 25 to about 50.

Ash Crypto frames the setup with two levels. A break above 61.5% would keep Bitcoin in the lead and altcoins weak. A drop below 58% would start rotation into Ethereum (ETH) and altcoins, he said.

"ETH has done well these last 4 months, but that only continues if dominance starts falling from 61%," the analyst added.

Meanwhile, the Altcoin Season Index reads a neutral 51, midway between the Bitcoin season (25) and altcoin season (75) thresholds.

One factor could slow any rotation. Exchange reserves of ERC-20 stablecoins stood at $55.97 billion on October 26. That compares with almost $78 billion in November 2025.

Traders usually fund crypto buys with stablecoins already on exchanges, so a smaller pile leaves less ready cash to deploy.

Dominance now sits about 1 point below the upper line and 2.5 points above the lower one. A move toward either will show whether the calmer altcoin market draws new buyers.

title: Jason Calacanis Predicts a ‘Brutal Year’ for Bitcoin, Urges Holders to Shift to AI
summary: The early Uber investor predicted more ETF outflows and a retest of a “57k low” within a year.
content:
Jason Calacanis , the early Uber investor and All-In podcast co-host, urged his followers to sell their bitcoin and put the money into artificial intelligence instead, posting on X early Tuesday that "a brutal year for Bitcoin is just getting started."

Calacanis made three predictions in the post. He said outflows from bitcoin exchange-traded funds "will continue," that the price will "test the 57k low again in the next 12 months," and that "Bitcoin will never break its all-time high again."

"Just sell and shift from Bitcoin to Super Intelligence because one provides little to no value, and the other provides unlimited upside for humanity," he wrote.

Calacanis argued that investors now have "far too many dynamic places to put your money that are creating MUCH more value," and described bitcoin as a network "that offers nothing beyond a store of value." He added that "no one is trying to convince people to buy Bitcoin anymore," and that the memes and NFTs that once drove interest had faded.

Calacanis also said he is long Bittensor , a decentralized network for AI models whose token trades as TAO. He wrote that he loves "bittensor's focus on scaling AI" in a reply to his own post 22 minutes later.

Bitcoin traded at about $79,787 on Tuesday morning, according to CoinGecko's price page , roughly 37% below its all-time high of $126,080 , set on Oct. 6, 2025.

CoinGecko's daily price data puts bitcoin's lowest reading of the past year at about $58,566 , on July 1, 2026. Intraday prices can dip below those daily figures.

Fund flows this month have been mixed. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of about $202.1 million in October through Oct. 26, according to SoSoValue data , across 10 days of inflows and eight days of outflows. Outflows of about $635.5 million on Oct. 22 came one day after the funds took in about $528.4 million.

Calacanis has a long history of being skeptical of Bitcoin. In August, he asked on X whether bitcoin would ever reach $1 million, or even $250,000, and said he believed Strategy co-founder Michael Saylor "broke the game of bitcoin by trying to corner the market." In September, he compared bitcoin's move near $81,000 to a dead cat bounce, a post that drew responses from Saylor and ARK Invest CEO Cathie Wood . In 2018, Calacanis said there was a 60% to 70% chance Bitcoin went to zero. It was trading around $3,700 at the time.

title: Bitcoin Mining Firm Luxor Raises $16 Million to Scale Its AI Compute Push
summary: The CMT Digital-led round, which drew mining-hardware makers Canaan and MicroBT, will fund Luxor’s expansion into AI compute trading, hardware and derivatives.
content:
Luxor Technology, a company that built its business around Bitcoin mining, has raised $16 million to expand into the fast-growing market for AI computing power, the latest sign of crypto infrastructure firms pivoting toward artificial intelligence.

The Seattle-based company said the strategic round was led by CMT Digital, the venture arm of Chicago's CMT Group, with participation from mining-hardware makers Canaan and MicroBT, as well as Halo, Steelhead, and angel investors.

The round combined primary and secondary capital, and Luxor framed each backer as an operating partner already embedded in the compute supply chain it serves, across hardware, capital, and power.

The raise follows the September launch of Luxor AI, a segment that extends the energy, hardware, software and trading stack Luxor built for Bitcoin mining into the AI and high-performance computing market. The company brings a sizable operating history to the effort: its hardware desk has traded $1 billion of mining ASICs, its energy arm services more than 75 megawatts of load across two U.S. grid regions, and its cloud platform had processed 1.8 million workloads so far this year as of September.

Luxor said it will use the funds to scale that cloud platform, provide working capital for its AI hardware business, grow its compute-derivatives trading, and make engineering and go-to-market hires.

A notable piece is its over-the-counter desk, which already offers cash-settled options, forwards and backstops on compute-rental indexes, turning AI computing power into something that can be priced and hedged like a financial instrument.

"Compute markets are converging: the same miners, power sites and capital that served digital mining are now powering AI," said Nick Hansen, Luxor's CEO and co-founder.

Bitcoin Miner Ditches Site for AI Deal That Could Top $1.2 Billion

The move fits a broader Bitcoin mining industry stampede towards AI .

Bitcoin miners have increasingly repurposed their power and infrastructure for AI, with some signing billion-dollar hyperscaler deals and others selling Bitcoin to fund the shift. Analysts at VanEck and Bernstein have cast miners as unlikely power brokers in the AI race, given their rare access to the electricity and sites that data centers need.

title: Strategy Buys $0 Bitcoin, Repurchases $205M in STRC as Saylor Reveals $5.1B Cash Holdings
summary: Michael Saylor said Strategy repurchased $205 million of its STRC preferred stock while purchasing no additional Bitcoin during the reporting week. As of Oct. 25…
content:
Key Takeaways

Michael Saylor said Strategy repurchased $205 million of its STRC preferred stock while purchasing no additional Bitcoin during the reporting week.

As of Oct. 25, Strategy held 848,517 BTC alongside approximately $5.1 billion in USD assets.

The repurchase highlights Strategy's growing focus on managing preferred-stock obligations alongside its long-term Bitcoin accumulation strategy.

Strategy, the Bitcoin treasury company led by executive chairman Michael Saylor, has shifted attention from Bitcoin accumulation to preferred-share repurchases after spending approximately $205 million on its STRC stock.

In an Oct. 26 post on X, Saylor disclosed that the company had repurchased $205 million of STRC, its variable-rate perpetual preferred stock.

He also reported holdings of 848,517 Bitcoin and approximately $5.1 billion in USD assets as of Oct. 25.

The announcement comes as Strategy manages an increasingly complex capital structure involving Bitcoin holdings, preferred-stock financing, and cash reserves.

Unlike buying Bitcoin , repurchasing preferred shares does not increase Strategy's cryptocurrency holdings. Instead, it reduces outstanding preferred equity and potentially lowers future dividend obligations.

Strategy's Oct. 26 regulatory disclosure confirms that the company purchased zero Bitcoin between Oct. 19 and Oct. 25.

The company also reported no Bitcoin sales and did not issue additional shares through its at-the-market offering program during the reporting period.

Instead, Strategy repurchased 2,068,459 STRC shares for approximately $204.9 million, paying an average of $99.06 per share. That represents a slight discount to STRC's $100 stated value.

The latest transaction followed a $193.1 million STRC repurchase the previous week, when Strategy also acquired 267 BTC for approximately $22.1 million.

Across those two weeks, Strategy spent approximately $398 million repurchasing STRC , compared with just $22.1 million purchasing Bitcoin. That means preferred-share repurchases accounted for roughly 95% of the combined spending on those two activities.

STRC, also known as Stretch, is Strategy's variable-rate perpetual preferred stock . Its dividend rate is adjusted monthly to encourage trading near its $100 stated value.

According to Strategy's published product information, STRC pays a 12% annual dividend in cash.

At that rate, retiring approximately $205 million of preferred shares could reduce annualized dividend obligations by roughly $24.8 million, assuming the dividend rate remains unchanged.

However, because STRC's dividend rate is variable, the actual savings will depend on future rate adjustments.

The transactions suggest Strategy is paying closer attention to the costs associated with its preferred-stock financing, even as Bitcoin remains central to its treasury strategy.

Although Saylor disclosed approximately $5.1 billion in USD assets, that figure does not represent unrestricted cash available entirely for Bitcoin purchases.

According to Strategy's filing, the company held approximately $4.83 billion in its USD Reserve and another $242.4 million in USD Cash as of Oct. 25.

Together, those holdings total approximately $5.07 billion, rounded to $5.1 billion in Saylor's announcement.

The difference between the two categories is important. Strategy's USD Reserve is primarily intended to support preferred-stock dividend payments and interest obligations on outstanding debt.

USD Cash, meanwhile, provides greater flexibility for Bitcoin acquisitions, reserve expansion, and other capital management activities.

Strategy funded the entire $204.9 million STRC repurchase using USD Cash, leaving approximately $242.4 million available in that category. This means that while the company holds billions of dollars in USD-denominated assets, much of that liquidity has been earmarked to meet its financial obligations rather than for immediate Bitcoin accumulation .

The repurchase is also part of a broader capital management program.

Strategy recently expanded its preferred-stock repurchase authorization from $2 billion to $3 billion. As of Oct. 25, approximately $956.8 million remained available under that authorization.

Separately, the company retained a $1 billion authorization to repurchase its MSTR common shares.

These programs give Strategy additional flexibility to manage its capital structure, particularly when market conditions make repurchasing securities more attractive than issuing new ones.

Despite making no new Bitcoin purchases during the reporting week, Strategy remains one of the largest corporate holders of the cryptocurrency.

As of Oct. 25, the company held 848,517 BTC, acquired for approximately $64.02 billion, including fees and expenses. Its average acquisition cost stands at $75,446 per Bitcoin.

The absence of new purchases means Strategy's total Bitcoin holdings remained unchanged during the week, but it does not necessarily signal a permanent change in its accumulation strategy.

Instead, the latest filing illustrates how the company's financial priorities have expanded beyond simply purchasing more Bitcoin.

Strategy has increasingly positioned itself as a digital credit company, using preferred securities to raise capital while maintaining substantial exposure to Bitcoin.

This approach introduces additional financial considerations.

Unlike Bitcoin, which does not generate contractual cash flows for Strategy , preferred shares can carry recurring dividend obligations. Maintaining sufficient liquidity to meet those commitments becomes particularly important during periods of cryptocurrency market volatility.

Repurchasing STRC can reduce outstanding preferred equity and associated dividend obligations, while purchasing additional Bitcoin increases the company's exposure to future price movements.

The two activities therefore serve different financial purposes. Strategy's recent transactions show that management is willing to deploy substantial capital toward its preferred securities even when Bitcoin purchases pause.

However, the company has not explicitly explained why it prioritized STRC repurchases over new BTC acquisitions during the latest reporting week.

For investors, the key question is whether this represents a temporary pause in Bitcoin accumulation or a more sustained shift toward managing the cost of Strategy's expanding preferred-stock structure.

With 848,517 BTC on its balance sheet, approximately $5.1 billion in USD assets, and nearly $1 billion remaining under its preferred-stock repurchase authorization, Strategy has several options for deploying capital.

Its next disclosures will provide a clearer indication of whether Bitcoin purchases resume or preferred-share repurchases continue to dominate its near-term capital allocation.

title: Tom Lee Sees ‘One of the Biggest Rallies of Our Lifetime’ as $10.8B Bitcoin Options Expiry Looms
summary: Tom Lee’s bullish market outlook faces a near-term test as roughly $10.8 billion in Deribit Bitcoin options approach expiry. BlackRock’s IBIT attracted $110.3 million on…
content:
Key Takeaways

Tom Lee's bullish market outlook faces a near-term test as roughly $10.8 billion in Deribit Bitcoin options approach expiry.

BlackRock's IBIT attracted $110.3 million on Monday, following two sessions of substantial Bitcoin ETF withdrawals.

The recent comments have put Lee's past $250,000 Bitcoin target in focus.

Tom Lee's prediction of "one of the biggest rallies of our lifetime" faces a fresh test as Bitcoin approaches Friday's multibillion-dollar options expiry, with the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision coming first.

The Fundstrat co-founder recently spoke bullishly about stocks and said that a major crypto bull cycle is underway, prompting some bulls to revive Lee's long-term price call that Bitcoin could reach $250,000.

Speaking in a recent CNBC appearance, Lee said he sees the stock market igniting into the biggest rally seen in decades.

He described a potential advance beginning in the fourth quarter and extending into 2027.

It comes just weeks after the bullish executive said the "crypto bull market is underway" in Bitmine's Oct. 7 chairman's message.

He added that the "cycle is likely to be the largest."

Lee pointed to institutional participation, Bitcoin's earlier move above its 200-day moving average, and the expansion of blockchain-based finance as reasons for his optimism.

Lee reaffirmed his $250,000 Bitcoin target in a January appearance on The Master Investor Podcast, linking his optimism to broader adoption and the growing use of blockchain in finance.

Host Wilfred Frost asked: "And your price target for Bitcoin this year is 250,000?"

"Yeah. So we think Bitcoin will make a new high this year," Lee replied.

Asked what would drive that advance, Lee pointed to "the usefulness of crypto increasing," arguing that banks increasingly recognize the benefits of blockchain-based settlement.

His bullish outlook also rested on the belief that Bitcoin has room to attract a much wider investor base.

"Bitcoin is digital gold, but the universe of people that believe that thesis is not the same universe that owns gold," he said.

However, Lee cautioned that adoption would not translate into a smooth price trajectory.

"But the path to getting that adoption rate higher is going to be very jagged," he said.

"And I think 2026 will be a really important test because if Bitcoin makes a new all-time high, we know that that deleveraging event is behind us."

Around $10.79 billion worth of Bitcoin options on Deribit are due to expire on Friday, Oct. 30, according to PerpFinder's Oct. 27 data.

That includes $6.96 billion in call options, which can benefit from rising prices, and $3.83 billion in put options, which can protect against falls.

As the deadline approaches, traders may close or replace their positions, potentially adding to price swings. However, a large expiry does not guarantee that Bitcoin will rise or fall.

First comes Wednesday's Federal Reserve interest-rate decision, which could influence investors' appetite for Bitcoin ahead of Friday's expiry.

At the same time, Farside Investors recorded $110.3 million in net inflows into BlackRock's IBIT on Monday, Oct. 26, accounting for the entire positive total shown across the US spot Bitcoin ETF group that day.

That followed net withdrawals of $635.6 million on Oct. 22 and $137.9 million on Oct. 23 — a combined $773.5 million.

Monday's inflow replaced approximately 14% of those withdrawals, leaving the three-session balance at a net outflow of $663.2 million.

Using a starting price of $80,000, Bitcoin would need to gain 212.5% to reach $250,000 — more than tripling in value.

At that price, Bitcoin's maximum supply of 21 million coins would imply a fully diluted valuation of $5.25 trillion.

The timeframe makes Lee's forecast particularly ambitious.

With just over two months remaining in 2026, Bitcoin would need to add $170,000 per coin to reach its target before year-end.

A move at this scale would likely require an exceptional surge in buying, massive demand, and a sharp improvement in market sentiment.

A favorable Fed decision or a few positive ETF sessions could help support a recovery, but would not offer enough evidence that a rally of that scale was underway.

While reaching $250,000 is not mathematically impossible, the required growth in size and speed makes it a highly speculative end-of-year outcome.

title: Why This Team of Ninjas Is Tripling Down on Mining Bitcoin
summary: NIP Group says Bitcoin mining has “earned its place” as the esports giant swaps 247 million shares for more machines.
content:
Ninjas in Pyjamas Group, the company behind the legendary esports team, has acquired a third batch of Bitcoin miners in exchange for over 247 million Class A ordinary shares.

Hicham Chahine, the founder and CEO of NIP Group, told Decrypt that he wants to bet on Bitcoin mining while the market is "cooling," rather than when it's hot and competition is higher. He added that the facilities could be used for artificial intelligence in the future.

"Now that this tranche is closed, we're at roughly 13.85 EH/s. That puts us among the largest publicly listed miners in the world, roughly 195 Bitcoin a month," Chahine said. "That's real revenue, and it supports everything else we're building. This year we reviewed every single piece of NIP Group, not just mining. We made decisions with one goal: better margins and a clear path to profitability. Mining had to earn its place in that review, and it did."

Why Prediction Markets Got the Brazilian Election So Wrong

It comes after the esports team expanded its Bitcoin operation last year as it looked to mine 160 Bitcoin a month. This most recent acquisition brings that target up by 35 Bitcoin to 195 Bitcoin a month, or $2.8 million at today's prices.

Chahine told Decrypt that NIP Group is "optimistic about where this is heading," adding that the third batch of Bitcoin miners will require "minimal ramp time."

NIP Group is a digital entertainment company known for esports and gaming ventures. It owns Ninjas in Pyjamas, which fields professional esports teams in games like Counter-Strike 2, Valorant, League of Legends, and Rocket League.

The firm's stock, NIPG, has dropped 40.7% from $6.74 to $4 since the Bitcoin announcement last week, according to Yahoo Finance data. This marks an all-time low for the stock. Bitcoin has dropped 2% to $79,820 over the same period of time, per Decrypt data.

Game Publishers Have Pushed to Cut Discs Since 2007, Infinity Ward Veteran Says

Chahine explained that the purchased facilities could shift to focus on artificial intelligence infrastructure if the market demands.

"We look at what AI and [high-performance computing] customers will actually pay, how long they'll commit and whether that demand is sustained or temporary," Chahine told Decrypt . "When those workloads clearly beat mining on returns, consistently and not just for a week or two, that's when we may move capacity. If the numbers say shift, we shift."

Bitcoin in 'Wait and See Mode'—And That Might Be a Good Thing

Of course, any sort of future pivot would require notable legwork, as Bitcoin miners can't simply be turned into AI data centers at the flick of a switch. But, Chahine said, the infrastructure around the mining facilities is a good foundation for what AI and high-performance computing need.

"When we talk about AI, we mean using that footprint and that know-how for compute-heavy work when the economics make sense," he said. "We're a gaming and entertainment company at heart, and our fans already live on compute, bringing infrastructure and entertainment under one roof makes sense."

China's AI bubble has burst: the STAR50 index of Chinese AI and chip leaders has lost about 40% in under four months, erasing roughly $480 billion. Reuters' analysis showed on Monday, October 26, how stretched valuations and Western equipment bans broke the rally. The selling didn't stop there. On Tuesday, Cambricon, China's answer to Nvidia, fell another 5.7%.

The damage has spread across Asia, and U.S. chip stocks are already 24% below their June high. So is America's AI trade next, and what would that mean for Bitcoin and AI crypto tokens?

A rally that ran far ahead of earnings. At its peak, the STAR50 traded near 250 times trailing earnings; even after the crash, it sits around 100 times, against roughly 30 for the Nasdaq 100.

The individual names tell the story. Robot maker Unitree, whose IPO retail buyers oversubscribed 8,000 times, has halved since its August debut. GPU makers MetaX and Moore Threads have each roughly halved since July. Optical suppliers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink are down about 60% from their summer highs as Washington moves to bar them from U.S. data centers. Cambricon is down 42.8% from its June 30 close and SMIC 49.3%.

There was no single trigger. Traders pointed to valuations, tax bills and the equipment bans, while state-backed investors sold into rallies as regulators cracked down on leverage and high-frequency trading. With AI stocks making up 42% of China's market value and 57% of its turnover, by Goldman Sachs' count, the slide pulled the CSI 300 about 20% below its June high.

Korea took the hit too. SK Hynix, the memory maker at the heart of the AI chip trade, is down 49.4% since June 30, and the KOSPI is down 33.5%.

The broad market has held up far better. The Nasdaq Composite is only 5.2% below its record, and Nasdaq 100 futures were up 0.1% on Tuesday morning. The valuation gap is the main buffer: U.S. AI leaders trade at about a third of the STAR50's multiple and, unlike most of China's chip names, earn large profits.

Traders aren't pricing a U.S. crash. A Polymarket contract on whether the AI bubble bursts gives 9.4% for 2026 and 22.5% by June 30, 2027. The next tests come fast: the Fed decides on Wednesday, and Anthropic's IPO will soon ask investors for billions more for AI.

So far, very little. Since June 30, when Cambricon and SMIC peaked, Bitcoin has gained 35.7%, Bittensor's TAO 21.9%, and Render 9.7%, while the Artificial Superintelligence Alliance's FET is flat. Bitcoin's 2026 low came on July 1, so the window flatters it, but the direction is clear.

Over the past 90 days, the daily moves of Bitcoin and TAO have shown almost no link to Cambricon's, with correlations of −0.06 and −0.08. China's domestic AI crash has stayed in China.

A U.S. sell-off would be different. Bitcoin's daily moves have tracked the Nasdaq 100 more closely, with a correlation of 0.37, and AI tokens follow Bitcoin first: TAO's correlation with Bitcoin is 0.71, against 0.36 with U.S. chip stocks. When the market turns, AI tokens fall harder.

title: VivoPower advances Norway AI data center as analyst sees valuation upside
summary: VivoPower PLC (NASDAQ:VIVO, FRA:51J) is moving ahead with its planned AI data center in Norway while pursuing a broader expansion into sovereign AI infrastructure, with Noble Capital Markets pointing to significant valuation upside as the company advances its development pipeline. On October...
content:
VivoPower PLC ( NASDAQ:VIVO , FRA:51J ) is moving ahead with its planned AI data center in Norway while pursuing a broader expansion into sovereign AI infrastructure, with Noble Capital Markets pointing to significant valuation upside as the company advances its development pipeline.

On October 12, VivoPower announced that construction had begun at the initial 40-megawatt (MW) AI data center at its Mo i Rana facility. The company has selected a global AI industry leader as its preferred tenant, although a definitive lease agreement has yet to be announced.

The facility is being designed to meet the prospective customer's requirements, with local contractors handling site preparation and structural work ahead of specialized mechanical and electrical installation.

Construction is taking place on adjacent land, allowing existing Bitcoin mining and grid-balancing operations to continue. When the current mining lease expires in June 2027, VivoPower plans to redirect the existing power capacity towards AI applications and develop an additional 40MW of capacity.

VivoPower is also expanding its commercial reach through a partnership with Open Innovation AI announced on October 21.

The agreement will see the companies jointly pursue sovereign AI data center developments, targeting 1 gigawatt (GW) of capacity over the next three years across the Nordics, mainland Europe, the Gulf Cooperation Council and selected Asian markets.

Open Innovation AI provides hardware-agnostic technology for AI infrastructure orchestration, operations and security. The partnership is intended to help VivoPower pursue governments and enterprises seeking secure AI infrastructure under local control.

"We believe the collaboration strengthens VivoPower's ability to attract governments and enterprises seeking locally controlled, secure AI infrastructure," analysts at Noble Capital Markets wrote.

Analysts noted that the 1GW target is not contracted capacity, and each project will require separate agreements.

Noble rates VivoPower as Outperform, with a $10 price target based on its expectations for earnings growth from the company's AI infrastructure strategy.

The broker estimates that VivoPower trades at 0.7 times its calendar 2028 enterprise value-to-EBITDA estimate of $121 million, compared with an average of 7.8 times for industry peers.

Its price target uses a 5.5-times multiple of estimated 2028 EBITDA and assumes a fully diluted share count of 62.6 million shares.

Noble views the start of construction as a positive step, improving the company's risk-reward profile as it moves towards developing operational AI infrastructure.

summary: Strategy’s golden cross may signal a rally, but its shrinking Bitcoin premium, slower Bitcoin purchases, preferred-stock buybacks, and potential MSCI exclusion weaken the bullish case.
content:
Strategy's (MSTR) chart just turned positive for the first time in over three years. Its 50-day moving average has moved above its 200-day average. Traders call this a "golden cross." The last time this happened was in March 2023, and the stock rose nearly 700% in the year after that. So, many people have turned more bullish, expecting another rally. But to be honest, the signal looks pretty weak to me. The two averages are only $0.14 apart, at $135.67 and $135.53. The stock also hasn't gotten back above its 20-day average of $147.40 yet. I also checked other chart signals that track buying strength, and they still look weak.

I think people need to understand why the signal worked so well in 2023. At that time, investors were happy to pay far more for Strategy's shares than its Bitcoin (BTCUSD) holdings were worth. By late 2024, that premium had reached nearly 4x. So Strategy was able to sell new shares, buy more bitcoin, and continue to push the stock higher.

But the market is no longer willing to do so now. On the simple measure tracked by SaylorTracker, the stock was worth about 0.87 times its bitcoin in October. Strategy's own dashboard uses a different formula and shows a small premium, but even that is significantly lower than what it was in late 2024. The company's bitcoin buying has also slowed to about $20 million to $30 million a week. Meanwhile, I pointed out recently that much more of its money is going into buying back its preferred stock instead. On Oct. 19, it also raised its cap on the buyback program to $3 billion.

There is another risk that could hurt the stock. MSCI (MSCI), a big index company, could drop Strategy from its lists in November, and funds that follow those lists would then have to sell the stock. MSCI already flagged Strategy in a test run earlier this year.

Strategy operates as a Bitcoin treasury company. It offers investors varying degrees of economic exposure to Bitcoin by offering a range of securities. MSTR strategically accumulates BTC through equity and debt financing proceeds, positioning it as both an inflation hedge and a vehicle for potential value appreciation. Alongside its Bitcoin treasury operations, Strategy also provides AI-driven enterprise analytics solutions. It has a market cap of $30.6 billion. Founded in 1989, the company is headquartered in Tysons Corner, Virginia.

Shares of the world's largest corporate holder of Bitcoin have fallen 10.72% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. MSTR stock was pressured by the decline in Bitcoin prices, as Strategy is sitting on billions of dollars in unrealized losses on its Bitcoin holdings at current levels. Notably, the stock fell to a low near $82, climbed to a peak near $197, and then roughly doubled off its summer bottom.

Strategy reported its second-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings on July 29. The company posted revenue of $122.37 million, down 0.46% from the $122.93 million forecast. The loss per share came in at $24.45, missing the Wall Street consensus of $0.79. Strategy reported an operating loss of $8.3 million and a net loss of $8.6 billion, driven mainly by a non-cash Bitcoin mark-to-market charge.

Looking forward, MSTR is set to announce its third-quarter earnings on Oct. 29. The company focused on its long-term strategy rather than giving a traditional business forecast. It wants to increase the amount of Bitcoin it holds per share, grow its digital credit business, and maintain a healthy cash reserve in US dollars. Management also wants STRC, its main digital credit product, to trade between $99 and $100.

Wall Street is mostly bullish on MSTR stock. Clear Street raised its price target from $201 to $211 and reiterated a Buy rating ahead of the company's Q3 earnings. The firm believes Strategy improved its financial position during the quarter by issuing common stock to buy back preferred shares. Similarly, Cantor Fitzgerald also raised the firm's price target to $208 from $186 and kept an Overweight rating.

Overall, analysts have a consensus "Strong Buy" rating for MSTR stock. Out of 19 analysts covering the stock, 16 have a "Strong Buy" rating, one has a "Moderate Buy" rating, and two have a "Hold" rating. The mean target price of $233.17 indicates potential upside of about 51% from current levels.

title: BlackRock Just Announced a New Bitcoin ETF. Should You Buy it?
summary: The new ETF offers a sense of safety, but that doesn't mean it's a good purchase.
content:
An interesting new asset linked to Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) might make its debut soon. On Oct. 19, BlackRock (NYSE: BLK) submitted filings to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) seeking permission to issue a new Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF), the iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF, ticker PBIT. Unlike the asset manager's other Bitcoin ETF, the iShares Bitcoin Trust , the new one, if it's approved, is intended to soften Bitcoin's declines in exchange for capping its gains, according to the filing.

But how would that work, and would it make the new ETF worth buying if the SEC gives BlackRock the go-ahead?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Bitcoin is a great asset to own, but its main drawback, volatility, is more than many investors can stomach.

In its lifetime so far, the coin has experienced numerous declines of about 80%. Even when its pullbacks and bear markets are shallower than that, they can still be quite painful; it's now 35% less than its all-time highs of $126,000, set about a year ago.

To address this problem, BlackRock's new ETF would put a limit on those losses, like a seat belt that also puts a hard ceiling on the vehicle's top speed.

Under the hood, the ETF would buy call options (rights to buy an asset at a set price, called the strike) on its main spot Bitcoin ETF, targeted at near 90% of its starting value. Then it would sell call options at higher strike prices to pay for the purchased calls. Each tranche's initial loss exposure is thus about 10% before fees, while the sold calls cap the gains above their strike price.

Three overlapping tranches would be rolled monthly, so the downside insurance would be kept up to date at regular intervals, and each new tranche's cap would reset higher or lower according to market conditions. After a rally, each new tranche's buffer would start further below the current price.

This idea isn't completely novel, and it has held up well in at least one recent test.

One ETF issued by Calamos targets full downside protection rather than a 10% buffer, and it lost just 1% of its value during its one-year protection period starting October 2025, while Bitcoin entered a bear market and plunged.

The catch is that the lost opportunity cost can be high during crypto bull markets, and even during regular seasonality.

Another Calamos 10%-buffer fund had a 22.2% upside cap for its one-year outcome period beginning Feb. 2, 2026. Across Bitcoin's entire historical performance, it has grown by a median of 26.6% in the fourth quarter. For all of 2024, it gained 119.5%.

That would be a lot of upside to miss out on. The new ETF's upside limits aren't disclosed yet.

The Managed Protection ETF's fee hasn't been disclosed yet, either.

BlackRock's spot Bitcoin ETF charges 0.25% per year. If that's anything to go by, the additional features included with the Managed Protection ETF mean that its expense fee will likely be higher. Calamos' 10%-buffer fund charges 0.69% per year.

In contrast, holding Bitcoin directly on an exchange or in a crypto wallet incurs no annual fee, though exchanges do charge transaction fees for each purchase and sale.

Taxes could be an issue, too. BlackRock's prospectus states that its options strategy backing the ETF could generate short-term gains, which would then be taxed as ordinary income, thereby further damping the after-tax returns versus owning the asset directly.

So should you buy this new fund if the SEC says it can launch?

Probably not, unless you're an investor who wants to own some Bitcoin but is fearful of panic-selling.

Even then, a small position or regular purchases in modest amounts may be easier to live with. By capping upside, the fund trims the short, vigorous rallies that drive much of Bitcoin's return. And without that, there are better assets to own that don't cost as much in fees.

title: Willy Woo Runs 10,000 Bitcoin Simulations and Finds a 2028 Top Near $413,000: How Real Is It?
summary: On-chain analyst Willy Woo posted 10,000 simulated price paths for Bitcoin on Monday, October 26, from a random-walk model trained on BTC’s history that builds in the shrinking returns of each cycle, to map where the next tops and bottoms could land. content:
On-chain analyst Willy Woo posted 10,000 simulated price paths for Bitcoin on Monday, October 26, from a random-walk model trained on BTC's history that builds in the shrinking returns of each cycle, to map where the next tops and bottoms could land. The Bitcoin news traders noticed: the median path peaks at $413,000 in December 2028.

Woo himself is more cautious. "She's optimistic," he wrote, naming the band between roughly the 28th and 50th percentile as reasonable, a 2028 top between $241,000 and $413,000, and adding: "It's a simulation, NOT my prediction."

Bitcoin trades at $79,770 today. So what did the model find, and what does it leave out?

The spread is the real result. By February 2033, the 90th percentile sits 33 times above the 10th. Even the gloomy 10th percentile ends 2033 at $120,000, but its 2030 low of $51,900 is about 35% below today's price.

What is the "power-law degradation of returns"? It is the idea that each Bitcoin cycle grows by less than the one before. The bigger the asset gets, the more money it takes to move it.

The history fits. Bitcoin went from about $1,150 at its 2013 top to nearly $20,000 in late 2017, a 17-fold gain. The 2021 top of $69,000 was about 3.5 times that, and October 2025's record of $126,080 was only 1.8 times.

A power law describes that slide: returns fade steadily over time instead of in random jumps. The "c=0.45" in the chart's subtitle sets how fast they fade. "Phase-conditioned" means each simulated day is drawn to match where Bitcoin sits in its cycle, whether rally, top, bear market, or recovery, which is why all 10,000 paths keep the four-year shape.

Next to that history, the median still looks generous. A $413,000 top would be 3.3 times the 2025 peak, almost double the last cycle's gain. Woo's lower bound, $241,000, is 1.9 times the peak, in line with the 1.8 times of the last cycle.

DISCOVER: Is Something Huge Brewing for Bitcoin? Perplexity AI Predicts a Big Move on the Horizon

A lot, which is why Woo calls it a simulation. A random walk trained on past prices assumes Bitcoin will keep moving the way it has, with similar swings and the same four-year rhythm. The market around it has changed.

New buyers: U.S. spot ETFs hold about $102.8 billion of Bitcoin, and Strategy alone holds 848,517 BTC. Neither existed in earlier cycles, and their flows don't follow the halving.

Rates and liquidity: the Federal Reserve raised rates in September and decides again on Wednesday. Every past cycle top came with easy money.

Supply: 20.1 million of the 21 million coins are already mined, so each halving cuts new supply by less in dollar terms.

Rules and risks: regulation, competition, and technical threats such as quantum computing are outside any price model.

A small sample: Bitcoin has had only four full cycles, so 10,000 paths still rest on four tops.

So the chart is a map of possibilities, with no price target and no timing in it.

Bitcoin trades at $79,770, down 2.1% in a week and 36.7% below its October 2025 record. It sits under the 50-day EMA at $80,765, and buyers defended $79,221 on Saturday and again on Monday.
