title: BTC Vs. TAO: Jason Calacanis Says Bitcoin Will Never Hit New Highs, Backs Bittensor Instead
summary: Bitcoin's main upgrade this year changed how the network lines up waiting payments, while Bittensor's biggest first-hand milestone was Gracecale's fund adding more of its tokens.
content:
Jason Calacanis told his followers on Tuesday to sell Bitcoin and move into artificial intelligence.

The all-in co-host said he is long Bittensor's Tau, a token tied to a decentralized AI network.

He called ETF outflows a warning sign, but spot Bitcoin ETFs drew around $110 million on Monday after seeing two days of outflows.

Angel investor Jason Calacanis, an early investor in Uber (UBER) and Robinhood (HOOD), told his followers to sell Bitcoin (BTC) and invest in artificial intelligence on Tuesday, but said he was long Bittensor (TAO).

Bitcoin's rough stretch was just getting started, the All-In podcast co-host wrote on X. "A brutal year for Bitcoin is just getting started," he wrote.

Calacanis said Bitcoin could revisit its 2026 low within a year. "We will test the 57k low again in the next 12 months," he wrote. He also said Bitcoin "will never break its all-time high again."

His argument is that money works best where it grows fastest. Calacanis said there are plenty of faster-growing places for investors to put capital today. He said Bitcoin was a "dead network that offers nothing beyond a store of value".

Calacanis said that "The viral nature of bitcoin was it's power... if you didn't own you were MOCKED!" He thinks the promise of changing the world has moved from Bitcoin to AI. He wrote, "Just sell and shift from Bitcoin to Super Intelligence because one provides little to no value, and the other provides unlimited upside for humanity."

Calacanis said one telling sign was the Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs). "Outflows from ETFs are signal and will continue," he wrote.

According to data from SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows amounting to $635.6 million on Oct. 22. That was the largest one-day withdrawal since June 25. The selling didn't last. The funds attracted $110.34 million on Monday, ending two straight sessions of outflows, data from SoSoValue showed.

However, he was not completely rooting against crypto. Calacanis named his AI bet, saying, "I am long $TAO and love Bittensor's focus on scaling AI."

Bittensor is a decentralized network that uses TAO to reward machine learning algorithms that offer AI services. TAO's price edged up over 0.2% at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TAO dropped to 'extremely bearish' from the 'bearish' zone, with chatter around it at 'normal' levels over the past day. According to platform data, message volume around Bittensor has increased over 60% in a week.

On Stocktwits, Bitcoin was among the top trending tickers at the time of writing. Bitcoin's price was trading around $79,680, down 0.3% in the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Bitcoin remained in the 'bearish' zone, accompanied by 'normal' chatter levels over the past day. According to platform data, message volume around Bitcoin has increased over 28% over the past week.

The biggest upgrade to Bitcoin this year was to the software that most people use to run the network. Introduced in April, it modifies how the network organizes the queue of transactions awaiting processing. That should make it more orderly to decide which payments go through next, and replace a stuck payment with a higher-fee version. The update also added an optional way to send payments more privately. July saw a smaller follow-up that fixed bugs.

The clearest first-hand record this year for Bittensor is not about the network itself. According to Grayscale's filing, its Bittensor fund increased its holdings from 36,193 to 38,289.6 TAO in the first quarter, and TAO's price rose from around $220 to around $307 during that period alone. However, investors still can't redeem their shares for the token, pending regulatory approval.

BTC's price is down over 9% so far this year, while TAO's price has gained over 12% year-to-date.

content:
BTC USD traded near $79,700 on Tuesday, October 27, after U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $110.3 million on Monday, ending a two-day, $773.4 million outflow run a day before the Federal Reserve's rate decision. All of it went into one fund: BlackRock's IBIT.

The flows look small next to the coins the funds track. A new chart from River shows that funds and ETFs hold only 8.5% of the Bitcoin that can still trade, against 79.6% for individuals.

So why do a few hundred million dollars in ETF flows still move the price, and which levels matter before Wednesday?

Less than they sold. Counting Monday, the funds are about $202 million in net outflows for October, after 18 trading days that split almost evenly between buying days and selling days.

The swings were big for a month that went nowhere. The funds took in $526.6 million on October 19, led by $665.2 million into IBIT, and $528.4 million on October 21. Then they lost $635.5 million on October 22, the largest one-day outflow since June 2025, and another $137.9 million on Friday, with IBIT, Fidelity's FBTC and ARK's ARKB leading the selling.

title: Ripple Secures U.S. National Trust Bank License
summary: Financial technology firm Ripple has secured a license to operate a national trust bank in the United States. ...
content:
Financial technology firm Ripple has secured a license to operate a national trust bank in the United States.

The privately held company, which builds blockchain technologies for cross-border transactions and tokenization, can now operate a specialized bank under U.S. federal supervision.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the regulator that oversees American banks, has approved "Ripple National Trust Bank."

The license gives Ripple a traditional bank license. The company applied for the banking license in July 2025.

A national trust bank is a specialized financial institution that operates under a federal charter and can perform trust, fiduciary, and custody services on behalf of clients.

On social media, Ripple said that it plans to offer custody services to institutions, which means it will hold digital assets such as Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) for big companies.

Ripple will also help other companies use cryptocurrencies for payments, trading, and treasury management.

Ripple also plans to use the new bank license to expand its stablecoin (CRYPTO: $RLUSD), which is designed to maintain a 1:1 value with the U.S. dollar.

RLUSD debuted in late 2024 and has grown to a market value of about $2.5 billion U.S., ranking it among the world's top 50 stablecoins.

The stablecoin is used in Ripple's payments business and as collateral. Ripple also uses XRP (CRYPTO: $XRP) to facilitate cross-border payments and transactions.

As a private company, Ripple's stock does not trade on a public exchange.

title: JPMorgan Chase Says That Bitcoin Will Outperform Stocks, Bonds, and Gold Over the Next 10 Years. Here's Why It Might Be Right
summary: The banking giant is still pretty skeptical about Bitcoin.
content:
Per a new report, the asset management arm of JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM) has a base case in which Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) beats domestic stocks, bonds, and even gold during the next 10 years. It expects the crypto to return 10% annually during that period, versus 7.5% for U.S. large-cap stocks, 5.6% for broad U.S. bonds, and 5.5% for gold.

It's the first time the report has put a range on Bitcoin's returns, and it comes with a handful of heavy caveats. Although the figures it calculated are unlikely to prove true in 2036, the drivers for those results are hard to argue against, and it's my view that JPMorgan Chase is directionally correct. Here's why.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The JPMorgan Chase report is largely about the investing implications of the macroeconomic conditions facing the world during the coming years, touching on everything from inflation to global warming and, of course, Bitcoin.

It expects artificial-intelligence-driven productivity gains to push the U.S. economy's real growth rate to 2.1% annually, with inflation averaging 2.4% in the same period. It also raised its expected annual return for large companies, such as those in the S&P 500 index , from 6.7% to 7.5%, citing strong profit margins.

But it contends that Bitcoin will be buoyed by three different factors that will offer better performance than this.

The most important driver, with a 65% weight in the calculation, is Bitcoin's slowing supply growth relative to global money growth. The second-most-important factor, with a weight of 30%, is Bitcoin's inclusion in portfolios alongside allocations to other scarce store-of-value assets, such as gold. The last driver is the weakest: the coin's increasing network activity.

The bank's estimated growth rate for its base case implies that Bitcoin would be priced at about $211,130 by 2036. Its bear case, which calls for an 11.2% annual loss, implies a price of about $24,817, roughly 70% below its $81,300 level as of Oct. 26. The bull case would see it grow by 16.6% annually.

But no matter which of those scenarios plays out, the bank expects the coin's volatility to be 55%, based on historical data.

Overall, JPMorgan Chase's projections for Bitcoin's price growth are on the bearish side compared to Bitcoin's history, but they look reasonable. The coin has a 10-year compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 63%.

The supply model is difficult to dispute; Bitcoin's next halving, when the number of new coins miners earn per block is halved, is expected sometime in April 2028. The U.S. M2, one gauge of the broad money supply, grew by 5.7% in the year through August 2026.

The bank doubts that a currency-debasement scare will spark a rush into crypto, but its model doe assumes a modest shift. Its projected inflation during the next decade is significantly lower than September 2026's 3.7% annual pace, which means that if inflation remains elevated, the importance of Bitcoin as a potential hedge against it could drive its performance toward the bull case.

Still, the bank calls the coin "a speculative asset and a hedge against monetary easing." It says volatility has declined, but unstable correlations make Bitcoin premature as a diversifier.

Though JPMorgan Chase still doesn't recommend buying Bitcoin, it probably makes sense to own at least a little to gain exposure to its upside in the bank's base case, and perhaps a bit more upside if the bull case plays out.

title: Bitcoin and ETH Holders Could Face a Deeper Pullback, Ansem Warns

content:
Crypto trader Ansem has turned bearish on Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH). He warns that both assets broke their mid-timeframe trend and could slide faster below $82,000 and $2,400.

Ansem also says being bullish onchain has become a contrarian position. In his view, sentiment is the worst he has seen in roughly nine years, and Bitcoin and ETH holders could face a deeper pullback.

Ansem bases his call largely on stock market technicals. In his view, AI momentum stocks printed a parabolic blow-off top, a steep final surge that often marks the end of a rally. A lower high and a broken trend followed.

Ansem. Source: X

Headline risk adds more pressure. The Federal Reserve announces its rate decision on October 28, in a packed Fed week that also brings major earnings reports.

Crypto analyst Benjamin Cowen has also laid out a bearish Q4 roadmap for Bitcoin.

Still, Ansem is not bearish on Bitcoin over the longer term. He expects a pullback first and then a move higher.

The crypto trader also expects heavy volatility in both directions through the fourth quarter. Even so, he believes parts of the onchain market could still do well.

Ansem saves his sharpest criticism for Crypto Twitter itself. Traders complain about lower price ceilings on tokens, he says, while too few people build protocols that could change that.

Ansem. Source: X

title: JPMorgan Predicts Bitcoin Will Outpace Stocks, Bonds, and Gold Over the Next Decade. Is Bitcoin Now a Screaming Buy?
summary: The leading cryptocurrency has outperformed all major asset classes over the last 10 years, and JPMorgan Chase expects the same over the next 10.
content:
JPMorgan Chase 's (NYSE: JPM) asset management division recently released the 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, an annual research report that includes 10- to 15-year return projections. For the first time, it has a returns forecast for Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), and expects the top cryptocurrency to outperform the major asset classes.

It's another sign of the growing acceptance of cryptocurrency. CEO Jamie Dimon previously called Bitcoin a fraud, and as recently as 2025, he said he didn't see its value. However, a positive forecast doesn't necessarily mean Bitcoin is a slam-dunk investment.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

JPMorgan's base case for Bitcoin is 10% annualized returns over the next 10 to 15 years, but the bank sees a wide range of potential returns. Its bear case is -11.2%, and its bull case is about 16.5%.

For perspective, JPMorgan forecasts annualized returns of 7.5% for U.S. large-cap stocks , 7.7% for small-cap stocks, 5.5% for gold, and 5.6% to 6.6% for U.S. bonds. Real estate investment trusts (REITs) came in at 8.2%.

If JPMorgan's base cases are accurate, $100 invested in Bitcoin would grow to $259 over the next 10 years. The same amount invested in large caps would grow to $206.

The press release for JPMorgan's report specifically noted that Bitcoin isn't included as an allocation. The bank also hasn't yet included Bitcoin in its main covariance matrices, the models it uses to determine how much of an asset belongs in a portfolio.

JPMorgan laid out two obstacles to Bitcoin portfolio use: volatility and unstable correlations with other assets. Cryptocurrency is known for its volatility, and in Bitcoin's case, JPMorgan assumes 55% annualized volatility, compared to 18% for U.S. large caps and 17.2% for gold.

This volatility is why there's such a large gap between the bull and bear cases for Bitcoin. In the bear case, where Bitcoin loses 11.2% per year, you'd end up with roughly 30% of your money after 10 years.

Bitcoin's unstable correlations with other assets make it difficult to allocate in a portfolio. You can't count on it as a hedge or to balance out risk, because even though it's sometimes called "digital gold," Bitcoin doesn't perform that way. Gold has held its value during several stock sell-offs, whereas Bitcoin frequently falls with the stock market.

A small position in Bitcoin is worth considering if you have a high tolerance for risk and volatility. The cryptocurrency has historically outperformed stocks by a wide margin during its bull markets, with the trade-off that it suffers much greater losses during bear markets. As of Oct. 26, with Bitcoin trading about 36% below the all-time high it set in October 2025, investors can buy in well below its peak.

It's not a must-have, though -- investing in stocks is the far more proven option, and you don't need Bitcoin to get market-beating returns. Even JPMorgan considers Bitcoin a speculative asset, and its bear case shows the potential downside. If you decide to buy Bitcoin, a sensible approach is to limit it to about 5% of your portfolio.

title: 10,000 Bitcoin Simulations Say BTC's Median Path to $1M Comes in 2033
summary: Bitcoin simulations from Willy Woo put the median path to $1 million in 2033, with a 43% drop after a 2028 top.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) simulations from on-chain analyst Willy Woo show the median path reaching $1.03 million in February 2033. The same path first falls 43% from its 2028 cycle high.

Woo stresses the model is not a prediction, but calls $241,000 to $413,000 a reasonable 2028 top. The 29th percentile path he highlights never reaches $1 million. Holders targeting that level wait more than six years in the median case.

Woo built a Monte Carlo simulation, a method that runs thousands of random trials to map possible outcomes. The model trained on prices from the 2018 market bottom to the 2022 bottom.

Woo dropped older data, when 100x gains came easily. He argued that derivatives, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and fast liquidations better describe today's market.

A power-law decay setting of 0.45, shrinks returns with each cycle. Additionally, the model tracks where Bitcoin sits inside its market cycle.

The median path reaches a cycle high of $413,000 in December 2028, then sinks to $234,000 by April 2030. The 29th percentile path sits above 29% of simulations. It tops out at $241,000 in December 2028 and bottoms at $126,000 in April 2030.

Historically, Bitcoin's next bottom has bounced off the prior top, and Woo singled out that path because it matches.

At the extremes, however, the 90th percentile path reaches $1.44 million in March 2029. The 10th percentile falls to $51,900 by April 2030.

All four highlighted paths post cycle highs between December 2028 and March 2029. Meanwhile, a separate 500-day halving rule places the sell window in 2029.

The model assumes future returns resemble the 2018 to 2022 record. Therefore, a change in market structure would break it. Likewise, cycle tools face a similar test, as Bitcoin traded beneath every band of the famous rainbow chart in June.

If power-law decay holds, each cycle yields smaller multiples, and seven-figure targets move later on the calendar.

title: Why Do Crypto Traders Keep Losing Money? Analyst Bitbull Explains
summary: Popular crypto influencer Bitbull explains why traders keep losing money, the dangers of revenge trading, and how emotions derail strategies.
content:
Bitcoin nearly touched $85,000 last week. Days later, it was struggling to hold $80,000. Traders who bet on the recovery suddenly found themselves facing another selloff.

The reversal came as leveraged bets remained elevated, even while buyers pulled back. According to Glassnode's latest market report, Bitcoin's futures market remains heavily exposed to further price swings.

For Bastian Keller, the trader better known as Bitbull, this is where many investors make their most expensive mistakes. Speaking to BeInCrypto at TOKEN2049 Singapore earlier this month, he explained why trading psychology can matter more than predicting the next price move.

Keller founded Bitbull Trading and TradeMania, a trading community and software platform. TradeMania has a commercial partnership with Bitunix, which Keller described as its main exchange partner.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qLcjjbQCGng

One of Keller's most controversial views challenges a common piece of advice given to aspiring traders: practise with fake money before risking your own.

He believes paper trading creates unrealistic confidence because traders know they have nothing to lose.

"When it's come then to real money, yeah, it's completely different," Keller said. "Emotions coming in, FOMO coming in, and then end of the day your your brain decide what you're doing."

His argument is straightforward. Someone might calmly hold a losing position in a simulated account. Put their savings on the line, and fear can take over.

Keller recommends starting with very small amounts of real money to understand that pressure.

"You can trade with $10. You can trade with $50," he said.

Paper trading remains useful for learning platforms and testing strategies without financial risk. Keller's criticism concerns whether those lessons prepare traders for the emotional pressure of real losses.

Keller learned this lesson through his own losses.

Before entering cryptocurrency in 2018, he traded Forex. He told BeInCrypto that he was scammed and struggled with the experience.

That history shaped what he calls the trading "circle of death."

A trader loses money. Instead of accepting the loss, they immediately enter another position to recover it. When that fails, they take an even bigger risk.

"Then you're going to your revenge trading, you lose more, you lose more, you lose more, and then everything is gone," Keller explained. "I was one of these guys before."

Revenge trading becomes particularly dangerous when leverage allows traders to control positions much larger than their deposits. Even a relatively small market move can wipe out their capital.

Bitcoin's latest reversal shows how quickly confidence can disappear.

Glassnode reported that Bitcoin futures open interest climbed from $36.5 billion to $37.5 billion over the past week. Traders holding bullish positions continued paying elevated funding rates even as prices fell.

Meanwhile, spot buying weakened, and investors increasingly sought protection through options.

The market also faces two major events: the Federal Reserve's October 28 interest-rate decision and the November 3 US midterm elections. Analysts expect volatility to rise.

For traders, this creates a difficult environment. A sudden rally can encourage aggressive buying, while the next reversal can trigger forced liquidations.

Keller believes beginners often make things harder by constantly chasing short-term movements.

"You don't have to do scalping," he said, encouraging traders to consider slower strategies that do not require watching charts every few minutes.

Keller is now trying to address some of these problems through TradeMania.

He said the platform is developing tools that analyze trading history and provide AI-generated feedback on trading behavior.

"You can track your trades and you can communicate with an AI agent as well," he explained.

The idea is to help traders identify recurring mistakes before they become costly habits. However, there is no independently verified evidence from the interview that the AI system improves trading returns.

For now, Keller's most practical advice remains surprisingly simple.

"First of all, don't trust everyone."

That warning extends to trading influencers, automated signals, and market predictions. With Bitcoin entering another uncertain period, managing risk may prove more important than getting the next price call right.

title: Mark Cuban puts Bitcoin and Apple in the same bucket
summary: His latest warning comes as markets chase AI optimism.
content:
Artificial intelligence can change the world without every company being worth the price investors are paying. That gap is getting harder to ignore.

The expectations surrounding Anthropic's upcoming IPO offer another sign of investor enthusiasm for artificial intelligence. The company publicly filed for its initial public offering on Oct. 26, though its share price and offering size have not yet been determined.

Some current and prospective investors, however, value the AI firm at around $1.5 trillion, Reuters reported .

Billionaire investor Mark Cuban thinks markets have already crossed into the crypto and AI bubble territory.

Related: Arthur Hayes says AI bubble won't burst like 2008

In an interview released Monday , Cuban said the setup differs from the dot-com boom because "everything's a meme stock."

Cuban was not saying Bitcoin is literally a stock. His point spotlighted the broader trading behavior.

On Jan. 9, 2024, for instance, Bitcoin jumped to around $48,000 after a false post from the SEC's compromised X account claimed spot Bitcoin ETFs had been approved.

Within minutes, however, BTC fell back to $45,000 right after the agency disavowed the announcement. Apple offers a more recent example.

Shares of the iPhone-maker rose as much as 1% in early trading on Oct. 23 as the iPhone Duo reached stores following strong pre-orders and delivery estimates stretching into January. Apple shares were down about 1.3% in trading Monday , giving back part of those gains.

Cuban argued that investors now move rapidly in and out of major assets on relatively small pieces of news instead of focusing on long-term value.

"We're trading them like baseball cards," Cuban said, adding that he believes markets are in a bubble for that reason.

He was less certain about what could end it.

"What causes it to burst? I have no idea."

Goldman Sachs revises rating and target on beaten-down AI stock

Sam Altman has kind words for Elon Musk's flying car

Trump vows crypto scam crackdown then gets hit with lawsuit

Meta spent $34.91 billion on capital projects in the third quarter of 2026, exceeding the $32.79 billion it generated in operating cash flow. This left the Mark Zuckerberg-led company with negative free cash flow for the period.

Last week, Meta beat Wall Street's third-quarter revenue expectations and forecast stronger fourth-quarter sales. But shares still fell about 7% on Oct. 22 as investors focused on its enormous AI spending plans and a new non-voting share class it said could help fund growth.

Earlier this month, the stock prices of Nvidia, Oracle and CoreWeave also dropped after investors received clarification around OpenAI's annualized revenue figures .

The difference reflected how revenue through partners was counted, not billions of dollars in suddenly lost sales. The clarification rippled through several AI-linked stocks.

Still, the AI boom is backed by real demand.

Nvidia reported $89 billion in data-center revenue for its fiscal second quarter , up 117% from a year earlier.

Cuban's point here is not that AI is fake, but that, in his view, investors are overpaying for the hype

His advice was simple: "Have some cash because at some point it's going to turn." He expects winners to emerge, but says he does not know which companies they will be.

content:
Bitcoin trades 37% below its $126,080 all-time high and needs a 59% rally to set a new record.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs hold $105 billion in net assets but saw a $636 million single-day outflow on October 22.

Bitcoin must close a month above $100,000 by December 2027 or a pre-halving record looks unlikely.

Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) must rise approximately 58.8% to set a new all-time high above its previous record of $126,080, reached on October 6, 2025. Many investors are closely watching this milestone since Bitcoin typically peaks significantly every four years during its halving cycle.

Bitcoin is trading at $79,401, which is about 37% lower than that record. Over the past 24 hours, it has fluctuated between $79,332 and $80,825. In the past month, Bitcoin has dropped by 5%, and it is down 30% over the past year. However, since July 28, when it traded at $63,847, it has risen about 24%.

Polymarket shows about a 5% chance that Bitcoin reaches a new high by December 31. So, can Bitcoin set a new record before the next halving in 2028?

To reach a new all-time high, Bitcoin would need a market capitalization of roughly $2.53 trillion, based on a $126,080 price multiplied by the circulating supply of 20,103,596 BTC. Bitcoin's market cap is around $1.60 trillion.

As Bitcoin's supply increases—capped at 21 million coins but still rising due to mining—the total investment needed to reach the previous peak also grows. This means that new investors will need to contribute more capital to achieve the same price target.

Moreover, Bitcoin dominates the cryptocurrency market, making up 59.5% of the total market value. For Bitcoin to hit a new high, it will likely need significant new demand from outside the crypto space.

Halvings are essential to Bitcoin, as they reduce the rewards miners earn for confirming transactions, effectively slowing the introduction of new supply every 210,000 blocks, or about every four years. The next halving is projected for 2028.

The last halving occurred in April 2024, and Bitcoin reached its all-time high about 18 months later. Since that peak, Bitcoin has not surpassed its previous record, so achieving a second high within the same cycle would break the trend many investors expect.

Spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs)—investment funds that directly hold Bitcoin—report $104.7 billion in net assets, according to SoSoValue. Since their launch, these funds have seen net inflows of $57.2 billion as of October 23.

However, investment patterns can be erratic. For example, on October 21, these funds saw $528.4 million in inflows, then $635.5 million in outflows the following day. The week ended with a net inflow of about $304.7 million.

Interest rates also play a crucial role. The Federal Reserve's benchmark rate has remained at 4.00%, while the 10-year Treasury yield dipped from 5.31% on October 5 to 4.96% on October 22. Since Bitcoin does not earn interest, lower yields can make it more appealing to hold. M2—the total amount of cash and deposits—climbed to $23.3 trillion in August. However, the VIX, a measure of market volatility, rose 28.1% within a month, reaching 19.5.

One significant player in the market is Strategy Inc. ( NASDAQ:MSTR ), a software company that has shifted its focus to Bitcoin. It holds 848,517 BTC, valued at around $67.4 billion. Its ongoing purchases help stabilize Bitcoin during price drops, but if Strategy or similar companies reduce their buying, ETFs may have to absorb all the demand.

Bitcoin's chances of reaching a new all-time high in 2026 seem low, with only a modest possibility of doing so before the 2028 halving. First, it must recover to $84,417, its September 26 price, 6.3% above its October 26 price. Next, it will need to exceed $100,000, roughly 26% more, which requires a Fed rate cut, consistent inflows into ETFs, and corporate buyers continuing to increase their holdings.

In a best-case scenario, where rates decrease in 2027, Bitcoin could surpass $100,000 with time to challenge its $126,080 record. In a more realistic case, Bitcoin might range between $63,847 and $100,000, missing the record. In a pessimistic outlook, rising ETF outflows and a VIX above 20 could push Bitcoin back to $63,847. Therefore, if Bitcoin fails to close a month above $100,000 by December 2027, a pre-halving record looks unlikely.

title: Bitcoin, AI stocks and Elon Musk: Analyst makes 3 bold predictions investors can't ignore
summary: Investor Anthony Pompliano says money printing will lift Bitcoin, AI leaders are undervalued, and betting against Musk is a mistake.
content:
Anthony Pompliano , CEO of Professional Capital Management, has laid out a list of his current market views on X , with Bitcoin, artificial intelligence and Elon Musk at the centre.

In the post, three calls stand out for investors weighing where to put money next.

Pompliano said government "will never stop printing money," a backdrop he expects to keep Bitcoin, gold and land rising for two decades. He called AI "drastically underestimated" and said the best AI companies are significantly undervalued.

He wrote, "Government will never stop printing money, so Bitcoin / gold / land will all do well for 2 decades. AI is drastically underestimated and the best AI companies are significantly undervalued."

He also warned that shorting individual stocks is very difficult, and named a company's internal speed of iteration as the biggest sign of whether it survives.

Related: Elon Musk has a bold answer to America's $40 trillion debt crisis

"Shorting individual stocks is very difficult, so I wouldn't try it but the biggest indicator of whether a company survives or not is the internal speed of iteration now," he noted.

Bonds, in his view, should not be in the conversation for anyone under 50, calling them "picking up pennies in front of steamroller."

Pompliano said, "Venture investing & public markets will blend in next 5 years, so private valuations will rise due to lots more capital chasing a few great companies."

The Bitcoin bullishness echoes an earlier report, where the crypto analyst said that Bitcoin could beat Tesla and SpaceX as a long-term wealth builder.

"Once Bitcoin gets back up north of $100,000, this thing will rocket," he said. Bitcoin traded near $62,162 at the time.

The boldest call concerns Musk.

Pompliano predicted a Tesla and SpaceX merger "will happen" and create the largest company in human history.

"Tesla / SpaceX merger will happen and create largest company in human history. My simple rule is to never bet against Elon," he wrote.

Musk confirmed on SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call last Tuesday that special committees at both companies are assessing a tie-up, though no terms have been agreed.

He called the merger a good idea but said he would not take part in negotiations because of his stakes in both companies. SpaceX holds 18,712 Bitcoin and Tesla 11,509, together more than 30,000.

Pompliano also urged young investors to look beyond what Wall Street has adopted , naming private markets, prediction markets, compute markets and data brokering, and said "agents are coming for finance."

"Young people should look at assets & markets that Wall Street hasn't adopted yet. This used to be Bitcoin/crypto, but now private markets, prediction markets, compute markets, and data brokering," he wrote.

title: Do Bitcoin ETF Flows Really Predict Future Bitcoin Price Moves? This New Research Has Important Implications for BTC Investors.
summary: Arrivals to and departures from the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF and other spot Bitcoin ETFs are interesting, but not necessarily instructive.
content:
Investing is inherently rooted in statistics. Fortunately, not the complex high school math kind of statistics. More like conversational, back-of-a-baseball-card type of statistics.

The emphasis on stats is prevalent in the world of exchange-traded funds (ETFs), where market participants of all stripes intently follow fund flows, also known as inflows and outflows. That's certainly been the case with the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (NASDAQ: IBIT) and the other spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) ETFs that debuted nearly three years ago.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

In theory, comings and goings involving the iShares ETF , the largest fund in the category, should be instructive about the largest cryptocurrency's upcoming price action . However, a new study reveals that those data points aren't as predictive as investors hope.

Every investor would like to have a (legal) edge of some kind. Still, a new study by DWF Labs confirms Bitcoin ETF flows aren't fortune-telling tools for a simple reason: Many investors make the quintessential mistake of performance chasing. In other words, they're reacting to what's already occurred, not what's upcoming.

The study notes that Bitcoin investors tend to exit spot ETFs following large declines and return to the funds after large rallies. That's called buying high and selling low when the better course of action is buying low and selling high. So, while the DWF Labs study notes some correlation between Bitcoin ETF flows and price, price moves first, and the flows/price relationship wanes within just a few days.

There are other reasons why Bitcoin ETF flows lack predictive power. Many crypto investors are HODLers, or devoted market participants, but the DWF study indicates those engaged with spot Bitcoin ETFs are jittery. Many sell these ETFs when Bitcoin slumps by just 7%. That's not even a correction, and it's nowhere near a bear market.

Arguably, the "weak stomachs" possessed by some ETF investors skew the potency of flows data because it's not unusual for Bitcoin to experience multiple declines of 7% (or more) over a few days or longer.

Investors' knack for selling Bitcoin ETFs at low prices merits deeper examination for a simple reason: sellers often do so at inopportune times. In five of the eight big sell-offs examined by DWF, the selling of spot Bitcoin ETFs intensified just days before a bottom was put in.

Don't bother wondering whether the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF's status as the largest spot Bitcoin ETF implies that its flows deliver better signals than those of smaller rivals. Home to $68.7 billion in assets under management as of Friday, Oct. 23, iShares is more than quadruple the size of the next-largest fund in the category. Still, DWF comes right in and says the iShares fund "doesn't carry more signal" than its competitors.

In fact, the song is the same with the iShares ETF as it is with other Bitcoin funds: Inflows generally arrive after big rallies, not before them.

None of that is an indictment of Bitcoin ETFs, but the DWF study is a reminder that Bitcoin investors shouldn't put much stock in ETF flows.

title: Will Bitcoin Hit $100,000 Before the End of 2026?
summary: The top cryptocurrency has been a hot buy in recent months.
content:
This year hasn't been a good one for the leading cryptocurrency Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC). It's been struggling to rally for prolonged periods, and since the start of the year, it's down around 10% -- and that's with it rising higher in recent months.

So far in 2026, it hasn't even hit the $100,000 mark, but that could change as it has been showing signs of life recently. Could it get there before the end of the year?

Concerns relating to U.S. debt and higher bond yields have been pushing more investors into Bitcoin, which can be seen as an alternative to the U.S. dollar and a way to hedge against fiscal instability.

Lately, however, Bitcoin has been trading lower as there may be a bit of profit-taking and renewed fears of overall market stability. With interest rates looking to be on the rise again this year, investors may be looking to exit volatile and speculative investments, such as Bitcoin. Much of its value depends on speculation and on the appetite for risk from retail investors, and without that, it may be difficult to see the cryptocurrency return to its peak anytime soon.

Not only might interest rates rise higher before the end of the year, but the outcome of the midterm elections may also impact the outlook for the crypto markets as a whole, as a potentially split Congress could make it much more difficult to pass any crypto-friendly reform.

In the near term, there may be a greater desire for investors to seek safety rather than to double down on risky assets such as Bitcoin, which is why I don't anticipate that the cryptocurrency will get back to $100,000 anytime soon. Bitcoin's recent rally may once again prove to be short-lived.

summary: Bitcoin sits roughly 37% below its all-time high, and the next halving clock is ticking toward 2028. Whether bulls can close that gap hinges on a fragile mix of Fed moves, ETF flows, and one company sitting on billions in BTC.
content:
Bitcoin trades 37% below its $126,080 all-time high, needing a 59% surge and $2.53 trillion market cap to set a new record.

Polymarket gives only a 5% chance Bitcoin hits a new high by December 31, with the base case ranging between $63,847 and $100,000.

Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) would need to climb about 58.8% to reach a new all-time high above its $126,080 record set on October 6, 2025. Many investors are focused on this figure because Bitcoin tends to peak dramatically every four years during its halving cycle.

Bitcoin is trading at $79,401, which is about 37% below that record. It has fluctuated between $79,332 and $80,825 in the last 24 hours. Over the past month, Bitcoin has dropped 5%, and it is down 30% over the last year, although it has gained around 24% since July 28, when it traded at $63,847.

Polymarket shows about a 5% chance that Bitcoin reaches a new high by December 31. So, could Bitcoin set a new record before the next halving in 2028?

To set a new record, Bitcoin would need a market cap of around $2.53 trillion, based on a price of $126,080 multiplied by the circulating supply of 20,103,596 BTC. Bitcoin's market cap stands at $1.60 trillion.

As Bitcoin's supply continues to grow—capped at 21 million coins but still increasing due to mining—the total investment required to reach the previous peak will also rise. This means prospective buyers will need to invest more money to hit the same record price.

Halvings are a built-in feature of Bitcoin that reduce the rewards miners receive for confirming transactions, effectively slowing new supply every 210,000 blocks, or about every four years. The next halving is expected in 2028.

The last halving occurred in April 2024, and Bitcoin set its all-time high about 18 months later. Since then, Bitcoin has not surpassed that peak, so a second record in the same cycle would break the pattern many investors rely on.

That's music to the ears of patient crypto investors, who have been waiting more than a year for Bitcoin to regain its upward ascent.

Over the past decade, crypto investors have noticed a handful of key indicators that can help to predict when Bitcoin will begin its next bull market rally. One of these is the 200-week moving average. If Bitcoin can climb significantly above its 200-week moving average for a prolonged period of time, the thinking goes, then it's likely off to the races.

The 200-week moving average is the one metric that Saylor specifically cited in recent comments about Bitcoin. Given that the typical Bitcoin market cycle lasts approximately 4 years, using a 200-week average (3.8 years) makes a fair amount of sense. Historically, it has marked the floor for a Bitcoin bear market. Right now, the 200-week moving average for Bitcoin is $67,000, while the current price of Bitcoin is $80,000.

The problem, though, is that Bitcoin no longer has any obvious catalysts to push it higher heading into 2027. Passage of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act was supposed to send Bitcoin sharply higher , but Congress fumbled that ball in September, and it didn't pass.

Moreover, overall macroeconomic indicators remain weak. Oil prices are increasing, inflation is surging, and Treasury yields are rising. It now looks like the Federal Reserve will raise rates, not lower them, further compounding the pessimistic macro outlook.

With that in mind, the primary catalyst for Bitcoin remains institutional adoption. As long as banks and financial institutions embrace Bitcoin, institutional investors keep putting money into Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and digital asset treasury companies keep buying Bitcoin, the price should rise.

Saylor did not set a specific Bitcoin price target for 2027. He merely noted that he thinks there's a high likelihood of Bitcoin hitting $100,000 within the next 12 months.

But let's think really big. What if Bitcoin can reclaim its all-time high of $126,000 from October 2025? That might sound improbable, but Wall Street investment firm Bernstein continues to bang the table for a price of $150,000, and some investors still cling to the idea that Bitcoin will hit $200,000 next year.

Right now, there is a tremendous amount of fear, uncertainty, and doubt (FUD) in the crypto market. The good news is that much of that should dissipate as soon as the midterm elections are over. If that's the case, then congressional lawmakers can get back to the business of passing comprehensive new crypto legislation, and Bitcoin can get back to the business of delivering market-beating returns for investors.

title: 'It Is Not Yet 100% Legal' — Kevin O'Leary Explains Why Most Institutions Haven't Really Touched Bitcoin Yet
summary: Crypto has a branding problem. Some coins want to be dollars, some attract speculators and a few swear they’ll rebuild how business runs. Treating them all as the same bet misses the point. "Shark Tank" investor O’Leary sorted crypto into three buckets in a TikTok video posted Oct. 19, grading each on volatility, regulatory clarity and real-world adoption. Stablecoins landed on the firmest legal ground. Bitcoin landed in Washington’s waiting room. Stablecoins are the Boring Hero "Everybody knows
content:
Crypto has a branding problem. Some coins want to be dollars, some attract speculators and a few swear they'll rebuild how business runs. Treating them all as the same bet misses the point.

"Shark Tank" investor O'Leary sorted crypto into three buckets in a TikTok video posted Oct. 19, grading each on volatility, regulatory clarity and real-world adoption. Stablecoins landed on the firmest legal ground. Bitcoin landed in Washington's waiting room.

"Everybody knows crypto is volatile, but crypto is different things," O'Leary said in the video.

He parked stablecoins, which are built to hold a steady value, at the calm end of his risk scale.

"On the most least volatile of that metric, you would call stable coins the safest right now," O'Leary said. He pointed to the GENIUS Act and U.S. Treasury backing, calling stablecoins "digital money."

O'Leary also said he uses stablecoins as a payment system every day, a sign the technology has a job beyond speculative trading.

The GENIUS Act handed payment stablecoins a federal rulebook. That doesn't make them bulletproof, though. Their reliability still depends on reserve backing, redemption terms and issuer compliance.

Bitcoin sits higher on O'Leary's risk ladder, an asset he described as one investors buy mainly to speculate.

"A little more risky and a lot more volatile is of course, Bitcoin," O'Leary said. "It is a risk asset so you're buying it as a speculator."

Then he turned to the CLARITY Act , the bill meant to give digital asset markets a clear set of rules.

"It is not yet 100% legal because the CLARITY Act has not been passed," O'Leary said. "That's law in Congress. We want that to happen. So most institutions haven't really touched Bitcoin yet."

That bill has had a bumpy ride. The House passed it 294-134 in July 2025, and the Senate Banking Committee advanced it 15-9 in May. Then it hit the Senate floor. On Sept. 15, a procedural vote to start debate failed 49-50, far short of the 60 votes needed.

Bitcoin is legal to own and trade in the U.S., and institutions already have exposure through investment products such as spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds. The open questions center on market oversight and structure, not Bitcoin's basic legality.

Blockchain tokens such as Ethereum fill O'Leary's third bucket. He compared blockchain technology with enterprise software, arguing that real adoption matters more than big promises.

"Although we've been talking about it for twelve years, virtually no one's using blockchain yet," O'Leary said. "But that could change."

That claim overlooks existing blockchain applications, including decentralized finance and stablecoin payments. Still, O'Leary's larger point is that lasting value comes from real-world use, not buzz.

He closed with a simple portfolio takeaway.

"So end of the day, what's the great investment strategy? Buy a little bit of everything," O'Leary said.

His message is that crypto isn't one uniform bet. Stablecoins, Bitcoin and blockchain tokens do different jobs, carry different risks and face different hurdles. For Bitcoin, one of the biggest is still sitting in the Senate.

title: Netanyahu's Crypto Plan Sparks Economic Fears Ahead of Israel Elections
summary: Netanyahu's crypto plan to dodge bank sanctions rides on Israel's vote. Here's what happens if he wins or loses.
content:
Israelis vote on Tuesday in an election that could end Benjamin Netanyahu's rule. Days before the vote, the prime minister has proposed an unusual financial backup plan: using cryptocurrency to protect Israel if international sanctions cut its banks off.

In a Friday interview, Netanyahu said he had ordered advisers to explore blockchain technology as a way around potential banking restrictions.

He offered no details. No Bitcoin-based system, budget, or implementation timeline has been announced.

The threat remains hypothetical. Western sanctions have targeted Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, while Israel's wider banking system remains connected internationally.

Netanyahu argues the country must prepare for possible financial isolation. However, the Bank of Israel rejected his proposal.

"Cryptocurrencies cannot serve as a means of circumventing sanctions," the central bank said.

Blockchain can transfer money across borders, but it cannot force foreign businesses or banks to accept payments.

"Changing the means of payment does not turn a prohibited transaction into a permitted one," crypto expert Tomer Sharoni explained.

The warnings went further. In a public letter, 109 economists and business leaders, including Nobel laureate Joel Mokyr, warned that sweeping sanctions could devastate Israel's technology sector and foreign investment.

Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot warned that Netanyahu's approach could threaten ordinary Israelis' wealth.

"Israelis will lose their pensions and all their investments, and many of them will leave the country."

Meanwhile, Israel's regulated crypto industry is progressing independently. Regulators approved the BILS shekel stablecoin in April, with financial safeguards and supervision.

Netanyahu's political future is far less certain.

The final election polls put his coalition at just 50 seats, 11 short of a parliamentary majority. His rivals also lack enough seats to govern.

Exit polls arrive Tuesday at 10 p.m. If neither side can form a government, Netanyahu could remain caretaker prime minister while Israel faces another election in 2027.

title: Is Bitcoin the Best Cryptocurrency You Can Buy Right Now?
summary: Wondering which digital coin to hold for the next decade? Bitcoin stands out as the bedrock of the crypto market while rivals face risky upgrades.
content:
If you're reading the financial news daily, you may well be under the impression that Bitcoin 's (CRYPTO: BTC) price is some kind of magic number that's directly linked to tech earnings, the price of oil , or whatever's going on in the Middle East on any particular Tuesday. The story is always in flux.

At the high end of the scale, Ark Invest (Cathie Wood) forecasts Bitcoin to reach nearly $800k by 2030. At the low end, JPMorgan Chase says it could go to zero in theory, while still setting a very reasonable base case of 10% returns per annum.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Here's my take: I can't guarantee that Bitcoin will beat all the other cryptos (or indeed any of them) over the next 1, 5, or 10 years. My time machine is in for repairs again (those flux capacitors are rather flimsy and expensive). I'd need it back before daring to make such a claim.

There's no guarantee that Bitcoin will be the best-performing digital asset, but it is very much the safest crypto investment you can make at the moment. You could probably make an argument for stablecoins , but in that case, you'd be just as well off with a high-yield savings account.

Competing networks are in a state of flux. Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) and Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) are both in the midst of huge network upgrades designed to increase transaction speed and open up new markets. All of that notwithstanding, Bitcoin's fundamental value lies in its stability, the trust it commands from institutions, and its proven track record of surviving multiple market cycles.

That would have sounded utterly unrealistic and wrong just a few years ago. The crypto space has moved on, though, and we now have an elder statesman of the sector with a growing track record of stability. That's Bitcoin.

It doesn't have to be the fastest network to be the best long-term holding. Looking ahead, the integration of quantum-safe encryption will be a key milestone. When that pivotal upgrade comes along, Bitcoin is set for many years of safe, stable, and generally useful blockchain ledger holdings.

The same arguments could be made for other cryptos too, just not as convincingly as they can be made for Bitcoin. It's still the bedrock of the crypto world even when the rest of the market is in a frenzy.

So if you're planning to buy just one cryptocurrency in the final quarter of 2026, Bitcoin should be it. Unlike many of its ultra-volatile peers, this cryptocurrency will let you sleep at night.

title: Michael Howell Says Bitcoin Outperforms Gold When Fed Liquidity Beats China
summary: Global Liquidity expert Michael Howell expected global liquidity to pick up sooner than his 2027 base case.
content:
Michael Howell said Bitcoin holding above $70,000 would make him "powerfully change" his view.

He said Bitcoin "tends to outperform gold when Fed Liquidity grows faster than PBoC Liquidity."

Howell warned of "further weakness in coming months" but said Bitcoin "is going to go up because the liquidity cycle is going to turn."

Macro analyst Michael Howell said on Monday that Bitcoin (BTC) holding above $70,000 could be a "game changer" for his outlook on global liquidity, while explaining that Bitcoin tends to beat gold when the U.S. Federal Reserve adds liquidity faster than China's central bank.

Speaking on the Bankless podcast, Howell, a global liquidity expert and the Managing Director at GL Indexes, said his base case was still that global liquidity will not bottom until the second half of 2027. However, he said Bitcoin's recent stability could be an early signal of a turn.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

"If you get Bitcoin holding above 70,000, if you see more evidence that bank reserves are being managed and maybe being pushed up, then I would powerfully change my view and expect to see liquidity picking up," Howell said. In that case, Bitcoin could be signaling the early stages of "another two to three year bull market," he added. He stressed, "It's not my base case."

Bitcoin was among the top trending crypto tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing. Howell's comments came as Bitcoin's price traded around $79,600 on Monday, nearly 14% above the $70,000 level he flagged.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the 'bearish' zone, while chatter stayed at 'normal' levels over the past day.

Howell said in the interview that Chinese money printing has been the main driver of gold's rise. "It'd be great to put more money into gold." he said, adding that "Look at China's warping great trade surface."

Citing Richard Nixon, Howell pointed out that "I mean, we talk about debasement, but broadly speaking, ever since Richard Nixon closed the gold window back in 1971, you effectively had free-floating currencies and ongoing debasement, or certainly accelerated displacement, one would say." Adding to it he said, "Paradoxically, the U.S. is moving more towards the Chinese model than maybe many people would like, and this is big government, big state."

Writing on Substack, Howell added that "Bitcoin tends to outperform gold when Fed Liquidity grows faster than PBoC Liquidity," referring to the People's Bank of China. He asked whether the Bitcoin-gold ratio was becoming a "scoreboard" for America versus China.

Howell warned that there may be "further weakness in coming months," but said he would buy on dips. "I think Bitcoin is going to go up because the liquidity cycle is going to turn," he said. He suggested holding both Bitcoin and gold. "They both work. Why don't you just own both?" he asked.

He said he would weigh the mix by volatility, holding more gold for now. As Bitcoin becomes more institutional, "its volatility will come down, and therefore you can increase your weighting over time," Howell said.

Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist Mike McGlone also focused on the Bitcoin-gold ratio. He said Bitcoin "has bounced from its earlier-in-the-year swoon to key inflection levels vs. gold, U.S. Treasury bonds and the S&P 500 (SPX)."

McGlone warned of "greater downside risks" unless Bitcoin "can recover from its relative-dud performer status of almost five years." His chart shows the ratio near 20, a level he flagged as key, adding that Bitcoin "may need higher stocks" to clear it. He also noted that Bitcoin's volatility against gold has fallen to "about 1-to-1," which he called "the lowest ever."

title: $8 Trillion in Big Tech Earnings, Fed Decision and Inflation Data: Bitcoin's Next Big Test?
summary: The Federal Reserve's Oct. 28 decision, followed by US inflation and GDP figures, could reshape expectations for interest rates and Bitcoin. Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon…
content:
Key Takeaways

The Federal Reserve's Oct. 28 decision, followed by US inflation and GDP figures, could reshape expectations for interest rates and Bitcoin.

Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report earnings as investors question whether massive AI infrastructure spending can deliver sustainable returns.

Bitcoin's recent weakness near $80,000 puts the spotlight on interest rates, institutional demand and whether crypto can withstand another technology-stock selloff.

Bitcoin faces a critical test during the week of Oct. 26, as major central bank decisions, US inflation data, and earnings from technology giants converge over the course of the week.

The Federal Reserve is expected to announce its interest rate decision Wednesday, followed by third-quarter US GDP and September personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation figures Thursday.

Meanwhile, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon will report quarterly earnings, putting the artificial intelligence investment boom under scrutiny.

The timing is particularly important for cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin recently slipped toward $79,100 after struggling to maintain the $80,000 level, while concerns about inflation and technology valuations have weakened investor confidence.

The Federal Reserve's Oct. 28 announcement is arguably the week's most important scheduled event for Bitcoin.

Following September's rate increase, the federal funds target range stands at 3.75% to 4.00%. Markets largely expect policymakers to hold rates unchanged .

According to CME FedWatch probabilities reported by MarketWatch on Oct. 26, traders assigned approximately a 9% probability to another quarter-point increase this week, rising to 73% for December.

That makes the Fed's forward guidance potentially more influential than Wednesday's decision itself.

Higher interest rates increase the appeal of interest-bearing assets while raising borrowing costs and tightening financial conditions. Bitcoin, which generates no contractual yield, can face pressure when investors demand greater compensation for holding riskier assets.

Coinbase Institutional's Oct. 16 research supports this connection. It found Bitcoin had shown greater resilience than semiconductor stocks during recent AI-related selloffs but remained sensitive to changes in interest rate expectations.

The report identified the $80,000 to $82,000 region as important near-term support, with further downside potentially bringing the $72,000 to $74,500 area into focus.

Wednesday brings earnings from Alphabet and Microsoft, followed by Amazon on Thursday.

Alphabet and Microsoft represent roughly $8 trillion in market value, making their results particularly important for the technology sector.

Investors will examine Microsoft's Azure cloud growth, Alphabet's advertising and cloud businesses, and Amazon's AWS performance. But the bigger question concerns the returns generated by billions of dollars committed to AI infrastructure.

Reuters reported that disappointing results from Meta and Lam Research had already weakened technology stocks, raising concerns about whether AI spending can sustain elevated valuations.

The earnings calendar adds another dimension: approximately 542 companies valued above $2 billion are scheduled to report this week, with Wednesday and Thursday accounting for 73% of the market capitalization represented.

Strong results could restore confidence in growth-sensitive assets, including cryptocurrencies. However, disappointing cloud growth or higher-than-expected capital expenditures could intensify selling pressure.

Bitcoin's reaction is not guaranteed to mirror the Nasdaq. Coinbase's research suggests its correlation with semiconductor stocks has weakened, indicating that monetary policy may currently matter more than AI-related equity movements.

Thursday's economic releases introduce another potential source of volatility.

According to Morningstar's economic calendar, September headline PCE inflation is forecast at 3.6% annually, compared with 3.4% in August. Core PCE is expected at 3.1%, up from 3.0%.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis has scheduled both PCE and third-quarter GDP figures for Oct. 29 at 8:30 a.m. ET.

Higher-than-expected inflation could reinforce expectations of another Fed rate hike in December. Conversely, softer inflation could reduce pressure on Treasury yields and support risk assets.

GDP presents a more complicated picture. Strong growth may indicate economic resilience, but combined with persistent inflation, it could also justify keeping monetary policy restrictive.

International developments add another risk.

The Bank of Japan concludes its policy meeting Friday, Oct. 30, with its benchmark rate currently around 1.25%.

A surprise hawkish signal could strengthen the yen and encourage investors to unwind yen-funded carry trades, potentially reducing liquidity across global financial markets.

For Bitcoin , the central question is whether institutional demand can absorb another macroeconomic shock.

A combination of softer inflation, reassuring Fed guidance, and stronger technology earnings could support a recovery. However, persistent inflation, hawkish central banks, and disappointing AI results could deepen the selloff.

With several major announcements arriving within 48 hours, Bitcoin investors face a test of whether the cryptocurrency can maintain its footing as global financial conditions shift.

Just five years after its founding, Anthropic could become more valuable than all Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) in circulation, with Polymarket traders giving the AI company a 77% chance of overtaking the cryptocurrency before year-end.

Anthropic filed its IPO prospectus Monday, ahead of an expected November Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT. Investors have reportedly discussed valuations between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion, although the company has yet to disclose an offering price.

Bitcoin's market capitalization stood around $1.61 trillion Monday, according to CoinGecko .

At a $1.75 trillion valuation, Anthropic would already be worth roughly $140 billion more than Bitcoin. Even at $1.5 trillion, a Bitcoin decline of about 7%, to roughly $74,600, could put the AI company ahead.

Anthropic generated $4.6 billion in revenue throughout 2025, according to its prospectus. By the third quarter of 2026, it was bringing in $16.8 billion in just three months, nearly four times its entire previous year's sales.

That single quarter even surpassed the $16.3 billion Anthropic generated in the first six months of 2026, itself a 14 fold increase from a year earlier.

At its third-quarter pace, the Claude developer was generating the equivalent of more than $67 billion annually.

Reuters previously reported that Anthropic projects annual revenue of $190 billion to $200 billion by 2028, helping explain the enormous valuations investors have considered.

Some investors have nevertheless lowered their IPO valuation expectations toward $1.5 trillion as quarterly revenue growth has slowed, according to Reuters.

Technology investor Paul Kedrosky recently warned Benzinga that cheaper, smaller AI models could threaten premium providers like Anthropic, as most consumers and businesses may not need expensive, cutting-edge models for everyday tasks.

A confirmed IPO valuation could resolve the contract before shares begin trading. A qualifying private funding valuation also counts.

Matt Hougan , chief investment officer at Bitwise , argued in a June memo that AI stocks, robotics companies and SpaceX were drawing investors away from cryptocurrencies.

"With AI sucking all the oxygen out of the room," he wrote, crypto was becoming a contrarian investment rather than a momentum trade.

Traders on Polymarket give the AI bubble just a 10% chance of bursting by Dec. 31, rising to 23% by June 2027. The market has attracted more than $3.1 million in trading volume.

"Money supply surges and bitcoin rallies hard," Hougan wrote, describing a scenario in which Bitcoin eventually benefits from an AI crash.

title: Franklin Templeton's New ETFs Could Create a Bitcoin Buying Machine
summary: Franklin Templeton's planned ETFs will send dividends from top US stocks into Bitcoin, then trim it at 5%. Here's the catch.
content:
For decades, index funds have used dividends to buy more stock. Franklin Templeton wants to use them to buy Bitcoin (BTC) instead.

The asset manager has filed for two Nasdaq-listed funds, each starting with 95% stocks and 5% Bitcoin exposure. Neither has launched yet.

Why does this matter for Bitcoin? Index funds invest in baskets of major company stocks. When those companies pay dividends, or cash rewards to shareholders, the money usually goes back into buying more stocks. Franklin Templeton wants to use that money to buy Bitcoin exposure instead, creating a regular source of BTC demand.

One fund holds the 500 largest US companies. The other holds the 100 biggest Nasdaq-listed firms, minus finance companies.

Each starts with 95% in stocks and 5% in Bitcoin. Then the dividends start flowing.

"All regular and special dividends are reinvested into Bitcoin at the market open on the day following the dividend ex-date, which increases Bitcoin exposure over time," reads an excerpt in the prospectus.

The fees are low. The larger fund charges 0.09% a year, or $9 on every $10,000 in year one.

Here is the twist. Every quarter, any Bitcoin share above 5% gets cut back to 4.5%. If it passes 20% between reviews, it is reset to 4.5% within two business days.

So, a Bitcoin rally triggers selling. A crash does the opposite, leaving fresh dividends to buy at lower prices.

The funds won't hold coins directly. They will buy Bitcoin funds, including Franklin-affiliated ones, alongside futures and options. Franklin says it may waive fees on its own products, but it can end that waiver at any time.

Franklin's own prospectus calls Bitcoin highly speculative and prone to big price swings.

The wider debate is loud. Himalaya Capital founder Li Lu called crypto fundamentally bogus last week. BlackRock, which manages more money than any rival, recommends a 1-2% Bitcoin position.

Franklin's design sits closer to BlackRock's camp. Its Bitcoin slice starts at 5% and gets trimmed once it grows.

The real test comes when trading begins on Nasdaq, where Franklin has registered the shares.

title: Chamath’s $0 Bitcoin Call Meets Musk’s AI ‘Death’ Warning — Where Could BTC Price Be by 2031?
summary: Chamath Palihapitiya predicts a turbulent 2027 for AI infrastructure, while Elon Musk warns many specialist cloud providers will fail or consolidate. Their latest exchange follows…
content:
Key Takeaways

Chamath Palihapitiya predicts a turbulent 2027 for AI infrastructure, while Elon Musk warns many specialist cloud providers will fail or consolidate.

Their latest exchange follows Palihapitiya's prediction that Bitcoin will eventually be hacked and become worthless.

Recent comments have put Bitcoin's five-year outlook into focus.

Elon Musk's warning about stranded AI computing capacity has drawn agreement from Chamath Palihapitiya, who predicts a turbulent 2027 as unsuccessful investments unravel.

For Bitcoin investors, the exchange adds another concern alongside Palihapitiya's recent prediction that Bitcoin will eventually become worthless.

Together, they raise a bigger question, what would Bitcoin need to achieve to trade substantially higher by 2031?

Musk's warning about stranded AI computing capacity prompted Chamath Palihapitiya to outline his own concerns about the industry's outlook.

In an Oct. 25 post on X, Palihapitiya argued that the AI infrastructure boom faces problems extending beyond demand for computing power.

He described specialist cloud providers, often called neoclouds, as "disorganized and poorly capitalized," while criticizing larger technology companies for slow decision-making.

His central concern is that construction constraints could leave expensive equipment unable to generate the returns investors expect.

"There are delays in the existing pipeline that will catch people off guard in 2027."

Palihapitiya said some computing capacity could be bought and paid for but remain underused or fail to earn enough to cover its financing costs.

"2027 will be a turbulent year because it will clear out a bunch of wrong/bad bets. It will also be a consolidation year for a few."

Musk endorsed the concerns, arguing that access to borrowing had tightened sharply for companies dependent on AI data centers .

"As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers."

He said the consequences could extend across more than 200 specialist providers.

"That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many."

The warning followed another post in which Musk predicted:

"I think we're going to see a lot of stranded compute in partially complete data centers."

Palihapitiya's AI warning follows a separate, more sweeping prediction about Bitcoin.

As CCN reported on Oct. 22 , he told the Moonshots podcast:

"I just think it's capped and then I think eventually it gets hacked and then it goes to zero."

His argument questioned whether Bitcoin's decentralized community could coordinate security changes before increasingly powerful computing technology threatened existing protections.

The latest Musk–Palihapitiya exchange supplies a different potential transmission channel into this.

An AI investment downturn could weaken risk appetite and force investors to sell liquid holdings.

Bitcoin could come under pressure even if its network continued operating normally.

As CCN's recent examination of AI-bubble risks explored, a subsequent recovery would depend partly on whether policymakers eased financial conditions—and whether that encouraged renewed crypto investment.

The connection also runs through listed companies converting mining infrastructure into AI facilities.

IREN's financial results reported $128.8 million in AI cloud revenue for its fiscal year ended June 2026, alongside $578.2 million in Bitcoin-mining revenue.

It also recorded $638.8 million in noncash impairments, primarily associated with decommissioning mining hardware as sites were converted for AI services.

The shift also extends beyond IREN.

As CCN previously reported , MARA CEO Fred Thiel has highlighted how access to power and predictable hosting contracts are drawing miners toward AI infrastructure.

Bitfarms announced plans to wind down its mining operations and convert its facilities, while Genesis Digital Assets has also pursued an AI expansion.

Palihapitiya is not alone in questioning Bitcoin's long-term survival.

World Gold Council CEO David Tait offered a similarly bearish call during an interview on The David Lin Report, saying Bitcoin ultimately "will go to zero."

His criticism focused on Bitcoin's credentials as "digital gold."

Tait argued that it has frequently traded alongside risk assets during market stress, rather than providing the protection investors might expect from a defensive holding.

However, he acknowledged that his forecast was a personal judgment rather than the result of a valuation model.

"It's just my personal opinion. Just instinct as a trader," he said.

Palihapitiya's zero-dollar prediction sits at the opposite end of the spectrum from Standard Chartered's $500,000 Bitcoin target for 2030, previously examined in CCN's coverage of bullish forecasts and AI-market risks.

The bank's thesis depends on institutional adoption and investment flows expanding substantially. Its deadline is 2030—not a specific forecast for 2031.

Using a starting price of $80,000, reaching $500,000 would require a 525% increase, taking Bitcoin to 6.25 times that level.

Spread over five years, that would demand approximately 44.3% annual compounded growth.

Meanwhile, Palihapitiya's outcome would require a 100% decline.

Even a devastating 99% crash would leave Bitcoin trading at $800.

Bitcoin's continued trade at a nonzero price is more plausible than its permanent worthlessness, provided its network remains secure.

However, rejecting the zero-dollar thesis does not mean that $500,000 is absolutely likely.

The two extremes also rest on different assumptions.

Standard Chartered anticipates expanding adoption while Palihapitiya anticipates a security failure that Bitcoin cannot adequately overcome.

Musk's warning about AI cloud businesses proves neither.

An infrastructure downturn could initially hurt Bitcoin by reducing risk appetite and tightening financing.

For 2031, the more defensible expectation is continued uncertainty and substantial price volatility — without clear confidence that either $0 or $500,000 is a definite.

Bitcoin held above $79,200 for a third straight day on Monday, October 26, as traders braced for a week that puts Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision, Thursday's Coinbase and Strategy earnings and Friday's $10.9 billion options expiry into three back-to-back sessions. Nobody wants to be early. The key Bitcoin news this week is the calendar.

Bitcoin trades near $80,300, flat on the day and down 2.4% in a week. Monday's dip to $79,369 was bought within hours, just as Saturday's low of $79,221, the lowest since September 18, was.

So what is pressing on the price, and which levels decide the break?

Five things, and most of them come from outside crypto.

ETF buyers turned sellers : U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $635.6 million on Thursday, the biggest one-day outflow since June 2025, and another $137.9 million on Friday. BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC led both days. That reversed more than two-thirds of the $1.07 billion the funds took in earlier in the week. Monday's figures arrive after the U.S. close.

The Fed is still leaning hawkish : Traders aren't expecting a cut. Polymarket puts a 94.5% chance on the Fed holding rates on Wednesday, after September's hike, and 5.5% on another raise. The statement matters less than Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference: with the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.99%, any hint of a December hike would weigh on risk assets again.

Oil is still above $100 : Brent trades near $110 on Monday, down from Friday's $116.72 close after tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. crude is back above $101. Expensive oil keeps inflation sticky, and sticky inflation keeps the Fed cautious.

Leverage has been flushed out : Saturday's drop to $79,221 cleared about $820 million in crypto liquidations, mostly from traders betting on higher prices. The reset is visible in funding: perpetual futures on OKX and Hyperliquid now pay the neutral base rate of 0.01% every eight hours, so neither side is crowded going into the Fed.

A big options expiry on Friday : About 135,700 BTC of Bitcoin options, worth roughly $10.9 billion, expire on at 08:00 UTC, 35% of all open contracts on the exchange. Max pain, where the most options expire worthless, sits at $78,000. Calls still outnumber puts almost two to one, with the largest bets at $95,000 and $100,000, but the puts that matter are lower: the biggest put positions, the market's downside hedges, sit at $75,000 and $70,000.

More than the Fed. The week's events in order:

Strategy is the one to watch for buying. Its latest filing, on October 19, showed 267 BTC bought at about $82,900, taking holdings to 848,517 BTC at an average cost of $75,446. It had not filed a new purchase by Monday's U.S. morning.

Bitcoin closed Sunday at $80,154, below its 50-day EMA at $80,808 for the first time since mid-August, and Monday has not won it back. Reclaiming that line is the first job for buyers.

Above it, $81,390 to $81,840 is the next barrier, where the 4-hour 50 and 200 EMAs meet. Then comes $82,850, which capped every bounce last week.

On the downside, $79,221 to $79,369 is the floor: Saturday's low and Monday's. A daily close below it would open the way to Friday's max pain at $78,000 and then the 200-day EMA at $76,348, with Strategy's $75,446 cost basis and the $75,000 put wall just beneath.

With leverage cleared and funding neutral, the next move will come from the calendar rather than the liquidation engine. Three sessions, three catalysts: the Bitcoin news that decides which side of $80,000 the month closes on starts Wednesday, and until then $79,221 is the line buyers can't afford to lose.

Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, said the drop was "primarily driven by a broader correction in global risk assets," with growing skepticism toward AI-related technology stocks a major factor.

"Investors are not necessarily questioning the long-term prospects of artificial intelligence, but rather whether current elevated valuations can be justified by future earnings and cash flows," Sun told Decrypt . Outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs and the unwinding of leveraged positions "further amplified the downward pressure," he said.

Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, said Bitcoin had come under pressure alongside tech stocks. "Persistent inflation, elevated Treasury yields and expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening have reduced enthusiasm for speculative assets," she told Decrypt .

Stephen Wundke, strategy and revenue director at quantitative investment firm Algoz, said $80,000 was a psychologically important mark for many investors, but warned that a break below it could be misleading, given low trading volumes over weekends.

More worrying, he said, was a broader decline in trading volumes as investors pull out of altcoins and park funds in stablecoins.
