"The bull case for Bitcoin is not dead but it is keeping its head below the parapet whilst so many stray bullets are flying across the globe," Wundke added.

Sun said that if Bitcoin falls further, he sees $75,000 as a key support level to watch, and expects volatility to stay elevated.

Hathorn said the Fed's decision on Wednesday and major technology earnings "could prove just as important for Bitcoin as developments within the cryptocurrency market itself." A more hawkish Fed could strengthen the dollar and weigh on risk assets, she said, while "Bitcoin's recovery may remain fragile unless stronger institutional demand accompanies any improvement in broader market sentiment."

title: Bitcoin’s Bear Market Is Over, Galaxy Research Says: 'Now Is an Attractive Time to Buy'
summary: Galaxy Research says Bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, pointing to a reclaimed 50-week moving average, fading selling pressure, and a strengthening debasement case.
content:
Galaxy Digital's head of research thinks the worst is over for Bitcoin.

In a report published Monday, Alex Thorn, Galaxy's head of firmwide research, argued that Bitcoin's bear market ended in June and that the asset is now in an accumulation phase. "Our conclusion is simple: we believe now is an attractive time to buy and hold bitcoin," he wrote.

The call comes as Bitcoin struggles for direction. It traded at around $80,000 on Thursday, 36% below its October 2025 high but 39% above its June 30 low. On Sunday, Bitcoin briefly slipped below $80,000 to about $79,700, according to CoinGecko.

Thorn's case starts with the charts. Bitcoin spent 44 weeks below its 50-week moving average before reclaiming it in September, and the week ended Oct. 18 marked its fifth straight weekly close above that line. Since 2011, Bitcoin has reclaimed the average after a stretch of 20 weeks or more four times. In each case, the price never closed more than 8.4% below the reclaim level over the following year and eventually regained its prior all-time high.

The halving cycle, the roughly four-year event when rewards for Bitcoin miners are cut in half thereby reducing new supply, points the same way. The three previous cycles bottomed between 777 and 912 days after a halving, and Thursday was day 916. The latest downturn was also the shallowest on record: a 53% drop, compared with declines of 77% to 93% in past cycles.

Onchain data appears to back that up. For the first time in any bear market, Bitcoin's market value never fell below its realized value, the average price at which every coin last moved. The ratio between the two bottomed at 1.10, compared with lows of 0.56, 0.69 and 0.75 in prior cycles.

Short-term holders, whose coins carried the recovery from $58,525, have an average cost of $74,811 and sit about 9% in profit. Yet the spent-output profit ratio, which tracks whether coins are being sold at a gain, sits at 1.009, suggesting few are cashing out.

Selling pressure is fading, too. Long-dormant coins, unmoved for five years or more, have been sold at about 34,000 BTC a month this year, half the 2024 pace. title: Franklin Templeton’s New ETFs Could Make Millions of Investors Own Bitcoin Without Realizing It
summary: Franklin Templeton’s proposed FBEQ and FIBT ETFs combine US stocks with Bitcoin exposure funded by reinvested dividends. Their indexes started with 95% in equities and…
content:
Key Takeaways

Franklin Templeton's proposed FBEQ and FIBT ETFs combine US stocks with Bitcoin exposure funded by reinvested dividends.

Their indexes started with 95% in equities and 5% in Bitcoin, with rebalancing rules designed to keep crypto as a secondary allocation.

Investors would own ETF shares, gaining indirect exposure to Bitcoin while remaining exposed to stock and crypto market risks.

Franklin Templeton is preparing two exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that could make Bitcoin exposure part of an ordinary stock investment, automatically directing equity dividends into the cryptocurrency.

The proposed products combine portfolios of US companies with a smaller Bitcoin allocation , putting the reinvestment decision inside the fund rather than leaving investors to make separate crypto purchases.

That could broaden Bitcoin's reach among investors primarily interested in equities. However, "without realizing it" comes with a qualification: both funds explicitly include Bitcoin in their names, and shareholders would own ETF shares rather than coins in personal wallets.

The Franklin US Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF and Franklin US Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF are moving toward Nasdaq listings under the tickers FBEQ and FIBT.

Their latest prospectuses identify Oct. 27, 2026, as the proposed effective date. That date should not be confused with a confirmed first trading session or an SEC endorsement of the investments.

Franklin initially proposed the products on June 18. Subsequent filings repeatedly postponed the effective date, with an Oct. 16 amendment setting the Oct. 27 timeline.

FBEQ will track the VettaFi US Large-Cap 500 Bitcoin DRIP Index, while FIBT will follow the VettaFi US Innovation 100 Bitcoin DRIP Index. Their stated annual operating expenses are 0.09% and 0.19%, respectively.

ETF commentator Nate Geraci praised the concept as smart product design, describing it as an accessible way for everyday investors to gain exposure to Bitcoin through familiar stock portfolios.

His comparison with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 captures the broad appeal, although the funds track their own VettaFi benchmarks.

DRIP stands for dividend reinvestment plan. Franklin's approach redirects dividends generated by stocks toward Bitcoin exposure rather than reinvesting them in those equities.

The underlying indexes began with 95% allocated to stocks and 5% to Bitcoin . Regular and special dividends are systematically reinvested into Bitcoin at the market open following the relevant ex-dividend date.

This creates a recurring source of crypto investment, although market movements mean Bitcoin's portfolio weight will not necessarily rise continuously.

The strategy also includes rules to prevent cryptocurrency from dominating the portfolio.

At quarterly rebalances, a Bitcoin weighting above 5% is reduced to 4.5%. Allocations at or below 5% remain unchanged. If Bitcoin exceeds 20% at a close between quarterly reviews , the index resets its weighting to 4.5% at the close of the second following business day.

These rules combine ongoing accumulation with periodic selling. Investors, therefore, should not expect the strategy to behave like an unrestricted, buy-and-hold Bitcoin investment.

The potential breakthrough is convenience. A single purchase could provide stock exposure and an automatically managed cryptocurrency allocation , removing the need to select a separate Bitcoin investment.

That structure could appeal to advisers building diversified portfolios and investors who want limited crypto exposure alongside equities. Whether it ultimately reaches millions of shareholders will depend on adoption; the filings provide no guarantee of that scale.

The funds can obtain Bitcoin exposure through exchange-traded products and derivatives , including futures and options. Consequently, investors gain exposure through a managed investment structure.

Dividends also remain part of shareholders' economic returns. Redirecting them into Bitcoin does not make the cryptocurrency allocation free or protect it against losses.

A smaller allocation can still affect performance materially during sharp price swings, while falling equities could compound losses.

Franklin's proposal could make Bitcoin a more routine portfolio ingredient. Its success will depend on whether investors want the combination and understand what their dividends are buying.

content:
Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, publicly filed for its IPO with the SEC on Monday, October 26, applying to list Class A shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker "ANT". It could be the largest stock market debut on record, yet the filing leaves the price range blank. The numbers inside it are anything but.

The Anthropic IPO prospectus shows revenue of $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.2 billion a year earlier. And prediction markets now price a 74.5% chance that Anthropic will be worth more than Bitcoin by the end of the year. So what did the S-1 reveal, and what could a listing this size mean for crypto?

DISCOVER: Best Meme Coins to Buy in 2026

A company growing faster than its losses. The S-1 shows revenue rising from $4.6 billion in all of 2025 to $16.3 billion in the first six months of 2026, a fourteen-fold jump on the same half a year earlier.

The headline loss looks alarming: $80.7 billion for the half. But $72.4 billion of it is a non-cash charge, the rising fair value of convertible notes and SAFEs issued to early backers as the company's valuation climbed. The operating loss, what the business itself lost, narrowed to $693 million from $2.1 billion a year earlier.

Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and J.P. Morgan top a list of 22 underwriters. The price range, share count and the size of the raise will come in a later amendment.

DISCOVER: Andreessen Horowitz Renames a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier: Where Will the Money Go Now?

Not the buyers of the shares. Public investors get Class A stock with one vote per share, but a single Class F share, held by a company owned by the seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei, carries 50.1% of the votes.

A separate body, the Long-Term Benefit Trust, will elect a majority of the board through its own Class T share. Anthropic will also be a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules. As a public benefit corporation, it must weigh its mission of developing AI safely alongside shareholder returns, and it has already placed 5% of its shares in a new Public Benefit Fund.

The IPO date will be most likely in November. On Polymarket, traders give an 83.5% chance that the shares start trading by November 30, and about 50% by November 20.

The valuation is the bigger question. Anthropic was last valued at $965 billion in its $65 billion Series H round in May. Polymarket's most likely IPO valuation range is now $1.5 trillion to $1.75 trillion, at 58%, close to double that private price only five months later.

The market thinks so. Bitcoin's market capitalisation stands at about $1.61 trillion at $80,100, and Polymarket gives 74.5% that Anthropic's value passes it by December 31. Traders put the most weight on a first-day closing value of $1.75 trillion to $2 trillion.

For crypto, the filing was a non-event on the screen. Bitcoin slipped 0.3% on the day and AI tokens barely moved: Bittensor's TAO was up 1.2% and Render 2.2%. The risk comes later. A raise of this size will need buyers, and the same growth investors who hold Bitcoin and AI tokens may sell some to make room for ANT.

Bitcoin is trading just below its 50-day EMA at $80,801. Resistance sits at $82,850, where every bounce stalled last week, and support at $79,221, Saturday's low. A close below that floor would put the 200-day EMA at $76,347 in play.

The Anthropic IPO will be the first time public investors can buy a stake in a frontier AI lab directly. If it prices near the top of Polymarket's range, the company behind Claude will open its first day of trading worth more than the world's largest cryptocurrency.

The stark warning came alongside a government push for households to prepare for disruptions to essential services.

Advice included keeping enough food and water for three days, cash, first-aid supplies, and a battery-powered torch available.

Asked whether blockchain offered an alternative, Netanyahu replied:

"One of them, certainly. I have already asked for a plan to be prepared for that."

The proposal comes as Israel faces growing international pressure over its treatment of Palestinians, including escalating settler violence and settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank.

Britain, France, and Canada announced restrictions on imports from Israeli settlements in September.

The devastation in Gaza has intensified scrutiny, as Gaza's Health Ministry reported 74,250 Palestinians killed since October 2023 in figures published on Oct. 7, 2026.

Amnesty International has also concluded that Israel's actions in Gaza constitute genocide, highlighting mass killings and the deliberate imposition of conditions calculated to destroy Palestinian life.

Israeli operations in southern Lebanon have also drawn allegations of war crimes, while deadly strikes have continued despite ceasefire arrangements.

Against that backdrop, Netanyahu's blockchain preparations take on a different character from Britain's warnings.

While the UK is urging readiness for potential security threats, Israel is exploring financial alternatives as its treatment of Palestinians pushes it closer to possible financial isolation.

VanEck's January 8 research sets out three hypothetical Bitcoin valuations for 2050:

$130,000 in its bear scenario

$2.9 million in its base case

$53.4 million in its bull case.

The most optimistic outcome assumes Bitcoin captures 20% of international trade and 10% of domestic GDP.

It also envisages the asset representing nearly 30% of the world's financial assets.

VanEck says this would require Bitcoin to:

"achieve parity with or surpass gold as a primary global reserve asset"

Geopolitical instability could strengthen parts of that investment case.

However, analysts are divided over whether mega demand for Bitcoin will occur as an immediate reaction to war.

BlackRock researchers have argued that Bitcoin's independence from individual governments could become more attractive when confidence in established financial systems weakens.

Their research describes Bitcoin as a "scarce, non-sovereign, decentralized global asset."

Applied to wartime environments, they argue that these characteristics make it attractive, as it's not controlled by a government facing rising military costs or financial pressure.

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes has also argued a similar thesis surrounding Bitcoin.

Speaking on the Coin Stories podcast in March 2026, Hayes argued that a prolonged war in the Middle East could increase pressure on the Federal Reserve to loosen monetary policy.

He has long argued that "money printing is good for Bitcoin."

Neither argument proves whether Bitcoin will rise if fighting escalates.

In an August 2026 update, BlackRock's Robbie Mitchnick described Bitcoin as having a "dual personality".

He explained that it can move in tandem with risk assets when investors reduce exposure, while potentially serving as a hedge during other periods of geopolitical disruption.

BlackRock's portfolio research also warns that Bitcoin's unstable correlations mean investors cannot rely on it to cushion losses in other assets.

The bullish wartime case will depend on what follows the initial shock. Whether confidence in sovereign currencies deteriorates and whether investors respond by buying Bitcoin.

Even if those conditions emerge, a rally towards a $53.4 million valuation would remain hard to justify.

Using today's price of $80,301 as a starting point, Bitcoin would need to rise 66,400% to reach $53.4 million, making each coin worth roughly 665 times its current value.

At that price, Bitcoin's maximum supply of 21 million coins would imply a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.12 quadrillion.

Putting that into perspective, the world's stock markets were collectively worth $157.8 trillion in 2025, while outstanding global fixed-income securities totaled $160.7 trillion, according to SIFMA.

Bitcoin's implied valuation would be roughly seven times either market.

That means Bitcoin alone would have a valuation several times that of the combined value of the world's listed companies and outstanding bonds.

This shows how ambitious the forecast truly is.

Reaching $53.4 million would require Bitcoin to become the world's dominant monetary asset, supported by global adoption that goes far beyond a temporary wartime surge.

However, despite this weekly gain, ENA's overall performance is concerning. The token is still down 9.6% over the last 14 days and 26.1% over the past month, trading 86.5% below its all-time high. Thus, while this past week was positive, it only slightly mitigated the sharp drop earlier in October.

Interestingly, ENA rose even as Arthur Hayes, a prominent crypto trader and co-founder of BitMEX, sold the token. According to data from on-chain tracker Lookonchain, Hayes sold 14 million ENA, valued at $2.7 million, while offloading $28.8 million worth of various tokens, primarily ETH and ENA, and securing a profit of $6.7 million.

The surge in ENA's price from October 19 to today may reflect a shift in market dynamics after a wave of selling earlier in the month. On October 5, the Ethena Foundation released all remaining locked tokens for early investors, flooding the market with new supply.

This led to a significant drop in ENA's price through October 19, exacerbated by forced liquidations—when exchanges close borrowed positions due to losses—and selling pressure from large holders.

Hayes' recent sales reflect his decision to close all trading positions for his fund, Maelstrom, as he locked in profits on ETH, ENA, and other altcoins, citing economic and geopolitical uncertainties as reasons for his cautious stance. He predicted the market might need to decline further before it can rebound, and he plans to stay out until conditions improve.

However, Hayes directed 14 million ENA to Cumberland, a large over-the-counter trading desk that conducts trades privately. Because those trades happen away from the public order book, that could help explain why ENA absorbed $2.7 million in sales without a significant price drop.

It's also uncertain how much of ENA's recent price increase came from short sellers being forced to buy back into the market. Short sellers profit when prices fall, so a rising price can compel them to cover their positions, driving the price up further without genuine new demand. This buying typically stops once short positions are cleared, which may lead to a decline after an initial spike.

While Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) and Solana (CRYPTO:SOL) were also slipping this week, ENA climbed from around $0.19 on October 19 during its recent upswing. In contrast, ETH traded near $2,301, just below its recent lows of about $2,308 on October 25 and $2,313 on October 15. After peaking around $2,524 on October 21, ETH was notably active on October 22, opening at roughly $2,472 and closing at $2,386.

Additionally, Bitcoin dropped from approximately $81,838 on October 19 to around $79,560. Solana also fell from $105 to $101 during the same period.

Tokens that have been beaten down often show stronger rebounds. ENA's 30-day drop of 26.1% exceeds ETH's 13.6% decline, suggesting ENA had more recovery potential once major selling pressure eased.

What sets ENA apart is its connection to Ethena's business performance. Ethena issues USDe (CRYPTO:USDE), a synthetic dollar designed to maintain a stable $1 value through crypto collateral and risk-management strategies. The platform holds various cryptocurrencies like ETH and pairs them with short futures positions that gain value when prices decline, effectively balancing each other out.

These short positions are perpetual futures, meaning they don't expire and use a funding rate to stay aligned with market prices. When many traders favor long positions, they pay this funding rate to short holders, allowing Ethena to collect income. Therefore, high funding rates boost Ethena's earnings, benefiting USDe holders and attracting more deposits.

As a result, ENA's value largely depends on USDe growth and funding rates. When ETH declines, funding rates often drop too, reducing Ethena's income. Thus, ENA's rise during ETH's 4.3% dip suggests easing selling pressure rather than improved business conditions.

It's unlikely that ENA will maintain this momentum for long. While it gained in one week, it is still down 26.1% over 30 days, and ETH continues to struggle. Moreover, the buyback initiatives that could support ENA have not yet begun. Ethena passed a governance vote to enable a fee switch that allocates up to 95% of net revenue to ENA buybacks.

However, these buybacks will only start once the USDe supply exceeds $7.5 billion. USDe's supply ended the third quarter below this threshold, and its market value currently stands at about $4.6 billion.

If ENA falls back below $0.19, its recent rally could be viewed as a short-term bounce in an ongoing decline. However, if ENA holds above $0.19 while ETH rises above $2,524, this outperformance may signal stronger buying interest.

content:
Small Bitcoin holders are moving coins onto Binance at the fastest pace in six months, while whale deposits have fallen by a third since late August, CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost wrote on Monday, October 26. The split comes as BTC fights to hold $80,000 ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision. It is the most telling Bitcoin news on-chain this week: the two groups are reading the same dip in opposite ways.

The Bitcoin price trades near $80,450, flat on the day and down 3% in a week. So what are retail and whales doing, and which levels decide the next move?

Because they reacted differently to the slide from $87,000. CryptoQuant's chart tracks how much Bitcoin each group sends to Binance over 30 days. Retail inflows have climbed steadily since April and now sit near $11 billion, their highest in six months. Whale inflows went the other way. They peaked near $6 billion in late August and have dropped to about $4 billion.

Why does that matter? Coins usually go to an exchange for one of two reasons: to be sold, or to be traded. Rising retail deposits suggest smaller holders are nervous, or trying to trade the swings. Falling whale deposits mean the biggest holders aren't rushing to sell into this dip.

It fits last week's picture. Retail traders had largely left Bitcoin futures , CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju's data showed. Now they're showing up in spot instead. Small investors seem to have swapped leverage for coins on exchanges, and some of them look ready to sell.

Yes, even after Saturday's flush. About $820 million in crypto positions, mostly longs, were liquidated when BTC hit $79,221, but funding rates stayed positive. On OKX, longs paid shorts roughly 0.01% every eight hours on Monday morning. On Hyperliquid, funding is lower but still positive.

So the market hasn't turned bearish. Leverage is still leaning long, which can fuel a quick bounce, or another flush if $79,000 gives way.

Not every large short is a bet against Bitcoin, either. Lookonchain flagged $1.29 billion in shorts held by Abraxas Capital on Hyperliquid. Those accounts are hedges against the fund's spot holdings, not a directional call.

Where is the on-chain support? Lower than the current price, but rising. CryptoQuant analyst TraderGemini noted that the trader realized price, the average cost of coins held by active traders, has turned up again. "Historically, during bullish phases, this realized price has often acted as support when BTC corrected toward it," the analyst wrote.

That matters. A rising cost basis for active traders means the floor under the market keeps moving up, even while the price drifts lower, and dips toward it have tended to find buyers who don't want to sell below what they paid.

BTC closed Sunday below its 50-day EMA at $80,812 for the first time since mid-August. Getting back above it is the first step for buyers.

Overhead, $81,430 to $81,850 is the next barrier, where the 4-hour 50 and 200 EMAs meet, and $82,850 has capped every bounce since Thursday. Below, $79,221 to $79,369 is the floor: the lows of Saturday and Monday.

title: 1 Popular Cryptocurrency to Buy Before It Soars by 873%, According to Cathie Wood's Ark Invest
summary: Bitcoin recently lost more than half of its peak value, but it's slowly recovering.
content:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) fell to a 52-week low of $58,566 in July, which represented a 53% decline from last year's all-time high of $124,773. It has since rallied back to $81,800 (as of this writing on Oct. 23), giving investors hope that a new bull cycle may be underway.

Ark Investment Management, founded by technology investor Cathie Wood, is very bullish about Bitcoin's potential. It believes the cryptocurrency could amass a market capitalization of $16 trillion by 2030, which would translate to a price of $796,000 per coin.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

That implies a whopping 873% upside from the current level, so should investors buy Bitcoin today?

Ark Invest publishes a new edition of its "Big Ideas" report each year, highlighting different areas of the technology industry where its analysts see value. The 2026 report outlined six catalysts underpinning the 2030 forecast for Bitcoin, but two of them are expected to account for most of the potential upside.

Institutional investment : Ark predicts that investment funds will eventually allocate around 2.5% of their $200 trillion in managed assets to Bitcoin, adding $5 trillion to the cryptocurrency's market cap. Bitcoin is different from most of the other assets in traditional portfolios, so it can add a level of diversification, and the widely available exchange-traded funds (ETFs) make it possible for many regulated funds to own the cryptocurrency.

Digital gold : Ark thinks Bitcoin can capture between 20% and 60% of gold's $28 trillion market cap as investors look for a modern digital alternative to the shiny yellow metal. This could add between $5.6 trillion and $16.8 trillion to the cryptocurrency's market cap.

The other four catalysts will only add a trivial amount to Bitcoin's value compared to the first two, according to Ark.

Emerging market safe-haven : Economic and political instability is prevalent in developing countries, so citizens can protect their wealth by parking it in a decentralized asset like Bitcoin, which the government can't control.

Nation-state treasury : Ark believes the treasury departments in a growing number of countries will hold Bitcoin the same way they hold gold and other assets. The U.S. is leading the way, having established a strategic Bitcoin reserve last year.

Corporate treasury : Companies like Elon Musk's Space Exploration Technologies and Tesla hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets as a hedge against economic uncertainty. Ark thinks this will become a trend.

Bitcoin on-chain financial services : Ark predicts more consumers and businesses will use the Bitcoin network to process transactions over time, because it allows them to bypass traditional payment rails which tend to be expensive and burdened by red tape.

Ark reduced the forecast size of the emerging-market safe-haven opportunity by around 80% between its 2025 and 2026 Big Ideas reports as U.S.-dollar-denominated stablecoins and other alternatives are growing in popularity in developing economies, which could hurt Bitcoin adoption.

At the same time, Ark increased the size of the digital gold opportunity -- not because it believes Bitcoin will capture a larger share of gold's market cap, but because the yellow metal is gradually becoming more valuable.

Therefore, it's important to remember that Ark's forecast is dynamic and could change significantly between now and 2030.

Before investors pile into Bitcoin based on Ark's 873% upside projection, they might want to pump the brakes and consider the tricky math required to get there.

For example, a $16 trillion market cap would make Bitcoin more valuable than Nvidia , Apple , and Alphabet combined, which are currently the world's three largest companies. Moreover, $16 trillion is more than half of the annual output of the entire U.S. economy, which was $30.8 trillion last year.

There is also a major problem with Ark's digital gold catalyst, which is supposed to contribute the most value to Bitcoin between now and 2030. Since the beginning of 2025, investors have contended with elevated inflation, global trade disruptions, geopolitical conflicts, and surging U.S. government debt. If Bitcoin were a true alternative to gold, investors would be buying it hand over fist to hedge against those headwinds.

However, the cryptocurrency has declined by 13% since Jan. 1, 2025, while actual gold has rocketed higher by 57%. In other words, in the face of real trouble, investors are making a clear choice to protect their money -- and it isn't Bitcoin.

Gold Price in US Dollars data by YCharts

If the digital gold catalyst doesn't work out, Bitcoin will have to unlock trillions of dollars in value from other sources to meet Ark's 2030 forecast, and I don't think any of the other five catalysts will be able to bridge the gap.

Therefore, while Bitcoin's latest recovery might continue, I don't think it's realistic to expect a rally to $796,000 per coin.

title: Strategy Pauses Bitcoin Buying, Spends $205M Buying Back STRC
summary: The Bitcoin treasury firm's USD Cash balance fell to $242.4 million after its biggest weekly STRC buyback in more than a month.
content:
Strategy did not buy any Bitcoin last week, breaking a run of weekly purchases that began in mid-September, as it spent $204.9 million buying back its STRC preferred stock instead, the company said on Monday.

The Bitcoin treasury firm also sold no shares through its at-the-market offering program between October 19 and 25, according to an SEC filing. It holds 848,517 BTC, acquired for a total of $64.02 billion at an average of $75,446 per coin.

The pause follows a string of smaller Bitcoin purchases. Strategy bought 267 BTC for $22.1 million the previous week, after spending $21.5 million on 250 BTC the week before that and $29 million in the week it posted a $21 billion third-quarter gain.

The STRC buyback, covering 2,068,459 shares, was the largest of those weeks, up from $193.1 million the week before and $192.4 million the week prior. Strategy paid for it entirely from USD Cash, the pool of money it keeps for general purposes including buying Bitcoin, which fell to $242.4 million from $447.3 million a week earlier.

Its separate USD Reserve, which is meant to cover preferred dividends and interest on its debt, held steady at $4.83 billion. After the latest buyback, $956.8 million remains available under the company's $3 billion program for repurchasing its preferred stock, which it raised from $2 billion a week ago. A separate program to buy back MSTR common stock has $1 billion left.

The pause comes as Strategy faces possible removal from MSCI's widely tracked equity indexes. MSCI finalized a rule on October 15 that treats "non-operating companies," those whose balance sheets are dominated by a single asset, as ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30. The index provider will publish the list of affected companies on November 11.

Bitcoin Treasury Giant Strategy Faces Index Removal Under Finalized MSCI Rules

Removal would force funds that track the indexes to sell the affected shares. Strategy chairman Michael Saylor had urged MSCI to drop what he called a "discriminatory" rule.

title: An Indian Exchange Lost $16 Million From Wallets It Said It Had Retired. Is It Safe to Leave Crypto on an Exchange?
summary: India's biggest crypto exchange just lost millions from wallets it claimed were retired, and the CEO had called earlier breach reports a false alarm. What really happens to your funds when an exchange's systems quietly fail behind the scenes?
content:
CoinDCX lost $16 million in USDT from old wallets after a July 2025 hack, but covered the loss and said customer funds were unaffected.

Crypto on exchanges carries no FDIC or SIPC protection, a fact illustrated by Mt. Gox creditors who have waited nearly 13 years and still aren't fully repaid.

Splitting holdings by keeping a small trading balance on an exchange while storing the rest in a self-custody wallet limits your exposure if an exchange fails.

CoinDCX, India's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said it lost about 15.99 million Tether (CRYPTO: USDT), worth around $16 million, from old wallets that it said were no longer in use after a July 2025 hack. This revelation came just days after CEO Sumit Gupta dismissed earlier breach reports as "a false alarm." It raises an important question for anyone who wants to keep crypto on an exchange.

According to CoinDCX, customer funds were not affected, and the company has promised to cover the loss. However, this incident reminds us that while your balance may look secure in an app, the systems behind it can fail unexpectedly. So, how vulnerable are those who keep Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) or other cryptocurrencies on an exchange?

Exchanges manage customer funds using two types of wallets. Hot wallets connect to the internet to enable quick transactions, while cold wallets are offline, making them more secure against theft. CoinDCX's troubles began with deposit addresses it set up in January 2025, which were compromised in a July 2025 hack.

Although CoinDCX said it had stopped using those old addresses, customers kept sending funds to them. Unfortunately, the internal service responsible for transferring those deposits into safer wallets failed. On-chain investigator ZachXBT noted that one of the compromised addresses still directed deposits to CoinDCX's current hot wallet as recently as April and May.

CoinDCX's customers are covered only because the exchange chose to absorb the loss and had the funds to do so. The company acknowledged it could have communicated the incident sooner.

When you keep your cryptocurrencies on an exchange, you don't truly "own" those coins; the exchange does. Instead, you hold a claim to them. In the U.S., crypto on exchanges lacks FDIC insurance, and the Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC) does not extend protections to cryptocurrencies not classified as securities.

In contrast, traditional bank customers enjoy strengthened protections. FDIC insurance covers up to $250,000 per depositor, and when a bank fails, another institution often assumes its accounts. For instance, when regulators shut down Nano Banc in Irvine, California, on September 25, Sunwest Bank took over its account holders' deposits.

Conversely, crypto customers may face a lengthy court process. After the Mt. Gox exchange collapsed in 2014, its trustee pushed the creditor repayment deadline to October 31, 2027, stretching the wait to about 13 years. FTX customers received compensation based on their account values as of November 2022 but missed out on Bitcoin's subsequent price rise.

While market fluctuations may seem daunting, the bigger risk lies in how you manage custody. For example, Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) has plunged around 44% over the past year, but holders still possess their coins.

If an exchange holding a customer's entire $20,000 balance fails, that amount becomes part of a bankruptcy claim. In contrast, a holder who keeps $2,000 on the exchange and stores $18,000 in a personal wallet risks only $2,000.

Keeping all your crypto on an exchange is the easiest option, with quick trades and easy password resets, but it's not ideal for long-term investors. Regular proof-of-reserves reports—showing that an exchange holds enough coins to cover customer balances—can help, but they reflect only one moment in time and may not account for the exchange's other liabilities. Additionally, insurance may cover only specific types of hacks, not a complete failure.

A more balanced approach is to split holdings. This means keeping a small trading balance on the exchange while storing most of your coins in a wallet where you control the private keys—the secret codes that secure your assets. This way, an exchange only retains what you might need for a short-term trade.

Full self-custody removes exchange-related risks but introduces others. If you lose your recovery phrase—the backup words used to restore access to your wallet—you could permanently lose your coins. This method suits experienced users who rarely sell and manage their backups carefully. Meanwhile, spot Bitcoin ETFs secure assets with a regulated custodian.

In short, it's generally safe to keep cryptocurrencies on an exchange for regular trading, but long-term holdings are at risk. Consider your balance size; if losing access for years would be damaging, it's too large to keep on an exchange. Regular proof-of-reserves reports, transparent communication, and a history of covering losses can enhance a platform's reliability. CoinDCX's handling of this incident highlights the importance of prompt, clear disclosure to maintain customer trust.

Consider the costs and responsibilities of moving coins off an exchange to help protect your investments.

title: Michael Saylor Reveals Strategy's $3B Bitcoin Credit Bet: Is MSTR Just a Byproduct?
summary: Michael Saylor says Strategy's central business is turning Bitcoin-backed capital into income-producing digital credit products. Strategy is repurchasing preferred shares to support their market prices…
content:
Key Takeaways

Michael Saylor says Strategy's central business is turning Bitcoin-backed capital into income-producing digital credit products.

Strategy is repurchasing preferred shares to support their market prices and reduce future dividend obligations.

The company's digital credit repurchase authorization has reached $3 billion, signaling a shift toward active balance sheet management.

Strategy executive chairman Michael Saylor is challenging the perception that his company's primary business is simply to accumulate Bitcoin and issue MSTR shares.

In an Oct. 20 discussion circulated from his Schwab Network interview, Saylor explained that Strategy's larger ambition is to transform Bitcoin-backed capital into digital credit products designed for investors seeking income rather than direct cryptocurrency exposure.

This marks an important evolution for the world's best-known corporate Bitcoin treasury strategy .

While MSTR shareholders remain exposed to Bitcoin's price movements, Strategy is developing preferred securities that offer dollar-denominated dividends, supported by its broader capital structure.

The approach also explains a decision that might otherwise seem counterintuitive: using available capital to repurchase preferred stock instead of acquiring additional Bitcoin.

Saylor's model separates Bitcoin capital, common equity, and digital credit into different investment propositions.

Bitcoin provides the underlying reserve asset. MSTR offers shareholders leveraged exposure to the company's Bitcoin holdings and its financial business. Preferred securities such as STRC are designed to provide income with lower price volatility than Bitcoin itself.

In a September explanation of Strategy's model, Saylor described the objective as reducing volatility, shortening cash-flow duration, and extracting yield from Bitcoin-backed capital.

However, Strategy is not directly generating Bitcoin yield in the conventional sense. Its preferred dividends are corporate payment obligations supported by liquidity reserves, financing activity, and the company's assets.

That difference is essential because the income products remain exposed to Strategy's creditworthiness and ability to fund distributions.

Strategy's capital allocation strategy has increasingly focused on keeping its preferred securities trading close to their stated value.

STRC , for example, has a stated amount of $100 per share. When its market price falls below that level, Strategy can repurchase shares at a discount, reducing outstanding preferred claims and future dividend requirements.

The company believes supporting prices near par can improve investor confidence and eventually allow it to issue additional securities on more favorable terms.

On Oct. 19, Strategy increased its digital credit repurchase authorization from $2 billion to $3 billion.

Its SEC filing showed that the company repurchased approximately 1.94 million STRC shares for $193.1 million during the preceding week, leaving $1.16 billion available under the expanded authorization.

The objective is not merely to stabilize preferred securities. A successful credit business could also support a premium valuation for MSTR relative to Strategy's underlying Bitcoin assets.

The strategy introduces a different set of risks from simply holding Bitcoin.

Preferred dividends require dollar liquidity, while Bitcoin's market value can fluctuate sharply. Strategy must therefore balance its cryptocurrency reserves against payment commitments and financing costs.

Its capital framework includes dollar reserves, preferred-share repurchases, and authorization to sell Bitcoin under specified circumstances.

However, dividends are not guaranteed, and preferred shareholders remain exposed to market-price declines and corporate credit risk .

The risks become more pronounced during periods of sustained Bitcoin weakness. On Oct. 24, longtime Bitcoin critic Peter Schiff warned that the cryptocurrency's decline below $80,000 could accelerate, identifying $75,000 as the next potential downside target.

Schiff also cautioned that a further decline over the weekend could leave spot Bitcoin ETF investors particularly exposed, as they cannot trade ETF shares until traditional markets reopen on Monday.

While Schiff's forecast remains speculative, a prolonged Bitcoin downturn could weaken Strategy's balance sheet, complicate capital raising, and make its preferred securities less attractive to income-focused investors.

If demand for digital credit weakens, Strategy could struggle to issue new securities at attractive prices, limiting its ability to expand the business.

In that scenario, its investment proposition would depend more heavily on its existing Bitcoin holdings .

For MSTR investors , the key question is whether Strategy can build a sustainable credit business around Bitcoin without allowing financing costs, dilution, and dividend commitments to outweigh the benefits of accumulating more BTC.

title: Prediction: Can XRP Reach $100 by 2030?
summary: XRP bulls have mapped out a path to $100 by 2030, but the math behind that target reveals obstacles that go far beyond typical crypto volatility. Here is what would actually have to happen across global finance for that price to become real.

XRP is trading at $1.29 following a 12.9% drop in October. It has fluctuated between a high of $1.56 on September 29 and a low of $1.25 on October 24, and it has declined 51% from $2.65 over the past year.

For XRP to hit $100, it would need to reach a market value not seen in the crypto space so far. Only a few key factors could drive it to this level.

Market capitalization is calculated by multiplying a token's price by the total number of tokens in circulation. About 63.4 billion XRP are in circulation out of a maximum supply of 100 billion. To reach $100, XRP would need to multiply its price by 77.5 times, resulting in a market value of around $6.34 trillion.

This figure is about 3.9 times larger than Bitcoin's market cap (CRYPTO:BTC), with Bitcoin trading at $79,401. It's also about 2.3 times the entire cryptocurrency market, which is valued at $2.7 trillion. In other words, XRP alone would need to be worth more than all other cryptocurrencies combined. This is significant, especially since XRP's all-time high is only $3.65, achieved in July 2025, and it trades 64.6% below that peak.

As supply increases, this target becomes more challenging each year. Ripple, the company behind XRP, holds some of these tokens in escrow — a locked account that releases them gradually. If all 100 billion XRP tokens are circulating by 2030, hitting $100 would push the market value to about $10 trillion, meaning every released token raises the target even higher.

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) allow investors to gain exposure to XRP through traditional brokerage accounts. As of October 23, U.S. XRP ETFs held net assets of $1.48 billion, with total new money added since their launch reaching $1.80 billion.

However, inflows have been minimal, with the largest single-day inflow over the past month only reaching $8.2 million on October 8. In the week starting October 19, three out of five trading sessions saw no new money entering these funds, with only $709,000 on October 21 and $3.55 million on October 22. On October 16, the funds even saw a $2.5 million outflow.

To reach a $6.34 trillion valuation, XRP ETF assets would need to grow from billions to trillions, a far cry from the $1.48 billion the funds hold.

The strongest evidence of what positive market sentiment can do for XRP comes from late 2024. The price jumped from $0.51 at the end of October to $1.94 by the end of November — a staggering 280% increase, driven by expectations of a more favorable regulatory environment after the presidential election. XRP reached $3.40 in January 2025 and hit a record high of $3.65 in July 2025.

Despite this significant rally, the price never reached $4. Since then, XRP has decreased by 29.5% in 2026 alone. While another similar surge could propel XRP back toward $3.65, it would still be around 96% below the $100 target.

For XRP to realistically hit $100, several conditions must align. Financial institutions and payment companies would need to process a substantial portion of global payments and settlements using XRP. Additionally, demand for ETFs would have to rise dramatically, from billions to trillions. Furthermore, tokenization—converting assets like bonds or real estate into tradable tokens—would have to occur at scale on the XRP Ledger.

XRP would also need to play a role alongside RLUSD, Ripple's stablecoin. As a U.S. dollar-pegged stablecoin, RLUSD would let banks settle payments without worrying about XRP's price volatility.

The short answer is no; XRP has a very slim chance of reaching $100 by 2030. This target implies a market value of $6.34 trillion at the circulating supply and around $10 trillion at full supply—figures that far exceed the overall $2.7 trillion crypto market and go well beyond mainstream expectations.

Before dreaming of hitting $100, XRP first needs to recapture its $1.56 high from September 29, 20.9% above its October 26 price. Then it must pass $2.65 and its record high of $3.65. A sustained move above $3.65, along with a notable rise in ETF assets, would signal progress. However, if ETF inflows remain low and XRP falls below $1.25, it may drop back towards $1.07, a level it traded at in late July.

title: Bettors Expect a Democratic Midterm Win. How Gold, Bitcoin, and Stocks Could Feel It
summary: A Democratic Congress could reshape spending, war funding, AI rules, and executive power, with knock-on effects for markets.
content:
Voters on each side fear what the other party would do with Congress, a CNBC survey shows. For investors, the question is how a Democratic majority could reshape oil, AI, and policy risk.

Polymarket gives Democrats a 93% chance of winning the House and 65% for the Senate. A recent World Gold Council note maps four policy areas a Democratic Congress could influence, each with implications for gold, Bitcoin, and stocks.

Spending is the first area. According to the WGC, a Democratic Congress could limit the White House's ability to pass deficit-expanding bills. Edward Jones similarly expects gridlock to make large new fiscal initiatives less likely.

Gold could feel mixed effects. Smaller deficits could ease fiscal concerns and revive demand for Treasuries and the dollar, weighing on gold. However, pressure to reduce tariffs could cut government revenue and widen the deficit, potentially supporting the metal.

Stocks: Lower Treasury yields could support equities by reducing borrowing costs and increasing the present value of future earnings. Edward Jones data also shows the S&P 500 has generally risen after midterm elections since 1970, regardless of which party won.

Bitcoin (BTC) tends to move opposite the dollar, and Glassnode data shows that inverse correlation at its most negative it has recorded. A firmer dollar from smaller deficits would therefore weigh on BTC. However, that link has weakened at times.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

The second area, war funding, ties the vote directly to oil. In the CNBC survey, 21% of Democrats worry a Republican Congress would continue military efforts in Iran. By contrast, 11% of Republicans worry Democrats would end them.

Trump recently ruled out imminent military action against Iran. The council argues a Democratic Congress could restrict war funding and push toward de-escalation.

For now, oil points the other way. Brent crude trades near $114, and higher energy costs have lifted inflation worries. Traders see about an 80% chance of a December Fed hike.

Gold would benefit from de-escalation, the council says, as cheaper oil eases inflation expectations, yields, and the dollar. The metal fell below $4,000 on Friday, its lowest since mid-July, and traded at $4,010.48 on Monday.

Stocks would gain if cheaper oil softens yields and inflation fears.

Bitcoin has swung on Iran headlines this month, with escalation news cutting it 2% to 5% intraday. A deal that weakens the dollar could help. BTC now trades at $79,894, down 1.2% in 24 hours.

AI policy is the third area. According to the council, a Democratic Congress could scale back federal support for AI or tighten its regulation.

In the CNBC survey, 19% of Democrats fear a Republican Congress would fail to regulate AI and data centers. Among Republicans, 6% fear Democrats would overregulate them.

Gold could gain from that slowdown as softer growth, lower yields, and a weaker dollar support it.

Stocks , especially tech, would take the most direct hit, the council suggests. Investors already doubt whether hyperscaler spending will pay off. Weaker tech shares could then dent household wealth and consumer spending.

Bitcoin faces a split effect. A weaker dollar would help, but a tech sell-off could drag BTC lower alongside equities.

The final area is executive power, which voters already worry about. In the CNBC survey, 44% of all voters fear Trump operating beyond his constitutional power, including 74% of Democrats. Among Republicans, 16% fear a Democratic Congress would impeach him.

The council expects blocked legislation to push the administration toward more executive orders and emergency powers. The court fights, and policy swings that follow could raise political risk premiums.

Gold usually benefits from that uncertainty, according to the council. It also expects the shift to strengthen central banks' interest in diversifying reserves into gold.

Stocks could struggle as policy becomes less predictable, which tends to weigh on valuations.

Bitcoin carries its own executive-power risk. Much of today's crypto rulebook comes from the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) rather than Congress. A future commission can withdraw those rules.

By the council's read, three of the four areas lean supportive of gold. For Bitcoin, the dollar is the common thread, while stocks hinge mostly on yields. Polymarket still gives Republicans an 8% chance of holding the House and 36% for the Senate.

ALBANY, N.Y., Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Soluna Holdings, Inc. ("Soluna" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: SLNH), a developer of green data centers for intensive computing applications, including AI and Bitcoin mining, today announced that it has repaid, in full, the $28.7 million in principal outstanding, as of June 30, 2026, under its credit facility with Generate Capital, PBC ("Generate"). The facility has been terminated, and Generate's liens on the related project assets have been released, allowing for the transition of power to the Dorothy 3 AI campus.

Soluna repaid $19.1 million of Generate debt in August 2026, as disclosed in its most recent quarterly report on Form 10-Q, and paid off the remainder in October 2026, fully retiring the Generate facility. With the facility retired, the Company's total debt principal falls from $37.9 million at June 30, 2026 to $9.2 million, which reflects its remaining debt balances as of that date.

"Repaying the Generate facility in full retires this portion of our debt and releases the liens on those project assets," said Michael Picchi, CFO of Soluna. "It simplifies our capital structure as we continue developing our AI and high-performance computing pipeline."

Soluna entered into the Generate credit facility in September 2025 to refinance Dorothy 1A and Dorothy 2, unlocking project equity capital, and to fund the completion of Dorothy 2. Generate financing also helped fund the Company's April 2026 acquisition of the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm, giving Soluna ownership of the renewable generation asset powering Project Dorothy.

"Generate's support helped us unlock equity in our Dorothy projects, complete Dorothy 2 and acquire the Briscoe Wind Farm," said John Belizaire, CEO of Soluna. "Their team understood our business and backed us at an important stage of our growth. We're grateful for that partnership as we mark the full repayment of this debt."

Highlights

title: Strategy Just Dropped 13% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
summary: Key TakeawaysStrategy stock has fallen 13% since Sept. 22 (through Friday’s close), most of it on Oct.
content:
Strategy stock has fallen 13% since Sept. 22 (through Friday's close), most of it on Oct. 16, after MSCI's new rule put Strategy's place in its global indexes at risk.

Funds tracking MSCI hold only about 13 million shares, but the rule threatens the premium Strategy needs to keep selling stock for bitcoin.

Strategy bought just over 500 bitcoin in two weeks while putting more than $190 million a week into repurchases of its STRC preferred stock.

Third-quarter results on Oct. 29 and MSCI's Nov. 11 list come next, and the list is worth waiting for before buying more.

Strategy ( MSTR:NASDAQ ) stock is down 13% since Sept. 22 (through Friday's close), more than twice the Nasdaq 100's 6% drop. Most of that came the day after MSCI ( MSCI:NYSE ) changed who qualifies for its indexes, and bitcoin's slide did the rest.

Bitcoin fell below $84,000 on Oct. 7 in a wave of leveraged selling, then slid again on Oct. 14 after a hotter-than-expected inflation report. Strategy went down with it, as did crypto stocks in general ( Coinbase ( COIN:NASDAQ ) fell 16% over the month).

The stock moves harder than the coin, both ways. When the OCC finalized its GENIUS Act stablecoin rules on Oct. 21, bitcoin rose about 3% and Strategy rose roughly three times as much .

That's leverage at work: debt and preferred stock sit ahead of common shareholders, and the premium investors pay swings on top. Strategy's total debt went from $2.25 billion in fiscal 2023 to $8.25 billion in fiscal 2025…

On the evening of Oct. 15, MSCI adopted a rule that makes non-operating companies ineligible for its global indexes. Strategy fell 10% the next day, even with bitcoin up that morning. MSCI will name the companies it hits on Nov. 11, and the rule kicks in at the Nov. 30 close.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Strategy, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Strategy's Analyst Ratings

The forced selling is small: funds tracking MSCI hold about 13 million shares, less than a day's volume. The premium takes the bigger hit. Strategy grows the bitcoin value behind each share, net of its debt and preferred stock, by selling common stock above that net value and buying more bitcoin. Its gauge for that cushion, mNAV (the share price divided by net bitcoin value per share), was only about 1.07x in August. Without index funds as reliable buyers, a premium that thin is harder to win back.

And it's the whole pitch. As Strategy founder and executive chairman Michael Saylor said on Bloomberg Talks on Oct. 13: "you should buy the digital equity of a company like MSTR or Strive and you can expect to outperform Bitcoin because we're able to amplify our Bitcoin per share with our digital credit."

Selling stock has paid for that. Diluted shares nearly tripled from fiscal 2021 to fiscal 2025, and the count has kept climbing this year…

Strategy raised just $21 million from common stock in the week to Oct. 11, enough for 250 bitcoin. Over those same seven days, it bought back $192.4 million of its STRC preferred stock.

The next week, it bought 267 bitcoin for $22.1 million and spent $193.1 million more on STRC, and on Oct. 19 its board added $1 billion to the buyback. Over those two weeks, Strategy put about nine times as much into its preferred stock as into bitcoin, all while Saylor was telling Bloomberg that bitcoin's bull market is just beginning.

Three dates come first: Oct. 28, when shareholders vote on paying preferred dividends daily; Oct. 29, when third-quarter results land after the bell (with an estimated $20.91 billion digital-asset gain already disclosed); and Nov. 11, when MSCI publishes its list.

Analysts still see plenty of upside: the consensus target was $239 on Oct. 16, 64% above Friday's close, though down from $560 a year earlier…

Cantor Fitzgerald raised its target to $208 from $186 on Oct. 16, and its target rests mostly on bitcoin reaching $112,000 within 12 months.

Personally, I wouldn't sell over one index rule and bitcoin's swings, but I wouldn't load up before Nov. 11 either. Until the list is out, Strategy is just bitcoin with leverage.

Of course, if mNAV holds above 1x even with Strategy on the list, stock sales that fund bitcoin purchases would keep adding net bitcoin value per share, and the leverage that hurt this month could start working for it.

Strategy (NasdaqGS:MSTR) unveiled a new plan to distribute its common and preferred shares through onchain tokenized markets.

The approach uses tokenized representations of Strategy equity to offer access via blockchain-based trading venues alongside traditional listings.

Management framed the move as part of a broader effort to align the company with growing institutional use of tokenization in capital markets.

The shift to onchain stock distribution should not crowd out other key factors you weigh on Strategy today. Check out 2 warning signs (1 major) that Strategy investors should know about.

Strategy operates as a bitcoin treasury business within the broader software industry, placing digital asset infrastructure at the center of its day to day activity. That focus gives the company a direct incentive to test how tokenized equity and onchain venues might reshape capital raising and secondary trading for corporate issuers.

1 thing going right for Strategy that this headline doesn't cover.

For investors in Strategy, this tokenized stock push reinforces the idea that management wants the business model tied tightly to real world use of blockchain in capital markets. It leans into the existing bitcoin treasury and digital asset infrastructure focus rather than redirecting the story. The move could widen the investor base and create new distribution channels, although it also adds execution questions around regulation, liquidity quality and how onchain and traditional listings interact in practice.

One key gap remains. The announcement does not spell out how tokenized issuance will affect future share count, especially given shareholders were heavily diluted over the past year. The practical signal to watch is the next detailed capital raising or buyback disclosure from Strategy, including any breakdown of how much issuance or repurchase volume is routed through onchain venues versus conventional markets.

It is an intentionally extreme, over-the-top scenario built around a hypothetical landmark catalyst that isn't completely impossible, but remains highly unlikely.

The concept in question centers on a major regulatory and institutional shift in which most of the world's largest asset managers, along with several major governments, would officially mandate that newly issued tokenized real-world assets.

This could include assets such as bonds, funds, and equities, with settlement and core smart-contract functions running primarily on Ethereum and its recognized Layer 2 ecosystem.

This shift would make Ethereum the default global platform for settlement and programmability in the multi-trillion-dollar tokenized asset market.

On the higher timeframes, ETH has been consolidating in the $2,300–$2,400 region after a broader pullback from higher levels earlier in the cycle. Price continues to defend key intermediate supports while facing resistance around the $2,500–$2,700 zone.

In a standard bull market, a sustained breakout above $3,000–$3,200 would confirm intermediate strength and open the path toward a retest of the prior all-time high near $4,946.

Under the extreme mandatory tokenized-asset settlement scenario outlined above, clearing that previous high would likely trigger powerful measured-move extensions and multi-cycle Fibonacci projections from the long-term base.

Momentum indicators are currently in oversold-to-neutral territory, with substantial room to reach the extreme overbought readings typical of parabolic advances.

Under this highly speculative scenario, and assuming a full-blown crypto bull market returns alongside supportive external conditions, Ethereum (ETH) could reach somewhere between $25,000 and $40,000, with a stretch target toward $60,000+ by January 1, 2027.
